instruction: What is the short title of Republic Act No. 9184?
input: SECTION 1. Short Title.  This Act shall be known as the “Government Procurement Reform Act.”
output: The "Government Procurement Reform Act."

instruction: According to RA 9184, what is the declared policy of the State?
input: It is the declared policy of the State to promote the ideals of good governance in all its branches, departments, agencies, subdivisions, and instrumentalities, including government-owned and/or -controlled corporations and local government units.
output: To promote the ideals of good governance in all branches and instrumentalities of the government.

instruction: As a procurement officer, what are the five governing principles that must be followed under RA 9184?
input: All procurement... shall, in all cases, be governed by these principles: (a) Transparency... (b) Competitiveness... (c) Streamlined procurement process... (d) System of accountability... (e) Public monitoring...
output: Transparency, competitiveness, streamlined process, a system of accountability, and public monitoring.

instruction: What is the definition of "Approved Budget for the Contract" (ABC) for National Government Agencies?
input: Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC) - refers to the budget for the contract duly approved by the Head of the Procuring Entity, as provided for in the General Appropriations Act and/or continuing appropriations, in the case of National Government Agencies...
output: The budget for the contract approved by the Head of the Procuring Entity, as provided in the General Appropriations Act and/or continuing appropriations.

instruction: Who is considered the Head of the Procuring Entity for a Local Government Unit?
input: Head of the Procuring Entity - refers to: ... (iii) the local chief executive, for local government units.
output: The local chief executive.

instruction: What is the full name of the GPPB as defined in the Act?
input: GPPB - refers to the Government Procurement Policy Board established in accordance with Article XX of this Act.
output: The Government Procurement Policy Board.

instruction: If a bidder needs to prepare a proposal for an infrastructure project, which documents should they base their bid on?
input: Bidding Documents - refer to documents issued by the Procuring Entity as the basis for Bids, furnishing all information necessary for a prospective bidder to prepare a bid for the Goods, Infrastructure Projects, and Consulting Services to be provided.
output: The Bidding Documents issued by the Procuring Entity.

instruction: Explain the concept of "Competitive Bidding" under RA 9184.
input: Competitive Bidding - refers to a method of procurement which is open to participation by any interested party and which consists of the following processes: advertisement, pre-bid conference, eligibility screening of prospective bidders, receipt and opening of bids, evaluation of bids, post-qualification, and award of contract...
output: A procurement method open to any interested party, including processes like advertisement, pre-bid conference, eligibility screening, bid receipt and opening, bid evaluation, post-qualification, and contract award.

instruction: Which government activities and projects are subject to the provisions of the Government Procurement Reform Act?
input: This Act shall apply to the Procurement of Infrastructure Projects, Goods and Consulting Services, regardless of source of funds, whether local or foreign, by all branches and instrumentalities of government, its departments, offices and agencies, including government-owned and/or -controlled corporations and local government units...
output: The procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services by all government branches and instrumentalities, regardless of funding source.

instruction: What are "Consulting Services" as defined in the Act?
input: Consulting Services - refer to services for Infrastructure Projects and other types of projects or activities of the Government requiring adequate external technical and professional expertise that are beyond the capability and/or capacity of the government to undertake such as, but not limited to: (i) advisory and review services; (ii) pre-investment or feasibility studies; (iii) design; (iv) construction supervision; (v) management and related services; and (vi) other technical services or special studies.
output: Services for government projects requiring external technical and professional expertise beyond the government's capacity, including advisory, feasibility studies, design, construction supervision, and management services.

instruction: Define "Bid" as it pertains to government procurement.
input: Bid - refers to a signed offer or proposal submitted by a supplier, manufacturer, distributor, contractor or consultant in response to the Bidding Documents.
output: A signed offer or proposal from a supplier, manufacturer, distributor, contractor, or consultant in response to Bidding Documents.

instruction: What does G-EPS stand for?
input: G-EPS - refers to the Government Electronic Procurement System as provided in Section 8 of this Act.
output: The Government Electronic Procurement System.

instruction: How does the Act ensure public monitoring of the procurement process?
input: Public monitoring of the procurement process and the implementation of awarded contracts with the end in view of guaranteeing that these contracts are awarded pursuant to the provisions of this Act and its implementing rules and regulations, and that all these contracts are performed strictly according to specifications.
output: It allows for public monitoring to ensure contracts are awarded and performed according to the Act and its implementing rules and regulations.

instruction: If a bidder needs to know what is included under "Goods," what types of items would they find in this category?
input: Goods - refer to all items, supplies, materials and general support services... whether in the nature of equipment, furniture, stationery, materials for construction, or personal property of any kind, including non-personal or contractual services such as the repair and maintenance of equipment and furniture, as well as trucking, hauling, janitorial, security, and related or analogous services...
output: All items, supplies, materials, and general support services, including equipment, furniture, stationery, construction materials, and non-personal or contractual services like repair, maintenance, trucking, hauling, janitorial, and security services.

instruction: What is the purpose of the "Streamlined procurement process" principle?
input: Streamlined procurement process that will uniformly apply to all government procurement. The procurement process shall be simple and made adaptable to advances in modern technology in order to ensure an effective and efficient method.
output: To make the procurement process simple, adaptable to technology, and uniform across all government procurement activities for effective and efficient methods.

instruction: What does the `System of accountability` principle entail for public officials and private parties?
input: System of accountability where both the public officials directly or indirectly involved in the procurement process as well as in the implementation of procurement contracts and the private parties that deal with government are, when warranted by circumstances, investigated and held liable for their actions relative thereto.
output: It ensures that both public officials and private parties involved in procurement are investigated and held liable for their actions when warranted.

instruction: What is the function of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC)?
input: BAC - refers to the Bids and Awards Committee established in accordance with Article V of this Act.
output: It is a committee established in accordance with Article V of the Act to handle bids and awards.

instruction: For a government-owned corporation, who approves the budget for the contract?
input: Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC) - refers to the budget for the contract duly approved by the Head of the Procuring Entity... the Corporate Budget for the contract approved by the governing Boards, pursuant to E.O. No. 518, series of 1979, in the case of Government-Owned and/or Controlled Corporations...
output: The governing Board, through the Corporate Budget for the contract.

instruction: If an international agreement affects government procurement, what must a procuring entity do?
input: Any treaty or international or executive agreement affecting the subject matter of this Act to which the Philippine government is a signatory shall be observed.
output: The procuring entity must observe the provisions of the treaty or international or executive agreement.

output: All branches and instrumentalities of the government, including departments, offices, agencies, government-owned corporations, and local government units.

instruction: What kind of services fall under "Consulting Services" in addition to advisory and review services?
input: Consulting Services... such as, but not limited to: (i) advisory and review services; (ii) pre-investment or feasibility studies; (iii) design; (iv) construction supervision; (v) management and related services; and (vi) other technical services or special studies.
output: Pre-investment or feasibility studies, design, construction supervision, management services, and other technical or special studies.

input: IRR - refer to the implementing rules and regulations to be promulgated in accordance with Section 75 of this Act.

instruction: What is the primary policy of the Philippine government regarding the awarding of government contracts?
input: SECTION 1. Policy Requiring Public Bidding. — It is the policy of this Administration that all Government Contracts of Government Agencies, including procurement contracts, shall be awarded through open and competitive public bidding, save in exceptional cases provided by law and applicable rules and regulations, as described in Section 3 of this Executive Order.
output: All government contracts should be awarded through open and competitive public bidding, except in exceptional cases provided by law.

instruction: Who has the final authority to approve and enter into government contracts awarded through public bidding, regardless of the amount?
input: SECTION 2. Approval of Government Contracts Awarded Through Public Bidding. — ...the Heads of the procuring entities shall have full authority to give final approval and/or enter into all Government Contracts of their respective Government Agencies, awarded through public bidding, regardless of the amount involved.
output: The heads of the procuring entities have full authority to give final approval and/or enter into these contracts.

instruction: Can the Head of a procuring entity delegate their authority to approve and sign government contracts?
input: The Heads of the procuring entities may delegate in writing this full authority to give final approval and/or enter into Government Contracts awarded through public bidding as circumstances may warrant (i.e., decentralization of procurement in a Government Agency), subject to such limitations imposed by the Head of the procuring entity concerned...
output: Yes, they can delegate this authority in writing, as long as it's subject to the limitations they impose.

instruction: What is the definition of a 'Government Agency' as mentioned in this Executive Order?
input: For this purpose, a Government Agency shall refer to the various units of the Government, including a department, bureau, office, instrumentality, government-owned and/or -controlled corporation or its subsidiary, or state college or university (Cf. Section 2(4) of Executive Order No. 292 dated July 25, 1987, otherwise known as the Administrative Code of 1987).
output: A Government Agency refers to various government units like departments, bureaus, offices, instrumentalities, government-owned and/or -controlled corporations, or state colleges or universities.

instruction: What is required before a procuring entity can use an alternative method of procurement for a contract worth at least P300 Million?
input: SECTION 4. Approval of Government Contracts Entered Into Through Alternative Methods of Procurement, Other Than Through Public Bidding. a. For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Of At Least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million). — Where the Head of the procuring entity has made a determination that a Government Contract... falls under any of the exceptions from public bidding... the Head of the procuring entity shall, before proceeding with the alternative methods of procurement... obtain the following requirements: i. An opinion from the Secretary of Justice that said Government Contract falls within the exceptions from public bidding; and ii. Approval from the Director-General of NEDA to proceed with a specific alternative method of procurement...
output: They must first obtain an opinion from the Secretary of Justice and approval from the NEDA Director-General.

instruction: Under what circumstance does the NEDA Director-General's authority to approve alternative procurement methods get transferred?
input: This authority to approve shall be lodged with the Director-General of NEDA until such time that the GPPB created under Republic Act No. 9184 informs the NEDA in writing of its decision to exercise such authority.
output: The authority is lodged with the NEDA Director-General until the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) informs NEDA in writing of its decision to exercise such authority.

instruction: Who has the authority to approve and enter into government contracts valued below P300 Million that use alternative procurement methods?
input: b. For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Below Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million). — Except for Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, the Heads of the procuring entities shall likewise have full authority to give final approval and/or enter into Government Contracts of their respective Government Agencies, entered into through alternative methods of procurement allowed by law, other than through public bidding, where the Government Contract involves an amount below Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million).
output: The heads of the procuring entities have full authority to give final approval and/or enter into these contracts, unless they require presidential action.

instruction: What makes a government contract invalid and not binding on the government?
input: All Government Contracts entered into in violation of the provisions of law, rules and regulations, and this Executive Order shall be considered contracts entered into without authority and are thus invalid and not binding on the government.
output: A contract is invalid and not binding if it's entered into in violation of the provisions of law, rules, regulations, and this Executive Order.

instruction: What is required for a government contract to be considered binding on the government?
input: All Government Contracts shall require the approval and signature of the respective Heads of the procuring entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, as required by law, applicable rules and regulations, and by this Executive Order, before said Government Contracts shall be considered approved in accordance with law and binding on the government...
output: It requires the approval and signature of the head of the procuring entity or their duly authorized official.

instruction: How quickly must a government contract requiring presidential action be submitted to NEDA after being approved by the head of the procuring entity?
input: b. All Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall be submitted with complete documentation to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the approval by the Head of the procuring entity concerned or his/its duly authorized official, as the case may be, for NEDA’s review and evaluation.
output: Within seven days from the approval by the head of the procuring entity, the contract must be submitted to NEDA with complete documentation.

instruction: What specific law governs contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services?
input: a. Contracts for the Procurement of Infrastructure Projects, Goods, and Consulting Services. Contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Cf. Section 4, Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Republic Act No. 9184, also known as the Government Procurement Reform Act, and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: What law governs contracts for the acquisition of real property for national government infrastructure projects?
input: b. Contracts for Acquisition of Right-of-Way, Site or Location for National Government Infrastructure Projects. Contracts for the acquisition of real property needed as right-of-way, site or location for national government infrastructure projects shall be governed by Republic Act No. 8974 (Cf. Section 5(n), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Republic Act No. 8974.

instruction: What law governs government contracts financed with Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds?
input: d. ODA-funded Contracts. Government Contracts financed wholly or partly with Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds shall be governed by Republic Act No. 4860, as amended, Republic Act No. 8182, as amended by Republic Act No. 8555, and Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Cf. Section 4, Republic Act No. 9184)
output: They are governed by Republic Act No. 4860, Republic Act No. 8182, and Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: What is the definition of 'Splitting of Government Contracts'?
input: SECTION 11. Splitting of Government Contracts. — Splitting of Government Contracts is not allowed. Splitting of Government Contracts means the division or breaking up of Government Contracts into smaller quantities and amounts, or dividing contract implementation into artificial phases or sub-contracts for the purpose of evading or circumventing the requirements of law and this Executive Order, especially the necessity of public bidding and the requirements for exceptions therefrom in accordance with Section 4(a) hereof.
output: It is the division of contracts into smaller quantities or artificial phases to evade or circumvent legal requirements, particularly public bidding.

instruction: Are transactions of government financial institutions (GFIs) covered by this Executive Order?
input: SECTION 9. Transactions of Government Financial Institutions. — Transactions of government financial institutions in the ordinary course of business shall not be covered by the provisions of this Executive Order. Such transactions shall instead be subject to applicable provisions of law and to guidelines, rules and regulations issued by the Department of Finance.
output: No, transactions of GFIs in the ordinary course of business are not covered by this Executive Order; they are subject to Department of Finance guidelines.

instruction: What must accompany a government contract when it is submitted to NEDA for review and evaluation?
input: Government Contracts submitted hereunder shall be accompanied by a complete execution copy of the contract, related agreements, annexes, other approvals and permits, including a detailed summary of the pertinent laws, rules and regulations governing the processing and award of the contract, and accompanied by the requirements of Section 4(a) hereof where alternative methods of procurement were resorted to.
output: It must be accompanied by a complete copy of the contract, related agreements, annexes, approvals, permits, a summary of governing laws and rules, and any Section 4(a) requirements if alternative procurement was used.

instruction: Who issues the guidelines for joint venture agreements with private entities?
input: SECTION 8. Joint Venture Agreements. — The NEDA, in consultation with the GPPB, shall issue guidelines regarding joint venture agreements with private entities with the objective of promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions...
output: The National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA), in consultation with the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB), issues the guidelines.

instruction: What is the purpose of Executive Order No. 109-A?
input: WHEREAS, it has become necessary to amend the provisions of Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 to make it conform with the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184;...
output: It amends Executive Order No. 109 to conform with the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act.

instruction: Who must approve a government contract that is required by law to be acted upon by the President?
input: a. All Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: The NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, must favorably act upon and/or approve it.

instruction: How long does NEDA have to submit its recommendation on a government contract requiring presidential approval to the NEDA Board?
input: c. Within thirty (30) days from its receipt of the Government Contract with complete documentation, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, NEDA shall submit its recommendation to the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, for appropriate action.
output: NEDA has thirty days from the receipt of the complete documentation to submit its recommendation to the NEDA Board.

instruction: What must be done with a government contract worth at least P300 Million after it is signed or approved?
input: SECTION 10. Submission of Government Contracts. — With a view to creating a repository of all important Government Contracts, a complete copy of all Government Contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the date of signing and/or approval thereof...
output: A complete copy of the contract, along with related documents, must be submitted to the NEDA Director-General within seven days.

instruction: What law governs Build Operate and Transfer (BOT) schemes and other variations?
input: c. BOT Contracts. Contracts undertaken through Build Operate and Transfer (BOT) schemes and other variations shall be governed by Republic Act No. 6957, as amended by Republic Act No. 7718, and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
output: They are governed by Republic Act No. 6957, as amended by Republic Act No. 7718, and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: If a government contract is being processed under the old Executive Order No. 109, what happens to its processing?
input: SECTION 13. Prospective Application. — All Government Contracts, including those presently being processed and/or reviewed in accordance with Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002, shall hereafter be processed and/or reviewed in accordance with this Executive Order.
output: It must now be processed and/or reviewed in accordance with this new Executive Order.

instruction: What is the primary objective behind the issuance of Executive Order No. 109-A?
input: WHEREAS, in line with the government’s program of good governance, Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 entitled “Streamlining The Rules And Procedures On The Review And Approval Of All Contracts Of Departments, Bureaus, Offices, And Agencies Of The Government, Including Government-Owned Or Controlled Corporations And Their Subsidiaries” was issued for the expeditious implementation of development projects and the speedy delivery of basic services while promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions;
output: The objective is to promote good governance, including transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions, and to streamline the approval process.

instruction: According to RA 9184, who is a 'Head of the procuring entity'?
input: As defined under Section 5(j) of Republic Act No. 9184, a Head of the procuring entity refers to (i) the head of the agency or his duly authorized official, for national government agencies, or (ii) the governing board or its duly authorized official, for government-owned and/or -controlled corporations.
output: For national government agencies, it's the head of the agency or their duly authorized official. For government-owned and/or-controlled corporations, it's the governing board or its authorized official.

instruction: What should the GPPB do regarding ODA-funded contracts?
input: The GPPB may issue guidelines for Government Contracts finance with ODA funds with the objective of promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions, and, where applicable, complying with the requirements of an open and competitive public bidding, consistent with Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations...
output: The GPPB may issue guidelines to promote transparency, competitiveness, and accountability, and ensure compliance with open and competitive public bidding requirements.

instruction: What does this Executive Order say about splitting government contracts?
input: SECTION 11. Splitting of Government Contracts. — Splitting of Government Contracts is not allowed.
output: Splitting of government contracts is not allowed.

instruction: What is the consequence for a government official who approves a contract that violates the law?
input: The Heads of the procuring entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, shall be responsible and accountable for ensuring that all Government Contracts they approve and/or enter into are in accordance with existing laws, rules and regulations and are consistent with the spending and development priorities of government.
output: They are responsible and accountable for ensuring the contract is in accordance with existing laws and regulations.

instruction: When did this Executive Order take effect?
input: SEC. 15. This Executive Order shall take effect immediately upon publication in two (2) newspapers of general circulation.
output: It took effect immediately upon its publication in two newspapers of general circulation.

instruction: What is the role of NEDA when a government contract requires presidential approval?
input: b. All Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall be submitted with complete documentation to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the approval by the Head of the procuring entity concerned...
output: NEDA reviews and evaluates the contract and then submits a recommendation to the NEDA Board for appropriate action.

instruction: What is the objective for NEDA and GPPB to issue guidelines for joint venture agreements?
input: The NEDA, in consultation with the GPPB, shall issue guidelines regarding joint venture agreements with private entities with the objective of promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions and, where applicable, complying with the requirements of an open and competitive public bidding.
output: The objective is to promote transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions, and to ensure compliance with open and competitive public bidding requirements.

instruction: If a government contract is for the lease of goods and real estate, what law governs it?
input: Contracts for the lease of goods and real estate shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Cf. Section 5(n), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: How is the NEDA Board involved in the approval of contracts that require presidential action?
input: All Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President...shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: The NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, must favorably act upon and/or approve the contract before it can be signed.

instruction: How is a procuring entity head defined under RA 9184?
input: As defined under Section 5(j) of Republic Act No. 9184, a Head of the procuring entity refers to (i) the head of the agency or his duly authorized official, for national government agencies, or (ii) the governing board or its duly authorized official, for government-owned and/or -controlled corporations.
output: It is either the head of the agency or their authorized official for national government agencies, or the governing board or its authorized official for government-owned corporations.

instruction: What is the role of the NEDA Director-General in the repository of government contracts?
input: SECTION 10. Submission of Government Contracts. — With a view to creating a repository of all important Government Contracts, a complete copy of all Government Contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the date of signing and/or approval thereof...
output: A complete copy of all government contracts valued at P300 Million or more must be submitted to the NEDA Director-General within seven days of signing.

instruction: What is the main difference in the approval process for a government contract above and below P300 Million using alternative procurement methods?
input: a. For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Of At Least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million). —...the Head of the procuring entity shall... obtain the following requirements: i. An opinion from the Secretary of Justice... ii. Approval from the Director-General of NEDA...b. For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Below Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million). —...the Heads of the procuring entities shall likewise have full authority to give final approval and/or enter into Government Contracts of their respective Government Agencies, entered into through alternative methods of procurement allowed by law...
output: For contracts of P300 Million or more, the head of the procuring entity must first get an opinion from the Secretary of Justice and NEDA Director-General approval. For contracts below that amount, the head of the procuring entity has full authority to approve and enter into them.

instruction: What is the legal standing of a contract that is entered into in violation of this Executive Order?
input: All Government Contracts entered into in violation of the provisions of law, rules and regulations, and this Executive Order shall be considered contracts entered into without authority and are thus invalid and not binding on the government.
output: Such a contract is considered invalid, entered into without authority, and is not binding on the government.

instruction: How long after a contract requiring presidential action is submitted to NEDA does the NEDA Board have to take action?
input: c. Within thirty (30) days from its receipt of the Government Contract with complete documentation... NEDA shall submit its recommendation to the NEDA Board... The NEDA Board, at a meeting chaired by the President, shall then act and/or approve the Government Contract, as it deems appropriate.
output: The NEDA Board should take action on the contract within thirty days from NEDA's receipt of the complete documentation.

instruction: What does the policy of good governance in government procurement aim to promote?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184, otherwise known as the Government Procurement Reform Act, which was enacted into law on January 10, 2003, likewise declared it the policy of the State to promote the ideals of good governance, with a view to transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability and public monitoring in the procurement process of Government Contracts;
output: It aims to promote transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability, and public monitoring in the procurement process.

instruction: What is the main objective of this Executive Order concerning the approval of contracts?
input: WHEREAS, in line with the government’s program of good governance, Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 entitled “Streamlining The Rules And Procedures On The Review And Approval Of All Contracts Of Departments, Bureaus, Offices, And Agencies Of The Government, Including Government-Owned Or Controlled Corporations And Their Subsidiaries” was issued for the expeditious implementation of development projects and the speedy delivery of basic services while promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions;
output: The main objective is to streamline the rules and procedures for the review and approval of government contracts to ensure expeditious implementation of development projects and speedy delivery of basic services.

instruction: What is the specific legal reference for the definition of 'Government Agency'?
input: For this purpose, a Government Agency shall refer to the various units of the Government, including a department, bureau, office, instrumentality, government-owned and/or -controlled corporation or its subsidiary, or state college or university (Cf. Section 2(4) of Executive Order No. 292 dated July 25, 1987, otherwise known as the Administrative Code of 1987).
output: The definition is referenced from Section 2(4) of Executive Order No. 292, the Administrative Code of 1987.

instruction: If a government contract is valued at P300 Million, is it considered for alternative procurement methods?
input: SECTION 4. Approval of Government Contracts Entered Into Through Alternative Methods of Procurement, Other Than Through Public Bidding. a. For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Of At Least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million).
output: Yes, a contract of exactly P300 Million falls under the category of 'at least P300 Million' and requires specific approvals for alternative procurement.

instruction: What is the primary law governing procurement contracts of local government units?
input: SECTION 12. Local Government Units. — Procurement contracts of local government units, regardless of the source of funds, shall be subject to the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
output: Procurement contracts of local government units are subject to Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations, regardless of the funding source.

instruction: What is the role of the Department of Finance regarding government financial institutions?
input: Transactions of government financial institutions in the ordinary course of business shall not be covered by the provisions of this Executive Order. Such transactions shall instead be subject to applicable provisions of law and to guidelines, rules and regulations issued by the Department of Finance.
output: The Department of Finance issues the guidelines, rules, and regulations that govern the transactions of government financial institutions in the ordinary course of business.

instruction: When should the NEDA Board take action on a government contract that requires presidential approval?
input: The NEDA Board, at a meeting chaired by the President, shall then act and/or approve the Government Contract, as it deems appropriate.
output: The NEDA Board should act on or approve the contract after receiving NEDA's recommendation.

instruction: What happens to Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002, as a result of this Executive Order?
input: SEC. 14. Repeal and Amendment. — Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 is hereby repealed. All orders, issuances, memoranda and other Presidential issuances expressly repealed by Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 shall remain repealed.
output: Executive Order No. 109 is repealed by this new Executive Order.

instruction: What is the purpose of submitting important government contracts to NEDA?
input: SECTION 10. Submission of Government Contracts. — With a view to creating a repository of all important Government Contracts, a complete copy of all Government Contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA...
output: The purpose is to create a repository of all important government contracts.

instruction: What is the specific amendment made to Memorandum Order No. 266, series of 1989?
input: Memorandum Order No. 266 dated November 28, 1989 insofar as it relates to joint venture agreements with private entities... is hereby amended accordingly.
output: The part of Memorandum Order No. 266 that relates to joint venture agreements with private entities is amended.

instruction: What is the specific amendment made to Department of Public Works and Highways Circular No. 125, series of 1993?
input: Department of Public Works and Highways Circular No. 125, series of 1993 insofar as it relates to the lease of real estate, are hereby amended accordingly.
output: The part of Circular No. 125 that relates to the lease of real estate is amended.

instruction: For a government contract worth at least P300 Million, what specific approvals are required for alternative procurement methods?
input: SECTION 4. Approval of Government Contracts Entered Into Through Alternative Methods of Procurement, Other Than Through Public Bidding. a. For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Of At Least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million). —...obtain the following requirements: i. An opinion from the Secretary of Justice that said Government Contract falls within the exceptions from public bidding; and ii. Approval from the Director-General of NEDA to proceed with a specific alternative method of procurement under the exceptional cases provided by law and applicable rules and regulations.
output: An opinion from the Secretary of Justice and approval from the NEDA Director-General are required.

instruction: What are the two main types of heads of procuring entities defined by RA 9184?
input: As defined under Section 5(j) of Republic Act No. 9184, a Head of the procuring entity refers to (i) the head of the agency or his duly authorized official, for national government agencies, or (ii) the governing board or its duly authorized official, for government-owned and/or -controlled corporations.
output: The two types are the head of the agency (or authorized official) for national government agencies and the governing board (or authorized official) for government-owned and/or-controlled corporations.

instruction: What is the core principle of government contracts under this Executive Order?
input: It is the policy of this Administration that all Government Contracts of Government Agencies, including procurement contracts, shall be awarded through open and competitive public bidding, save in exceptional cases provided by law and applicable rules and regulations, as described in Section 3 of this Executive Order.
output: The core principle is that all government contracts should be awarded through open and competitive public bidding.

instruction: What is the legal basis for the exceptions to public bidding?
input: Sections 48 to 53 of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations provide for exceptional cases where the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods and consulting services may be undertaken through alternative methods of procurement, other than through public bidding.
output: The exceptions are provided for in Sections 48 to 53 of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: What is the role of the NEDA Board in the approval of government contracts that require presidential action?
input: The NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, shall then act and/or approve the Government Contract, as it deems appropriate.
output: The NEDA Board acts on and/or approves the government contract after NEDA has submitted its recommendation.

instruction: Can the full authority to approve contracts using alternative methods be delegated for contracts below P300 million?
input: The Heads of the procuring entities may delegate in writing this full authority to give final approval and/or enter into Government Contracts involving an amount of below Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) entered into through alternative methods of procurement allowed by law, other than through public bidding, as circumstances may warrant...
output: Yes, the heads of procuring entities can delegate this full authority in writing, subject to any limitations they impose.

instruction: How is the NEDA Director-General notified of the NEDA Board's action on a government contract?
input: Within seven (7) days from the date of the NEDA Board’s action, NEDA, through its Director-General, shall formally notify the Head of the procuring entity concerned or his/its duly authorized official, as the case may be, of the action of the NEDA Board, including any comments thereon.
output: NEDA, through its Director-General, formally notifies the head of the procuring entity within seven days of the NEDA Board's action.

instruction: What types of contracts are governed by RA 9184?
input: Contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations... Contracts for the lease of goods and real estate shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
output: Contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, consulting services, and the lease of goods and real estate are all governed by RA 9184.

instruction: What is the purpose of issuing guidelines for joint venture agreements?
input: The NEDA, in consultation with the GPPB, shall issue guidelines regarding joint venture agreements with private entities with the objective of promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions and, where applicable, complying with the requirements of an open and competitive public bidding.
output: To promote transparency, competitiveness, and accountability, and to ensure compliance with the requirements of open and competitive public bidding.

instruction: What are the core ideals of good governance promoted by the Government Procurement Reform Act?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184, otherwise known as the Government Procurement Reform Act, which was enacted into law on January 10, 2003, likewise declared it the policy of the State to promote the ideals of good governance, with a view to transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability and public monitoring in the procurement process of Government Contracts;
output: The core ideals are transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability, and public monitoring.

instruction: What specific law governs contracts undertaken through Build Operate and Transfer (BOT) schemes?
input: BOT Contracts. Contracts undertaken through Build Operate and Transfer (BOT) schemes and other variations shall be governed by Republic Act No. 6957, as amended by Republic Act No. 7718, and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
output: Republic Act No. 6957, as amended by Republic Act No. 7718.

instruction: What is the consequence of not submitting a complete set of documents for a contract requiring presidential approval?
input: All Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall be submitted with complete documentation to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the approval by the Head of the procuring entity concerned...
output: The contract will not be reviewed and evaluated by NEDA, thus preventing the NEDA Board from taking action.

instruction: What is the role of the Secretary of Justice in the alternative procurement process for contracts over P300M?
input: a. For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Of At Least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million). —...the Head of the procuring entity shall... obtain the following requirements: i. An opinion from the Secretary of Justice that said Government Contract falls within the exceptions from public bidding...
output: The Secretary of Justice must provide an opinion that the government contract falls within the exceptions from public bidding.

instruction: What law governs the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services?
input: Contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Cf. Section 4, Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: How are procurement contracts of local government units handled?
input: Procurement contracts of local government units, regardless of the source of funds, shall be subject to the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
output: They are subject to the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: What is the effective date of this Executive Order?
input: SEC. 15. This Executive Order shall take effect immediately upon publication in two (2) newspapers of general circulation. DONE in the City of Manila, this 18 day of September, in the year of our Lord Two Thousand and Three.
output: September 18, 2003, upon its publication in two newspapers of general circulation.

instruction: What is the primary reason for issuing E.O. 109-A?
input: WHEREAS, it has become necessary to amend the provisions of Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 to make it conform with the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184;
output: To amend E.O. 109 to conform with the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184, also known as the Government Procurement Reform Act.

instruction: What is the consequence for a government official if they enter into a contract that violates the law?
input: The Heads of the procuring entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, shall be responsible and accountable for ensuring that all Government Contracts they approve and/or enter into are in accordance with existing laws, rules and regulations and are consistent with the spending and development priorities of government. All Government Contracts entered into in violation of the provisions of law, rules and regulations, and this Executive Order shall be considered contracts entered into without authority and are thus invalid and not binding on the government.
output: They are held responsible and accountable, and the contract they approved is considered invalid and not binding on the government.

instruction: What is the purpose of the 'repository of all important Government Contracts'?
input: With a view to creating a repository of all important Government Contracts, a complete copy of all Government Contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA, through its Director-General...
output: To create a centralized location for important government contracts valued at P300 million or more.

instruction: What is the significance of the NEDA Board being chaired by the President?
input: All Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: It ensures that the President has a direct role in the review and approval of government contracts that require presidential action.

instruction: What specific contracts are not covered by this Executive Order?
input: Transactions of government financial institutions in the ordinary course of business shall not be covered by the provisions of this Executive Order. Such transactions shall instead be subject to applicable provisions of law and to guidelines, rules and regulations issued by the Department of Finance.
output: Transactions of government financial institutions in the ordinary course of business are not covered.

instruction: What is the requirement for a contract to be binding on the government?
input: All Government Contracts shall require the approval and signature of the respective Heads of the procuring entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, as required by law, applicable rules and regulations, and by this Executive Order, before said Government Contracts shall be considered approved in accordance with law and binding on the government, except as may be otherwise provided in Republic Act No. 9184.
output: It must have the approval and signature of the head of the procuring entity or their duly authorized official.

instruction: Who is responsible for ensuring that a government contract is in accordance with existing laws and regulations?
input: The Heads of the procuring entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, shall be responsible and accountable for ensuring that all Government Contracts they approve and/or enter into are in accordance with existing laws, rules and regulations and are consistent with the spending and development priorities of government.
output: The heads of the procuring entities or their duly authorized officials are responsible and accountable.

instruction: Under what circumstances can the heads of procuring entities delegate their authority to approve government contracts?
input: The Heads of the procuring entities may delegate in writing this full authority to give final approval and/or enter into Government Contracts awarded through public bidding as circumstances may warrant (i.e., decentralization of procurement in a Government Agency), subject to such limitations imposed by the Head of the procuring entity concerned...
output: They can delegate their authority in writing as circumstances warrant, subject to the limitations they impose.

instruction: What are the rules regarding the splitting of government contracts?
input: Splitting of Government Contracts is not allowed. Splitting of Government Contracts means the division or breaking up of Government Contracts into smaller quantities and amounts, or dividing contract implementation into artificial phases or sub-contracts for the purpose of evading or circumventing the requirements of law and this Executive Order, especially the necessity of public bidding and the requirements for exceptions therefrom in accordance with Section 4(a) hereof.
output: Splitting of contracts is strictly prohibited as it is a method to evade or circumvent the requirements of the law, especially public bidding.

instruction: What are the requirements for a government contract entered into through alternative methods, with a value of at least P300M, to be considered approved?
input: After obtaining the foregoing requirements, except for Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, the Heads of the procuring entities shall have full authority to give final approval and/or enter into Government Contracts of their respective Government Agencies, entered into through alternative methods of procurement allowed by law, other than through public bidding, where the Government Contract involves an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million).
output: After obtaining an opinion from the Secretary of Justice and approval from the NEDA Director-General, the head of the procuring entity has the full authority to give final approval and enter into the contract.

instruction: What does this Executive Order state about the lease of real estate?
input: Contracts for the lease of goods and real estate shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Cf. Section 5(n), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Contracts for the lease of real estate are governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: Who must be formally notified of the NEDA Board's action on a contract and by whom?
input: Within seven (7) days from the date of the NEDA Board’s action, NEDA, through its Director-General, shall formally notify the Head of the procuring entity concerned or his/its duly authorized official, as the case may be, of the action of the NEDA Board, including any comments thereon.
output: The head of the procuring entity or their duly authorized official must be formally notified by NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven days of the NEDA Board's action.

instruction: What is the main goal of the Government Procurement Reform Act?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184, otherwise known as the Government Procurement Reform Act, which was enacted into law on January 10, 2003, likewise declared it the policy of the State to promote the ideals of good governance, with a view to transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability and public monitoring in the procurement process of Government Contracts;
output: Its goal is to promote good governance by ensuring transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability, and public monitoring in the government procurement process.

instruction: Who has the authority to approve government contracts that are required by law to be acted upon by the President?
input: a. All Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: The NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has the authority.

instruction: What is the minimum amount for a government contract to be submitted to NEDA for repository purposes?
input: SECTION 10. Submission of Government Contracts. — With a view to creating a repository of all important Government Contracts, a complete copy of all Government Contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA, through its Director-General...
output: A contract must be valued at least P300 Million.

instruction: If a government contract needs presidential approval, what must be done before it can be signed?
input: All Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President...shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: It cannot be signed until the NEDA Board, chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved it.

instruction: What is the timeframe for NEDA to notify a procuring entity head of the NEDA Board's action?
input: Within seven (7) days from the date of the NEDA Board’s action, NEDA, through its Director-General, shall formally notify the Head of the procuring entity concerned or his/its duly authorized official, as the case may be, of the action of the NEDA Board, including any comments thereon.
output: NEDA has seven days from the date of the NEDA Board's action to formally notify the head of the procuring entity.

instruction: Who has the full authority to approve and enter into government contracts that are awarded through public bidding?
input: Except for Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, the Heads of the procuring entities shall have full authority to give final approval and/or enter into all Government Contracts of their respective Government Agencies, awarded through public bidding, regardless of the amount involved.
output: The heads of the procuring entities have full authority, regardless of the amount involved, except for contracts requiring presidential action.

instruction: What is the policy for local government unit procurement contracts?
input: Procurement contracts of local government units, regardless of the source of funds, shall be subject to the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
output: Procurement contracts of LGUs are subject to RA 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations, regardless of the source of funds.

instruction: What is the official name of RA 9184?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184, otherwise known as the Government Procurement Reform Act...
output: The Government Procurement Reform Act.

instruction: Who is responsible for issuing rules and regulations for government financial institutions' transactions?
input: Such transactions shall instead be subject to applicable provisions of law and to guidelines, rules and regulations issued by the Department of Finance.
output: The Department of Finance.

instruction: What is the main change introduced by E.O. 109-A?
input: WHEREAS, it has become necessary to amend the provisions of Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 to make it conform with the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184;
output: It amends E.O. 109 to align with the provisions of the Government Procurement Reform Act (RA 9184).

instruction: What is the consequence of entering into a government contract without proper authority?
input: All Government Contracts entered into in violation of the provisions of law, rules and regulations, and this Executive Order shall be considered contracts entered into without authority and are thus invalid and not binding on the government.
output: The contract is considered invalid and not binding on the government.

instruction: How are government contracts financed with Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds governed?
input: Government Contracts financed wholly or partly with Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds shall be governed by Republic Act No. 4860, as amended, Republic Act No. 8182, as amended by Republic Act No. 8555, and Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations...
output: They are governed by RA 4860, RA 8182, and RA 9184, along with their respective Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: What is the purpose of the submission of contracts to NEDA, as per Section 10?
input: With a view to creating a repository of all important Government Contracts, a complete copy of all Government Contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the date of signing and/or approval thereof...
output: To establish a centralized repository for all significant government contracts.

instruction: What is the role of the NEDA Board regarding government contracts that need presidential approval?
input: The NEDA Board, at a meeting chaired by the President, shall then act and/or approve the Government Contract, as it deems appropriate.
output: The NEDA Board acts on and/or approves the contracts after they have been submitted with complete documentation and NEDA's recommendation.

instruction: What is the policy regarding the public bidding of government contracts?
input: It is the policy of this Administration that all Government Contracts of Government Agencies, including procurement contracts, shall be awarded through open and competitive public bidding, save in exceptional cases provided by law and applicable rules and regulations, as described in Section 3 of this Executive Order.
output: All government contracts should be awarded through open and competitive public bidding, with exceptions only as provided by law.

instruction: What document governs contracts for the lease of real estate?
input: Contracts for the lease of goods and real estate shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Cf. Section 5(n), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: What is the purpose of streamlining rules and procedures on government contracts?
input: WHEREAS, in line with the government’s program of good governance, Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 entitled “Streamlining The Rules And Procedures On The Review And Approval Of All Contracts Of Departments, Bureaus, Offices, And Agencies Of The Government, Including Government-Owned Or Controlled Corporations And Their Subsidiaries” was issued for the expeditious implementation of development projects and the speedy delivery of basic services while promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions;
output: To expedite the implementation of development projects and the delivery of basic services while promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability.

instruction: What specific law governs the acquisition of real property for national government infrastructure projects?
input: Contracts for the acquisition of real property needed as right-of-way, site or location for national government infrastructure projects shall be governed by Republic Act No. 8974 (Cf. Section 5(n), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Republic Act No. 8974.

instruction: What is the scope of government procurement contracts covered by RA 9184?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184 consolidated the procurement processes of Government Contracts, including the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods and consulting services, and lease of goods and real estate, among others;
output: RA 9184 covers the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, consulting services, and the lease of goods and real estate.

instruction: What must be done to ensure a government contract is valid and binding?
input: All Government Contracts shall require the approval and signature of the respective Heads of the procuring entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, as required by law, applicable rules and regulations, and by this Executive Order, before said Government Contracts shall be considered approved in accordance with law and binding on the government, except as may be otherwise provided in Republic Act No. 9184.
output: It requires the approval and signature of the head of the procuring entity or their duly authorized official, in accordance with the law.

instruction: Can a head of a procuring entity delegate their full authority to approve and enter into contracts?
input: The Heads of the procuring entities may delegate in writing this full authority to give final approval and/or enter into Government Contracts awarded through public bidding as circumstances may warrant...
output: Yes, they can delegate this authority in writing, but it's subject to limitations they impose.

instruction: What is the purpose of amending E.O. 109 with E.O. 109-A?
input: WHEREAS, it has become necessary to amend the provisions of Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 to make it conform with the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184;
output: To make the provisions of E.O. 109 conform with the Government Procurement Reform Act (RA 9184).

instruction: Who is responsible and accountable for ensuring that approved government contracts are in accordance with existing laws?
input: The Heads of the procuring entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, shall be responsible and accountable for ensuring that all Government Contracts they approve and/or enter into are in accordance with existing laws, rules and regulations and are consistent with the spending and development priorities of government.
output: The heads of the procuring entities or their duly authorized officials are responsible and accountable.

instruction: What happens to the provisions of Executive Order No. 109-A that are inconsistent with other presidential directives?
input: All other Presidential directives, issuances, orders, rules and regulations or parts thereof inconsistent with this Executive Order are likewise hereby repealed or modified accordingly.
output: They are repealed or modified accordingly.

instruction: When is splitting of government contracts considered a violation?
input: Splitting of Government Contracts means the division or breaking up of Government Contracts into smaller quantities and amounts, or dividing contract implementation into artificial phases or sub-contracts for the purpose of evading or circumventing the requirements of law and this Executive Order, especially the necessity of public bidding and the requirements for exceptions therefrom in accordance with Section 4(a) hereof.
output: It is a violation when it is done for the purpose of evading or circumventing the requirements of law, especially public bidding.

instruction: How are contracts for the acquisition of right-of-way for national government projects governed?
input: Contracts for the acquisition of real property needed as right-of-way, site or location for national government infrastructure projects shall be governed by Republic Act No. 8974 (Cf. Section 5(n), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: They are governed by Republic Act No. 8974.

instruction: What is the purpose of the GPPB issuing guidelines for ODA-funded contracts?
input: The GPPB may issue guidelines for Government Contracts finance with ODA funds with the objective of promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions, and, where applicable, complying with the requirements of an open and competitive public bidding, consistent with Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Cf. Section 4, Republic Act No. 9184)
output: To promote transparency, competitiveness, and accountability, and to ensure compliance with open and competitive public bidding requirements.

instruction: If a contract is below P300 Million and uses an alternative procurement method, who has the final approval authority?
input: For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Below Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million). — Except for Government Contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, the Heads of the procuring entities shall likewise have full authority to give final approval and/or enter into Government Contracts of their respective Government Agencies, entered into through alternative methods of procurement allowed by law, other than through public bidding, where the Government Contract involves an amount below Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million).
output: The head of the procuring entity has full authority to give final approval and/or enter into the contract, unless it requires presidential action.

instruction: What happens if a contract is not in accordance with existing laws and regulations?
input: All Government Contracts entered into in violation of the provisions of law, rules and regulations, and this Executive Order shall be considered contracts entered into without authority and are thus invalid and not binding on the government.
output: It is considered a contract entered into without authority, making it invalid and not binding on the government.

instruction: What is the definition of 'Government Contracts' for the purpose of this document?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184 consolidated the procurement processes of Government Contracts, including the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods and consulting services, and lease of goods and real estate, among others;
output: Government contracts include the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, consulting services, and the lease of goods and real estate.

instruction: What is the goal of the government's program of good governance?
input: WHEREAS, in line with the government’s program of good governance, Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 entitled “Streamlining The Rules And Procedures On The Review And Approval Of All Contracts Of Departments, Bureaus, Offices, And Agencies Of The Government, Including Government-Owned Or Controlled Corporations And Their Subsidiaries” was issued for the expeditious implementation of development projects and the speedy delivery of basic services while promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions;
output: To ensure expeditious implementation of development projects and speedy delivery of basic services while promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions.

instruction: What is the relationship between this Executive Order and RA 9184?
input: WHEREAS, it has become necessary to amend the provisions of Executive Order No. 109 dated May 27, 2002 to make it conform with the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184, otherwise known as the Government Procurement Reform Act;
output: This Executive Order was issued to amend a previous one to make it conform with the provisions of RA 9184.

instruction: What is the primary purpose of Memorandum Order No. 144?
input: REMINDING ALL HEADS OF NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, GOVERNMENT-OWNED AND CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS, AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO FAITHFULLY COMPLY WITH SECTION 13, ARTICLE V OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184, “AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION, STANDARDIZATION AND REGULATION OF THE PROCUREMENT ACTIVITIES OF THE GOVERNEMNT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES,” ON INVITATION OF NON-GOVERNMENT ORGANIZATIONS AS OBSERVERS IN THE BIDS AND AWARDS COMMITTEE PROCEEDINGS
output: The purpose is to remind heads of government agencies to comply with the requirement of inviting observers to Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) proceedings to enhance transparency.

instruction: Which government entities are reminded to comply with Memorandum Order No. 144?
input: all heads of National Government agencies, government-owned and controlled corporations, and local government units are hereby reminded to invite, in all stages of the procurement process, in addition to the representative of the Commission on Audit, at least two (2) observers to sit in Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) proceedings
output: Heads of National Government agencies, government-owned and controlled corporations (GOCCs), and local government units (LGUs).

instruction: Based on the memorandum, how many observers must be invited to the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) proceedings?
input: at least two (2) observers to sit in Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) proceedings, one (1) from a duly recognized private group in a sector or discipline relevant to the procurement at hand, and the other from a non-government organization (NGO), in order to enhance transparency of the procurement process.
output: At least two observers, in addition to the representative from the Commission on Audit (COA).

instruction: What is the date when Memorandum Order No. 144 was issued?
input: Issued this 13th day of August 2004.
output: August 13, 2004.

instruction: What is the full name of the law referred to as RA 9184?
input: Republic Act (RA) No. 9184, 'AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION, STANDARDIZATION AND REGULATION OF THE PROCUREMENT ACTIVITIES OF THE GOVERNEMNT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES'
output: An Act Providing for the Modernization, Standardization and Regulation of the Procurement Activities of the Government and for Other Purposes.

instruction: What is the primary policy regarding government contracts as stated in Executive Order No. 423?
input: Section 1. Policy Requiring Public Bidding. It is the policy of this Administration that all Government contracts of Government Agencies shall be awarded through open and competitive public bidding, save in exceptional cases provided by law and applicable rules and regulations, as described in Section 3 of this Executive Order.
