output: Executive Order No. 423 was signed by Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo on April 30, 2005.

instruction: What is the purpose of Executive Order No. 423?
input: REPEALING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 109-A DATED SEPTEMBER 18, 2003 PRESCRIBING THE RULES AND PROCEDURES ON THE REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF ALL GOVERNMENT CONTRACTS TO CONFORM WITH REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT REFORM ACT”
output: It repeals Executive Order No. 109-A to conform with Republic Act No. 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act.

instruction: According to the document, what is the definition of a 'Government Agency'?
input: For this purpose, a Government Agency shall refer to the various units of the Government, including a department, bureau, office, instrumentality, government-owned and/or controlled corporation or its subsidiary, or state college or university (Section 2[4] of Executive Order No. 292 dated July 25, 1987, otherwise known as the Administrative Code of 1987).
output: A Government Agency refers to various units of the Government, such as a department, bureau, office, instrumentality, government-owned and/or controlled corporation or its subsidiary, or state college or university.

instruction: For a procurement officer, who has the authority to approve government contracts awarded through public bidding?
input: Except for Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, the Heads of the Procuring Entities shall have full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into all Government contracts of their respective agencies awarded through public bidding, regardless of the amount involved.
output: The Heads of the Procuring Entities have full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into government contracts awarded through public bidding, regardless of the amount.

instruction: Under what condition can the Head of the Procuring Entity delegate their authority to approve government contracts?
input: The Heads of the Procuring Entities may delegate in writing this full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into Government contracts awarded through public bidding, as circumstances may warrant (i.e., decentralization of procurement in a Government Agency), subject to such limitations imposed by the Head of the Procuring Entity concerned (Section 5(j), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: They may delegate this authority in writing, as circumstances warrant (e.g., decentralization), subject to limitations they impose.

instruction: How is a 'Head of the Procuring Entity' defined under Republic Act No. 9184?
input: As defined under Section 5(j) of Republic Act No. 9184, a Head of the Procuring Entity refers to (i) the head of the agency or his duly authorized official, for national government agencies; or (ii) the governing board or its duly authorized official, for government-owned and/or controlled corporations, among others.
output: For national government agencies, it's the head of the agency or their authorized official. For government-owned and/or controlled corporations, it's the governing board or its authorized official.

instruction: What law provides for alternative methods of procurement besides public bidding?
input: Sections 48 to 53 of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations provide for exceptional cases where the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods and consulting services may be undertaken through alternative methods of procurement.
output: Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations provide for exceptional cases where alternative procurement methods may be used.

instruction: If a government contract involves at least P500 million and uses an alternative procurement method, what two requirements must be obtained before proceeding?
input: Where the Head of the Procuring Entity has made a determination that a Government contract, including Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, involving an amount of at least Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500 Million) falls under any of the exceptions from public bidding described in Section 3 hereof, the Head of the Procuring Entity shall, before proceeding with the alternative methods of procurement provided by law and applicable rules and regulations, obtain the following requirements: i. An opinion from the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) that said Government contract falls within the exceptions from public bidding; and ii. Approval from the Director-General of NEDA to proceed with a specific alternative method of procurement under the exceptional cases provided by law and applicable rules and regulations.
output: The Procuring Entity must first obtain an opinion from the GPPB confirming the exception from public bidding and approval from the NEDA Director-General to proceed with the specific alternative method.

instruction: What is required of the Head of the Procuring Entity when certifying a contract's compliance?
input: Provided, that the Head of the Procuring Entity certifies under oath that the contract has been entered into in faithful compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.
output: The Head of the Procuring Entity must certify under oath that the contract was entered into in faithful compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.

instruction: Under EO 423, who has the authority to approve government contracts involving less than P500 million entered into through alternative methods of procurement?
input: For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Below Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500 Million). – Except for Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, the Heads of the Procuring Entities shall likewise have full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into Government contracts of their respective agencies, entered into through alternative methods of procurement allowed by law.
output: The Heads of the Procuring Entities have full authority to give final approval to contracts below P500 million entered into via alternative methods, except those requiring Presidential action.

instruction: What is the requirement for a Department Secretary to approve a government contract under P500 million entered into via an alternative method?
input: Provided, that the Department Secretary certifies under oath that the contract has been entered into in faithful compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.
output: The Department Secretary must certify under oath that the contract has been entered into in faithful compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.

instruction: If a contract is entered into in violation of the provisions of EO 423, what is its legal status?
input: All Government contracts entered into in violation of the provisions of law, rules and regulations, and of this Executive Order shall be considered contracts entered into without authority and are thus invalid and not binding on the Government.
output: Such a contract is considered invalid and not binding on the Government, as it was entered into without authority.

instruction: For contracts that require Presidential action, what is the first step in the approval process as outlined in Section 6?
input: All Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: The NEDA Board, chaired by the President, must first favorably act upon and/or approve the contract before it can be signed.

instruction: Within how many days must a government contract requiring Presidential action be submitted to NEDA?
input: All Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall be submitted with complete documentation to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the approval by the Head of the Procuring Entity concerned or his/its duly authorized official, as the case may be, for NEDA’s review and evaluation.
output: It must be submitted within seven (7) days from the approval by the Head of the Procuring Entity.

instruction: What should accompany a government contract when it is submitted to NEDA for review?
input: Government contracts submitted hereunder shall be accompanied by a complete execution copy of the contract, related agreements, annexes, other approvals and permits, including a detailed summary of the pertinent laws, rules and regulations governing the processing and award of the contract, and accompanied by the requirements of Section 4(a) hereof where alternative methods of procurement were resorted to.
output: The contract must be accompanied by a complete execution copy, related agreements, annexes, other approvals, permits, a detailed summary of governing laws, and the requirements of Section 4(a) if alternative methods were used.

instruction: How long does NEDA have to submit its recommendation to the NEDA Board?
input: Within thirty (30) days from its receipt of the Government contract with complete documentation, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, NEDA shall submit, its recommendation to the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, for appropriate action.
output: NEDA has thirty (30) days from its receipt of the complete documentation to submit its recommendation to the NEDA Board.

instruction: After the NEDA Board acts on a contract, how long does NEDA have to notify the Procuring Entity?
input: Within seven (7) days from the date of the NEDA Board’s action, NEDA, through its Director-General, shall formally notify the Head of the Procuring Entity concerned or his/its duly authorized official, as the case may be, of the action of the NEDA Board, including any comments thereon.
output: NEDA must formally notify the Head of the Procuring Entity within seven (7) days from the NEDA Board's action.

instruction: For a contract that the NEDA Board has favorably acted upon, what two things must the Department Secretary and Head of Procuring Entity certify under oath?
input: Provided, that the Department Secretary and Head of Procuring Entity shall certify under oath that: (1) such contract complies with the Constitution and all existing laws, rules and regulations and that (2) such contract is not grossly disadvantageous to the government.
output: They must certify that the contract complies with the Constitution and all existing laws, rules and regulations, and that it is not grossly disadvantageous to the government.

instruction: Which law governs contracts for the acquisition of real property for national government infrastructure projects?
input: Contracts for the acquisition of real property needed as right-of-way, site or location for national government infrastructure projects shall be governed by Republic Act No. 8974 (Section 5[n]), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Republic Act No. 8974 governs such contracts.

instruction: What law governs contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services?
input: Contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 4, Republic Act. No. 9184).
output: These contracts are governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: Which law governs Build-Operate and Transfer (BOT) schemes?
input: BOT Contracts. Contracts undertaken through Build-Operate and Transfer (BOT) schemes and other variations shall be governed by Republic Act No. 6957, as amended by Republic Act No. 7718, and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
output: Republic Act No. 6957, as amended by Republic Act No. 7718, and its Implementing Rules and Regulations govern BOT schemes.

instruction: What is the policy for government contracts financed by Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds?
input: Government Contracts financed wholly or partly with Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds shall be governed by Republic Act No. 4860, as amended, Republic Act No. 8182, as amended by Republic Act No. 8555, and Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 4, Republic Act No. 9184).
output: They are governed by Republic Act No. 4860, RA 8182, and RA 9184 and their respective Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: Which government body can issue guidelines for government contracts financed with ODA funds?
input: The GPPB may issue guidelines for Government Contracts financed with ODA funds with the objective of promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions, and, where applicable, complying with the requirements of an open and competitive public bidding, consistent with Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 4, Republic Act No. 9184).
output: The Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) may issue such guidelines.

instruction: Who is responsible for issuing guidelines on joint venture agreements with private entities?
input: The NEDA, in consultation with the GPPB, shall issue guidelines regarding joint venture agreements with private entities with the objective of promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions, and, where applicable, complying with the requirements of an open and competitive public bidding.
output: The NEDA, in consultation with the GPPB, shall issue the guidelines.

instruction: What is the rule regarding transactions of government financial institutions?
input: Transactions of government financial institutions in the ordinary course of business shall not be covered by the provisions of this Executive Order. Such transactions shall instead be subject to applicable provisions of law and to guidelines, rules and regulations issued by the Department of Finance.
output: Transactions of government financial institutions in the ordinary course of business are not covered by this Executive Order; they are subject to laws and guidelines issued by the Department of Finance.

instruction: What is the threshold for a government contract to be submitted to NEDA for repository purposes?
input: With a view to creating a repository of all important Government contracts, a complete copy of all Government contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the date of signing and/or approval thereof.
output: A complete copy of all contracts involving at least P300 million must be submitted to NEDA.

instruction: What is 'splitting of Government contracts' and is it allowed?
input: Splitting of Government contracts is not allowed. Splitting of Government contracts means the division or breaking up of Government contracts into smaller quantities and amounts, or dividing contract implementation into artificial phases or sub-contracts for the purpose of evading or circumventing the requirements of law and this Executive Order, especially the necessity of public bidding and the requirements for exceptions therefrom in accordance with Section 4(a) hereof.
output: It is the division of contracts into smaller parts to evade legal requirements like public bidding, and it is not allowed.

instruction: What law governs procurement contracts of local government units?
input: Procurement contracts of local government units, regardless of the source of funds, shall be subject to the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
output: All procurement contracts of local government units are subject to the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: What happens to government contracts that were being processed under Executive Order No. 109-A?
input: All Government contracts, including those presently being processed and/or reviewed in accordance with Executive Order No. 109-A dated September 18, 2003, shall hereafter be processed and/or reviewed in accordance with this Executive Order.
output: They will now be processed and/or reviewed according to the rules of Executive Order No. 423.

instruction: What specific Executive Order is repealed by Executive Order No. 423?
input: Executive Order No. 109-A dated September 18, 2003 is hereby repealed.
output: Executive Order No. 109-A is repealed.

instruction: When did Executive Order No. 423 take effect?
input: This Executive Order shall take effect immediately upon publication in two (2) newspapers of general circulation.
output: It took effect immediately upon publication in two newspapers of general circulation.

instruction: As a bidder, what is the core procurement method mandated for government contracts that I should expect?
input: It is the policy of this Administration that all Government contracts of Government Agencies shall be awarded through open and competitive public bidding, save in exceptional cases provided by law and applicable rules and regulations, as described in Section 3 of this Executive Order.
output: You should expect that government contracts will be awarded through open and competitive public bidding.

instruction: If I am an auditor, what should I look for to confirm a contract's validity if it was awarded through public bidding?
input: Provided, that the Head of the Procuring Entity certifies under oath that the contract has been entered into in faithful compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.
output: You should look for a certification under oath from the Head of the Procuring Entity stating that the contract was entered into in faithful compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.

instruction: What is the maximum amount for a government contract that can be approved by the Head of the Procuring Entity through public bidding without needing Presidential action?
input: Except for Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, the Heads of the Procuring Entities shall have full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into all Government contracts of their respective agencies awarded through public bidding, regardless of the amount involved.
output: There is no maximum amount; the Head of the Procuring Entity has full authority regardless of the amount, as long as the contract is not one that legally requires Presidential action.

instruction: What is the significance of the NEDA Board being chaired by the President in the context of high-value contracts?
input: All Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: It signifies that for contracts requiring Presidential action, the President's approval is obtained through the NEDA Board, which they chair, before the contract can be signed.

instruction: What is the purpose of submitting government contracts of at least P300 million to NEDA?
input: With a view to creating a repository of all important Government contracts, a complete copy of all Government contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the date of signing and/or approval thereof, accompanied with a complete copy of its related agreements, annexes, other approvals and permits, and a detailed summary of the pertinent laws, rules and regulations governing the processing and award of the contract.
output: The purpose is to create a repository of all important government contracts.

instruction: If a government contract is financed with ODA funds, which laws should an officer consult in addition to RA 9184?
input: Government Contracts financed wholly or partly with Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds shall be governed by Republic Act No. 4860, as amended, Republic Act No. 8182, as amended by Republic Act No. 8555, and Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 4, Republic Act No. 9184).
output: They should also consult Republic Act No. 4860, as amended, and Republic Act No. 8182, as amended.

instruction: What is the legal consequence for a contract that is 'grossly disadvantageous to the government'?
input: Provided, that the Department Secretary and Head of Procuring Entity shall certify under oath that: (1) such contract complies with the Constitution and all existing laws, rules and regulations and that (2) such contract is not grossly disadvantageous to the government.
output: While not explicitly stated as a legal consequence for invalidation, the requirement to certify that a contract is 'not grossly disadvantageous' implies that such a contract would be a violation of the certification and therefore considered entered into without authority.

instruction: What specific laws govern the lease of goods and real estate?
input: Contracts for the lease of goods and real estate shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 5[n], Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations govern the lease of goods and real estate.

instruction: If a Head of a Procuring Entity wants to delegate authority for contracts using alternative methods under P500M, what must they do?
input: The Heads of the Procuring Entities may delegate in writing this full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into Government contracts involving an amount below Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500 Million) entered into through alternative methods of procurement allowed by law, as circumstances may warrant (i.e., decentralization of procurement in a Government Agency), subject to existing laws and such limitations imposed by the Head of the Procuring Entity concerned (Section 5(j), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: They may delegate this authority in writing, subject to existing laws and any limitations they impose.

instruction: For a government contract, what is the role of the Heads of Procuring Entities or their authorized officials in ensuring compliance?
input: The Heads of the Procuring Entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, shall be responsible and accountable for ensuring that all Government contracts they approve and/or enter into are in accordance with existing laws, rules and regulations and are consistent with the spending and development priorities of Government.
output: They are responsible and accountable for ensuring that all contracts they approve are in accordance with existing laws, rules, and regulations and are consistent with government spending and development priorities.

instruction: What is the consequence for a government contract entered into without the required authority?
input: All Government contracts entered into in violation of the provisions of law, rules and regulations, and of this Executive Order shall be considered contracts entered into without authority and are thus invalid and not binding on the Government.
output: The contract is considered invalid and not binding on the Government.

instruction: What is the significance of the phrase 'REPEALING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 109-A' in the title of Executive Order No. 423?
input: REPEALING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 109-A DATED SEPTEMBER 18, 2003 PRESCRIBING THE RULES AND PROCEDURES ON THE REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF ALL GOVERNMENT CONTRACTS TO CONFORM WITH REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT REFORM ACT”
output: It indicates that the new Executive Order supersedes the old one, specifically to align with RA 9184.

instruction: As a policymaker, what is the intended purpose of promoting 'good governance' in government procurement?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184, otherwise known as “the Government Procurement Reform Act”, which was enacted into law on January 10, 2003, likewise declared it the policy of the State to promote the ideals of good governance, with a view to transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability and public monitoring in the procurement processes of Government Contracts;
output: The purpose is to achieve transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability, and public monitoring in the procurement processes of government contracts.

instruction: Which government agencies are responsible for the review and approval process of government contracts?
output: The Heads of Procuring Entities have the primary authority, with NEDA and the NEDA Board involved for high-value contracts and those requiring Presidential action.

instruction: What are the key principles of good governance promoted by RA 9184?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184, otherwise known as “the Government Procurement Reform Act”, which was enacted into law on January 10, 2003, likewise declared it the policy of the State to promote the ideals of good governance, with a view to transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability and public monitoring in the procurement processes of Government Contracts;
output: The key principles are transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability, and public monitoring.

instruction: If a government contract is required by law to be approved by the President, what is the final step before signing after the NEDA Board's favorable action?
input: Should the NEDA favorably act on the contract, the Department Secretary and Head of the Procuring Entity is hereby given full powers and authority to approve, sign, execute and deliver any deed or document necessary and proper for the execution and implementation of such contract and subsequent amendments or supplements thereto.
output: The Department Secretary and Head of the Procuring Entity are given full powers to approve, sign, and execute the contract, provided they certify it complies with laws and is not grossly disadvantageous.

instruction: What is the consequence of 'splitting of Government contracts'?
input: Splitting of Government contracts is not allowed. Splitting of Government contracts means the division or breaking up of Government contracts into smaller quantities and amounts, or dividing contract implementation into artificial phases or sub-contracts for the purpose of evading or circumventing the requirements of law and this Executive Order, especially the necessity of public bidding and the requirements for exceptions therefrom in accordance with Section 4(a) hereof.
output: It is not allowed as it is a method of evading or circumventing the legal requirements of public bidding and is therefore a violation of the Executive Order.

instruction: What must accompany a contract submitted to NEDA for repository purposes?
input: a complete copy of all Government contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the date of signing and/or approval thereof, accompanied with a complete copy of its related agreements, annexes, other approvals and permits, and a detailed summary of the pertinent laws, rules and regulations governing the processing and award of the contract.
output: It must be accompanied by a complete copy of the contract, related agreements, annexes, other approvals and permits, and a detailed summary of the governing laws and rules.

instruction: What is the legal basis for the rules and procedures on government procurement?
input: REPEALING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 109-A DATED SEPTEMBER 18, 2003 PRESCRIBING THE RULES AND PROCEDURES ON THE REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF ALL GOVERNMENT CONTRACTS TO CONFORM WITH REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT REFORM ACT”
output: The legal basis is Republic Act No. 9184, the 'Government Procurement Reform Act'.

instruction: If a government contract is being processed and reviewed today, what set of rules should be followed?
input: All Government contracts, including those presently being processed and/or reviewed in accordance with Executive Order No. 109-A dated September 18, 2003, shall hereafter be processed and/or reviewed in accordance with this Executive Order.
output: The rules of Executive Order No. 423 must be followed.

instruction: What is the key difference in approval authority for contracts over P500M versus those under P500M, when using alternative procurement methods?
input: For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Of At Least Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500 Million). – Where the Head of the Procuring Entity has made a determination that a Government contract, including Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, involving an amount of at least Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500 Million) falls under any of the exceptions from public bidding described in Section 3 hereof, the Head of the Procuring Entity shall, before proceeding with the alternative methods of procurement provided by law and applicable rules and regulations, obtain the following requirements: i. An opinion from the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) that said Government contract falls within the exceptions from public bidding; and ii. Approval from the Director-General of NEDA to proceed with a specific alternative method of procurement under the exceptional cases provided by law and applicable rules and regulations. ... For Government Contracts Involving An Amount Below Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500 Million). – Except for Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, the Heads of the Procuring Entities shall likewise have full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into Government contracts of their respective agencies, entered into through alternative methods of procurement allowed by law.
output: For contracts over P500M, the Head of the Procuring Entity needs an opinion from GPPB and NEDA approval to proceed with an alternative method. For contracts under P500M, this is not required and they have full authority, except for those requiring Presidential action.

instruction: What is the responsibility of the GPPB regarding ODA-funded contracts?
input: The GPPB may issue guidelines for Government Contracts financed with ODA funds with the objective of promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions, and, where applicable, complying with the requirements of an open and competitive public bidding, consistent with Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 4, Republic Act No. 9184).
output: The GPPB may issue guidelines to promote transparency, competitiveness, and accountability, and ensure compliance with open and competitive bidding requirements for ODA-funded contracts.

instruction: What specific document is amended by Executive Order No. 423 regarding joint venture agreements?
input: Memorandum Order No. 266 dated November 28, 1980 insofar as it relates to joint venture agreements with private entities...are hereby amended accordingly.
output: Memorandum Order No. 266 dated November 28, 1980 is amended regarding joint venture agreements.

instruction: What is the role of the Department of Finance regarding transactions of government financial institutions?
input: Transactions of government financial institutions in the ordinary course of business shall not be covered by the provisions of this Executive Order. Such transactions shall instead be subject to applicable provisions of law and to guidelines, rules and regulations issued by the Department of Finance.
output: The Department of Finance issues guidelines, rules, and regulations for such transactions, as they are not covered by this Executive Order.

instruction: What does it mean for a contract to be 'not binding on the Government'?
input: All Government contracts entered into in violation of the provisions of law, rules and regulations, and of this Executive Order shall be considered contracts entered into without authority and are thus invalid and not binding on the Government.
output: It means the government is not legally obligated to honor or fulfill the terms of the contract.

instruction: What is the purpose of the policy of 'open and competitive public bidding'?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184, otherwise known as “the Government Procurement Reform Act”, which was enacted into law on January 10, 2003, likewise declared it the policy of the State to promote the ideals of good governance, with a view to transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability and public monitoring in the procurement processes of Government Contracts;
output: It is to promote the ideals of good governance, which includes transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability, and public monitoring.

instruction: What law governs contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services?
input: Contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 4, Republic Act. No. 9184).
output: They are governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: What is the role of the NEDA Director-General in the approval process for high-value alternative procurement contracts?
input: ii. Approval from the Director-General of NEDA to proceed with a specific alternative method of procurement under the exceptional cases provided by law and applicable rules and regulations.
output: The NEDA Director-General's approval is required to proceed with a specific alternative method for contracts of at least P500M.

instruction: What is a 'Procuring Entity' as defined by the document?
input: As defined under Section 5(j) of Republic Act No. 9184, a Head of the Procuring Entity refers to (i) the head of the agency or his duly authorized official, for national government agencies; or (ii) the governing board or its duly authorized official, for government-owned and/or controlled corporations, among others.
output: While the document defines the 'Head of the Procuring Entity,' it implies that a 'Procuring Entity' is the government agency, corporation, or unit undertaking the procurement, such as a national government agency or a government-owned and/or controlled corporation.

instruction: How are government contracts requiring Presidential action distinguished from others in the approval process?
input: All Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: They are distinguished by the requirement that they cannot be signed until the NEDA Board, chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved them.

instruction: When is an opinion from the GPPB required for a government contract?
input: An opinion from the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) that said Government contract falls within the exceptions from public bidding
output: It is required for contracts of at least P500M that fall under exceptions from public bidding.

instruction: If a government officer enters into a contract that violates this Executive Order, what is the status of the contract?
input: All Government contracts entered into in violation of the provisions of law, rules and regulations, and of this Executive Order shall be considered contracts entered into without authority and are thus invalid and not binding on the Government.
output: The contract is considered invalid and not binding on the government because it was entered into without authority.

instruction: What specific document is amended by EO 423 regarding the lease of real estate?
input: Department of Public Works and Highways Circular No. 125, series of 1993, insofar as it relates to the lease of real estate, are hereby amended accordingly.
output: Department of Public Works and Highways Circular No. 125, series of 1993, is amended regarding the lease of real estate.

instruction: What is the purpose of requiring a detailed summary of laws and rules to be submitted with a high-value contract to NEDA?
input: Government contracts submitted hereunder shall be accompanied by a complete execution copy of the contract, related agreements, annexes, other approvals and permits, including a detailed summary of the pertinent laws, rules and regulations governing the processing and award of the contract, and accompanied by the requirements of Section 4(a) hereof where alternative methods of procurement were resorted to.
output: The purpose is to provide context and demonstrate compliance with pertinent laws, rules, and regulations during the NEDA's review and evaluation.

instruction: What is the timeframe for NEDA's review and recommendation of a contract requiring Presidential action?
input: Within thirty (30) days from its receipt of the Government contract with complete documentation, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, NEDA shall submit, its recommendation to the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, for appropriate action.
output: NEDA must submit its recommendation within thirty days of receiving the complete documentation.

instruction: If a Head of a Procuring Entity delegates authority to approve contracts, what is the nature of the delegation?
input: The Heads of the Procuring Entities may delegate in writing this full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into Government contracts awarded through public bidding, as circumstances may warrant (i.e., decentralization of procurement in a Government Agency), subject to such limitations imposed by the Head of the Procuring Entity concerned (Section 5(j), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: The delegation must be in writing and is subject to any limitations imposed by the Head of the Procuring Entity.

instruction: What is the role of the NEDA in joint venture agreements?
input: The NEDA, in consultation with the GPPB, shall issue guidelines regarding joint venture agreements with private entities with the objective of promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions, and, where applicable, complying with the requirements of an open and competitive public bidding.
output: NEDA, in consultation with GPPB, is responsible for issuing guidelines to promote transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in joint venture agreements.

instruction: What is the effect of EO 423 on all other presidential directives and issuances inconsistent with it?
input: All other presidential directives, issuances, orders, rules and regulations or parts thereof inconsistent with this Executive Order are likewise hereby repealed or modified accordingly.
output: All other inconsistent presidential directives, issuances, orders, rules, and regulations are repealed or modified.

instruction: What two conditions must be certified under oath by a Department Secretary and Head of Procuring Entity after NEDA favorably acts on a contract requiring Presidential action?
input: Provided, that the Department Secretary and Head of Procuring Entity shall certify under oath that: (1) such contract complies with the Constitution and all existing laws, rules and regulations and that (2) such contract is not grossly disadvantageous to the government.
output: They must certify that the contract complies with the Constitution and laws and is not grossly disadvantageous to the government.

instruction: Who has the authority to sign all government contracts?
input: All Government contracts shall require the approval and signature of the respective Heads of the Procuring Entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, as required by law, applicable rules and regulations, and by this Executive Order, before said Government contracts shall be considered approved in accordance with law and binding on the government, except as may be otherwise provided in Republic Act No. 9184.
output: The respective Heads of the Procuring Entities or their duly authorized officials have the authority to sign.

instruction: What are the rules regarding contracts for the lease of goods and real estate?
input: Contracts for the lease of goods and real estate shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 5[n], Republic Act No. 9184).
output: They are governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: Under what specific law are contracts for the acquisition of right-of-way for national government projects governed?
input: Contracts for the acquisition of real property needed as right-of-way, site or location for national government infrastructure projects shall be governed by Republic Act No. 8974 (Section 5[n]), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Republic Act No. 8974 governs these contracts.

instruction: What is the role of the GPPB in high-value alternative procurements?
input: An opinion from the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) that said Government contract falls within the exceptions from public bidding;
output: The GPPB provides an opinion on whether a high-value contract (at least P500M) falls within the exceptions for public bidding.

instruction: What is the purpose of the 'Government Procurement Reform Act'?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184, otherwise known as “the Government Procurement Reform Act”, which was enacted into law on January 10, 2003, likewise declared it the policy of the State to promote the ideals of good governance, with a view to transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability and public monitoring in the procurement processes of Government Contracts;
output: Its purpose is to promote good governance through transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability, and public monitoring in government procurement.

instruction: What is the main commitment of the Arroyo Administration as mentioned in the document?
input: WHEREAS, the Arroyo Administration is committed to speedy and efficient delivery of quality services to the Filipino people;
output: The administration is committed to the speedy and efficient delivery of quality services to the Filipino people.

instruction: What is the policy regarding the procurement process to ensure efficiency?
input: WHEREAS, the procurement process must be simplified in order that all branches, departments, agencies, subdivisions, and instrumentalities of the government, including government owned and controlled corporations, and local government units be able to secure the goods and services when needed;
output: The procurement process must be simplified to ensure all government entities can secure needed goods and services when needed.

instruction: What is the significance of the `Provided, that` clause regarding the Head of the Procuring Entity's authority to approve contracts?
input: Provided, that the Head of the Procuring Entity certifies under oath that the contract has been entered into in faithful compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.
output: It is a legal condition or a prerequisite; the authority to approve is contingent upon the Head of the Procuring Entity's certification under oath that the contract is in faithful compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.

instruction: Under EO 423, what is the role of NEDA in the approval process for government contracts?
output: NEDA reviews, evaluates, and submits recommendations for government contracts that legally require Presidential action, and receives copies of contracts over P300 million for repository purposes.

instruction: How does EO 423 affect the review of government contracts of local government units?
input: Procurement contracts of local government units, regardless of the source of funds, shall be subject to the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
output: It reinforces that their procurement contracts are subject to RA 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

input: Splitting of Government contracts means the division or breaking up of Government contracts into smaller quantities and amounts, or dividing contract implementation into artificial phases or sub-contracts for the purpose of evading or circumventing the requirements of law and this Executive Order, especially the necessity of public bidding and the requirements for exceptions therefrom in accordance with Section 4(a) hereof.
output: They should check if the contract was broken into smaller quantities or artificial phases to avoid public bidding or other legal requirements.

instruction: What is the purpose of the policy on delegation of authority to Heads of Procuring Entities?
input: The Heads of the Procuring Entities may delegate in writing this full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into Government contracts awarded through public bidding, as circumstances may warrant (i.e., decentralization of procurement in a Government Agency), subject to such limitations imposed by the Head of the Procuring Entity concerned (Section 5(j), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: The purpose is to allow for decentralization of procurement within a Government Agency.

instruction: What law is amended by EO 423 regarding joint venture agreements with private entities?
input: Memorandum Order No. 266 dated November 28, 1980 insofar as it relates to joint venture agreements with private entities... are hereby amended accordingly.
output: Memorandum Order No. 266 dated November 28, 1980 is amended regarding joint venture agreements.

instruction: What is the key principle of the State's policy under RA 9184?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184, otherwise known as “the Government Procurement Reform Act”, which was enacted into law on January 10, 2003, likewise declared it the policy of the State to promote the ideals of good governance, with a view to transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability and public monitoring in the procurement processes of Government Contracts;
output: The key principle is the promotion of good governance, leading to transparency, competitiveness, streamlining, accountability, and public monitoring.

instruction: What types of contracts are governed by RA 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations?
input: Contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 4, Republic Act. No. 9184). Contracts for the lease of goods and real estate shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 5[n], Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services, as well as the lease of goods and real estate, are governed by RA 9184.

instruction: How is a government contract considered approved and binding on the government?
input: All Government contracts shall require the approval and signature of the respective Heads of the Procuring Entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, as required by law, applicable rules and regulations, and by this Executive Order, before said Government contracts shall be considered approved in accordance with law and binding on the government, except as may be otherwise provided in Republic Act No. 9184.
output: A contract is considered approved and binding after it has the approval and signature of the respective Heads of the Procuring Entities or their duly authorized officials, as required by law and this Executive Order.

instruction: What is the primary objective of the guidelines issued by NEDA and GPPB for joint venture agreements?
input: The NEDA, in consultation with the GPPB, shall issue guidelines regarding joint venture agreements with private entities with the objective of promoting transparency, competitiveness, and accountability in government transactions, and, where applicable, complying with the requirements of an open and competitive public bidding.
output: The primary objective is to promote transparency, competitiveness, and accountability, while also ensuring compliance with the requirements of open and competitive public bidding.

instruction: What must the NEDA Board do before a contract requiring Presidential action can be signed?
input: All Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: The NEDA Board must have favorably acted upon and/or approved the contract.

instruction: What is the deadline for submitting a complete copy of a contract of at least P300M to NEDA?
input: a complete copy of all Government contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the date of signing and/or approval thereof
output: It must be submitted within seven (7) days from the date of signing and/or approval.

instruction: If a government agency needs to procure goods, which law should their procurement officer follow?
input: Contracts for the procurement of infrastructure projects, goods, and consulting services shall be governed by Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 4, Republic Act. No. 9184).
output: The procurement officer should follow Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: What is the purpose of streamlining the procurement process as stated in the document?
input: WHEREAS, the procurement process must be simplified in order that all branches, departments, agencies, subdivisions, and instrumentalities of the government, including government owned and controlled corporations, and local government units be able to secure the goods and services when needed;
output: The purpose is to allow all government entities to secure goods and services when needed in a speedy and efficient manner.

instruction: What is the role of the Department Secretary in the approval process for contracts requiring Presidential action?
input: Should the NEDA favorably act on the contract, the Department Secretary and Head of the Procuring Entity is hereby given full powers and authority to approve, sign, execute and deliver any deed or document necessary and proper for the execution and implementation of such contract and subsequent amendments or supplements thereto.
output: The Department Secretary, along with the Head of the Procuring Entity, is given full power to approve and sign the contract after the NEDA Board has acted favorably.

instruction: What types of contracts are excluded from the provisions of Executive Order No. 423?
input: Transactions of government financial institutions in the ordinary course of business shall not be covered by the provisions of this Executive Order.
output: Transactions of government financial institutions in the ordinary course of business are not covered.

instruction: What is the significance of the `under oath` requirement for the Head of the Procuring Entity?
input: Provided, that the Head of the Procuring Entity certifies under oath that the contract has been entered into in faithful compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.
output: It adds a level of legal responsibility and accountability, making the certification a sworn statement of faithful compliance.

instruction: What is the policy on delegation of authority for contracts over P500M entered into through alternative methods?
input: Except for Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, the Heads of the Procuring Entities, after obtaining the foregoing requirements, shall have full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into said Government contracts of their respective agencies, entered into through alternative methods of procurement allowed by law.
output: The document doesn't explicitly mention delegation for this specific case, but states that the Heads of Procuring Entities have full authority after fulfilling the requirements from GPPB and NEDA.

instruction: If a government agency needs to acquire a site for a national infrastructure project, which law is applicable?
input: Contracts for the acquisition of real property needed as right-of-way, site or location for national government infrastructure projects shall be governed by Republic Act No. 8974 (Section 5[n]), Republic Act No. 9184).
output: Republic Act No. 8974 is applicable for this type of contract.

instruction: What does 'prospective application' mean in the context of this Executive Order?
input: All Government contracts, including those presently being processed and/or reviewed in accordance with Executive Order No. 109-A dated September 18, 2003, shall hereafter be processed and/or reviewed in accordance with this Executive Order.
output: It means that the Executive Order applies to all contracts from the date of its effectivity, including those that were already being processed under the old rules.

instruction: What is the policy for amending or supplementing a contract that requires Presidential approval?
input: All Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: Any subsequent amendments or supplements must also be favorably acted upon and/or approved by the NEDA Board before they can be signed.

instruction: What is the primary responsibility of a Head of a Procuring Entity regarding contract approval?
input: The Heads of the Procuring Entities or their respective duly authorized officials, as the case may be, shall be responsible and accountable for ensuring that all Government contracts they approve and/or enter into are in accordance with existing laws, rules and regulations and are consistent with the spending and development priorities of Government.
output: They are responsible and accountable for ensuring that all contracts they approve are in accordance with existing laws and regulations and are consistent with government spending priorities.

instruction: What are the requirements to be submitted along with a contract of at least P300 million to NEDA?
input: a complete copy of all Government contracts involving an amount of at least Three Hundred Million Pesos (P300 Million) shall be submitted to NEDA, through its Director-General, within seven (7) days from the date of signing and/or approval thereof, accompanied with a complete copy of its related agreements, annexes, other approvals and permits, and a detailed summary of the pertinent laws, rules and regulations governing the processing and award of the contract.
output: A complete copy of the contract, its related agreements, annexes, other approvals and permits, and a detailed summary of governing laws and rules must be submitted.

instruction: How is the NEDA Board involved in the approval process for government contracts?
input: All Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, and any subsequent amendments or supplements thereto, shall not be signed until after the NEDA Board, which is chaired by the President, has favorably acted upon and/or approved the same.
output: The NEDA Board must favorably act upon or approve government contracts that are legally required to be acted upon or approved by the President.

instruction: How does the document define 'splitting of Government contracts'?
input: Splitting of Government contracts means the division or breaking up of Government contracts into smaller quantities and amounts, or dividing contract implementation into artificial phases or sub-contracts for the purpose of evading or circumventing the requirements of law and this Executive Order, especially the necessity of public bidding and the requirements for exceptions therefrom in accordance with Section 4(a) hereof.
output: It is defined as dividing contracts into smaller quantities or amounts, or creating artificial phases or sub-contracts, to evade public bidding and other legal requirements.

instruction: How are government contracts financed by Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds governed?
input: Government Contracts financed wholly or partly with Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds shall be governed by Republic Act No. 4860, as amended, Republic Act No. 8182, as amended by Republic Act No. 8555, and Republic Act No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (Section 4, Republic Act No. 9184).
output: They are governed by RA 4860, RA 8182, and RA 9184 and their Implementing Rules and Regulations.

instruction: If a government financial institution's transaction is not covered by this Executive Order, what set of rules must be followed?
input: Such transactions shall instead be subject to applicable provisions of law and to guidelines, rules and regulations issued by the Department of Finance.
output: They must follow applicable provisions of law and guidelines, rules, and regulations issued by the Department of Finance.

instruction: What is the general policy of the Arroyo Administration regarding government contracts?
input: It is the policy of this Administration that all Government contracts of Government Agencies shall be awarded through open and competitive public bidding, save in exceptional cases provided by law and applicable rules and regulations, as described in Section 3 of this Executive Order.
output: The policy is to award all government contracts through open and competitive public bidding, with exceptions only as provided by law.

instruction: What is the purpose of repealing Executive Order No. 109-A?
input: REPEALING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 109-A DATED SEPTEMBER 18, 2003 PRESCRIBING THE RULES AND PROCEDURES ON THE REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF ALL GOVERNMENT CONTRACTS TO CONFORM WITH REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT REFORM ACT”
output: The purpose is to replace it with a new set of rules and procedures that conform with Republic Act No. 9184.

instruction: What is the timeline for NEDA to notify the Procuring Entity of the NEDA Board's action?
input: Within seven (7) days from the date of the NEDA Board’s action, NEDA, through its Director-General, shall formally notify the Head of the Procuring Entity concerned or his/its duly authorized official, as the case may be, of the action of the NEDA Board, including any comments thereon.
output: NEDA must formally notify the Procuring Entity within seven days from the date of the NEDA Board's action.

instruction: If a government contract needs Presidential action, who has the final authority to sign after NEDA's favorable action?
input: Should the NEDA favorably act on the contract, the Department Secretary and Head of the Procuring Entity is hereby given full powers and authority to approve, sign, execute and deliver any deed or document necessary and proper for the execution and implementation of such contract and subsequent amendments or supplements thereto.
output: The Department Secretary and the Head of the Procuring Entity have the full powers and authority to approve and sign the contract.

instruction: What types of contracts are governed by RA 6957, as amended by RA 7718?
input: Contracts undertaken through Build-Operate and Transfer (BOT) schemes and other variations shall be governed by Republic Act No. 6957, as amended by Republic Act No. 7718, and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
output: Build-Operate and Transfer (BOT) schemes and other variations are governed by this law.

instruction: What is the official title of Memorandum Order No. 171, s. 2005?
output: Memorandum Order No. 171 is titled 'APPROVING AMENDMENT TO SECTION 23.11.2 NO. 3 OF THE IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATIONS PART A (IRR-A) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT REFORM ACT'.

instruction: What is the primary purpose of Memorandum Order No. 171?
input: WHEREAS, there is a need to amend Section 23.11.2 No. 3 of IRR-A of R.A. No. 9184, to provide for Allowable Ranges of Contract Costs (ARCC) in relation to a prospective bidder’s largest single completed contract;
output: The purpose of the memorandum is to approve an amendment to Section 23.11.2 No. 3 of the IRR-A of R.A. No. 9184 to include the Allowable Ranges of Contract Costs (ARCC).

instruction: What specific law does Memorandum Order No. 171 amend the implementing rules for?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act (RA) No. 9184 otherwise known as the Government Procurement Reform Act was signed into law on January 10, 2003;
output: It amends the Implementing Rules and Regulations Part A (IRR-A) of Republic Act No. 9184, also known as the Government Procurement Reform Act.

instruction: Who signed Memorandum Order No. 171, s. 2005?
input: NOW, THEREFORE, I, GLORIA MACAPAGAL-ARROYO, President of the Republic of the Philippines, by virtue of the powers vested in me by law, hereby approve the amendment...
output: President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo signed Memorandum Order No. 171.

instruction: When was the Government Procurement Reform Act (RA 9184) signed into law?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act (RA) No. 9184 otherwise known as the Government Procurement Reform Act was signed into law on January 10, 2003;
output: Republic Act No. 9184 was signed into law on January 10, 2003.

instruction: When was Memorandum Order No. 171 signed?
input: Signed on May 19, 2005
output: It was signed on May 19, 2005.

instruction: According to the amendment, what is the required value of a prospective bidder's largest single completed contract?
input: The value of the prospective bidder’s largest single completed contract... must be at least fifty percent (50%) of the approved budget for the contract to be bid:
output: A prospective bidder's largest single completed contract must be at least 50% of the approved budget for the contract being bid.

instruction: How should a bidder adjust the value of their largest single completed contract to current prices?
input: The value of the prospective bidder’s largest single completed contract, adjusted to current prices using the National Statistics Office consumer price indices available at the G-EPS website...
output: The contract value should be adjusted to current prices using the National Statistics Office consumer price indices found on the G-EPS website.

instruction: For a contractor under the Small A or Small B categories, what is the alternative requirement to the 50% rule?
input: That in case of a contractor under Small A and Small B categories without similar experience on the contract to be bid, he may be allowed to bid if the cost of such contract is more than fifty percent (50%) of the Allowable Ranges Contract Cost (ARCC) of his registration.
output: A contractor under Small A or Small B without similar experience can bid if the contract cost is more than 50% of the Allowable Ranges Contract Cost (ARCC) of their registration.

instruction: What is the basis for the classification of contractors vis-à-vis the Allowable Ranges Contract Cost (ARCC)?
input: For this purpose, the classification of contractors vis-à-vis the ARCC shall be based on the Guidelines as prescribed by the Philippine Contractors Accreditation Board (PCAB).
output: The classification is based on the guidelines prescribed by the Philippine Contractors Accreditation Board (PCAB).

instruction: Who formulated and proposed the amendment to the IRR-A of R.A. 9184?
input: WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 75, Article XXV of R.A. No. 9184, the GPPB-Technical Support Office formulated and proposed the foregoing amendment which was favorably endorsed by GPPB per its Resolution No. 013-2004 dated August 20, 2004.
output: The GPPB-Technical Support Office formulated and proposed the amendment, which was then endorsed by the GPPB.

instruction: When did the GPPB endorse the proposed amendment?
input: WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 75, Article XXV of R.A. No. 9184, the GPPB-Technical Support Office formulated and proposed the foregoing amendment which was favorably endorsed by GPPB per its Resolution No. 013-2004 dated August 20, 2004.

instruction: Who jointly formulated the original IRR-A of R.A. No. 9184?
input: WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 75 of R.A. No. 9184, the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB), jointly with the members of the Joint Congressional Oversight Committee formulated the Implementing Rules and Regulations Part A (IRR-A) of R.A. 9184 which was approved by the President of the Philippines on July 11, 2003;
output: The Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) and the members of the Joint Congressional Oversight Committee jointly formulated the original IRR-A.

instruction: What was the Supreme Court's decision in the Macalintal vs. Comelec case, G.R. No. 157013?
input: WHEREAS, the joint participation of the Congressional Oversight Committee in the formulation of implementing rules and regulations has recently been declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in Macalintal vs. Comelec, G.R. No. 157013, July 2003;
output: The Supreme Court declared the joint participation of the Congressional Oversight Committee in formulating implementing rules and regulations as unconstitutional.

instruction: When was the original IRR-A of R.A. 9184 approved by the President?
input: WHEREAS, the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB), jointly with the members of the Joint Congressional Oversight Committee formulated the Implementing Rules and Regulations Part A (IRR-A) of R.A. 9184 which was approved by the President of the Philippines on July 11, 2003;
output: The IRR-A was approved by the President of the Philippines on July 11, 2003.

input: All other provisions of the IRR-A of R.A. 9184 shall remain unchanged.

instruction: What is a key difference in bidding requirements for Small A and B contractors compared to other bidders?

instruction: What is the specific change to Section 23.11.2 no. 3 of the IRR-A?
input: “3. The value of the prospective bidder’s largest single completed contract, adjusted to current prices using the National Statistics Office consumer price indices available at the G-EPS website, and similar to the contract to be bid, must be at least fifty percent (50%) of the approved budget for the contract to be bid: Provided, however, That in case of a contractor under Small A and Small B categories without similar experience on the contract to be bid, he may be allowed to bid if the cost of such contract is more than fifty percent (50%) of the Allowable Ranges Contract Cost (ARCC) of his registration. For this purpose, the classification of contractors vis-à-vis the ARCC shall be based on the Guidelines as prescribed by the Philippine Contractors Accreditation Board (PCAB).”
output: The section now specifies the value of a bidder's largest single completed contract must be at least 50% of the approved budget, introduces a price adjustment method, and provides an alternative requirement for Small A and Small B contractors based on ARCC.

output: A bidder may submit an offer with superior specifications or better terms at no extra cost to the government, but they will not receive any bonus, credit, or premium in the bid evaluation.

instruction: What is the penalty for a procuring entity that fails to enter into a contract with a winning bidder within the specified timeframe?
input: The Procuring Entity shall enter into contract with the winning bidder within the same ten (10) day period provided that all the documentary requirements are complied with.
output: The document does not specify a penalty, but it states that the procuring entity must enter into a contract with the winning bidder within ten calendar days, provided all documentary requirements are met.

instruction: How is a consultant's financial proposal handled in a Quality-Cost Based Evaluation?
input: For this purpose, it is hereby clarified that, in case of a Quality-Cost Based Evaluation, as distinguished from a Quality-Based Evaluation, the financial proposals of the consultants who meet the minimum technical rating shall be opened on a separate date and time set by the BAC, and not during negotiations.
output: The financial proposals of consultants who pass the minimum technical rating are opened on a separate date and time set by the BAC, and not during negotiation sessions.

instruction: What is the responsibility of a winning bidder regarding contract signing and documentary requirements?
input: The winning bidder or its duly authorized representative shall comply with all the remaining documentary requirements, if any, prior to formally entering into contract with the procuring entity concerned within ten (10) calendar days from receipt by the winning bidder of the Notice of Award.
output: Within ten calendar days of receiving the Notice of Award, the winning bidder must comply with all remaining documentary requirements before formally signing the contract.

instruction: How is the performance security affected by a cumulative increase in an infrastructure project's contract value?
input: For the procurement of infrastructure projects, the winning bidder shall post an additional performance security following the schedule above to cover any cumulative increase of more than ten percent (10%) over the original value of the contract: as a result of amendments to order or change orders, extra work orders and supplemental agreements, as the case may be.
output: If the cumulative value of the contract for an infrastructure project increases by more than ten percent due to amendments, change orders, or other agreements, the winning bidder must post an additional performance security.

instruction: When should negotiations with the first-in-rank consultant be completed?
input: Except for meritorious reasons, negotiations with any one consultant shall be completed within fourteen (14) calendar days.
output: Unless there are meritorious reasons, negotiations with a consultant must be completed within 14 calendar days.

instruction: What is the minimum number of suppliers or contractors to be invited for bidding under alternative methods of procurement?
input: For items (a) and (b) of Section 53, in the case of goods and infrastructure projects, the procuring entity shall draw up a list of at least three (3) suppliers or contractors which will be invited to submit bids.
output: The procuring entity must create a list of at least three suppliers or contractors to invite for bidding when using alternative methods for goods and infrastructure projects.

instruction: What is the primary content of the first envelope for the procurement of consulting services?
input: For the procurement of consulting services: ... 8. A sworn statement attesting compliance to the responsibilities of a Prospective or Eligible Bidder as provided in Section 17.7 of the IRR-A; 9. A sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act in relation to other provisions of RA 3019; and 10. Other information and/or documents specified in the bidding documents.
output: The first envelope for consulting services must include a sworn statement of compliance with Section 17.7 of the IRR-A, a sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act, and other documents specified in the bidding documents.

instruction: What is the rule on confidentiality during the bid evaluation process?
input: Reiterate and emphasize the importance of confidentiality during the bid evaluation process, and the applicable sanctions and penalties, as well as agree on measures to ensure compliance with the foregoing.
output: The pre-procurement conference must emphasize the importance of confidentiality during bid evaluation, including applicable sanctions and penalties, and establish measures to ensure compliance.

instruction: How should the warranty for goods, supplies, and materials be stated?
input: The warranty shall be stated in Philippine Pesos, shall remain effective during the applicable warranty period stated in Section 62.2 of the IRR-A and shall be returned only after the lapse of the said warranty period. The warranty shall be full for the first year, and renewable every year thereafter, subject to depreciation after the first year, on a straight line basis.
output: The warranty should be stated in Philippine Pesos, remain effective for the applicable period, and be returned only after it lapses. It is full for the first year and renewable annually thereafter, subject to straight-line depreciation after the first year.

instruction: What is required of each member of a joint venture for eligibility?
input: Each member of the joint venture shall submit the required eligibility documents;
output: Every member of a joint venture must submit their own required eligibility documents.

instruction: What specific documents are required in the first envelope for infrastructure projects?

A sworn statement attesting compliance to the responsibilities of a Prospective or Eligible Bidder as provided in section 17.7 of the IRR-A; 15. A sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act in ration to other provisions of R.A. 3019; and 16. instruction: Can a supplier start work under an amendment to order without approval from the head of the procuring entity?
input: Under no circumstances shall a supplier proceed to commence work under any amendment to order unless the same has been approved by the head of the procuring entity concerned or his duly authorized representative.
output: No, a supplier cannot start work under an amendment to order unless it has been approved by the head of the procuring entity or their authorized representative.

instruction: What are the exceptions to the rule on commencing work under an amendment to order?
input: As an exception to the rule the Regional Director/Head concerned may authorize the immediate start of work under any amendment to order in the event of emergencies to avoid detriment to public service, or damage to life and/or property or when time is of the essence: Provided, however, That the same is valid only on items up to the point where the cumulative increase in the contract cost which has not yet been duly fully approved by the head of the procuring entity concerned or his duly authorized representative does not exceed five percent (5%) of the original contract cost
output: In emergencies to prevent public detriment, damage, or when time is of the essence, a Regional Director or Head may authorize immediate work. This exception is valid only if the cumulative increase in contract cost does not exceed five percent of the original cost.

instruction: What is the limit for a cumulative increase in contract cost for which a Regional Director can authorize immediate work on an amendment to order?
input: Provided, however, That the same is valid only on items up to the point where the cumulative increase in the contract cost which has not yet been duly fully approved by the head of the procuring entity concerned or his duly authorized representative does not exceed five percent (5%) of the original contract cost:
output: A Regional Director can authorize immediate work for an amendment to order as long as the cumulative cost increase does not exceed five percent of the original contract cost.

instruction: What is the process for an amendment to order involving a cumulative amount exceeding five percent of the original contract price?
input: For an amendment to order involving a cumulative amount exceeding five percent (5%) of the original contact price, no work thereon shall be commenced unless the same has been approved by the head of procuring entity concerned or his duly authorized representative: Provided, That, the said cumulative amount does not exceed ten percent (10%) of the original contract price.
output: For an amendment to order that exceeds five percent of the original contract price, no work can start unless it is approved by the head of the procuring entity, and the cumulative amount cannot exceed ten percent of the original contract price.

instruction: What happens if a joint venture wants to participate in the bidding for consulting services?
input: Class “B” Documents – a) Valid joint venture agreement, in case of a joint venture. Each member of the joint venture shall submit the required eligibility documents; and...
output: The joint venture must submit a valid joint venture agreement, and each member of the joint venture must also submit all their required eligibility documents.

instruction: How is the performance security for an infrastructure project affected by approved contract time extensions?
input: The winning bidder shall cause the extension of the validity of the Performance Security to cover approved contract time extensions.
output: The winning bidder must extend the validity of their performance security to cover any approved contract time extensions.

instruction: What is the role of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) in a pre-procurement conference?
input: During this conference, the participants, led by the BAC, shall:

instruction: When is an amendment to order valid as an exception to the approval rule?
input: As an exception to the rule the Regional Director/Head concerned may authorize the immediate start of work under any amendment to order in the event of emergencies to avoid detriment to public service, or damage to life and/or property or when time is of the essence: Provided, however, That the same is valid only on items up to the point where the cumulative increase in the contract cost which has not yet been duly fully approved by the head of the procuring entity concerned or his duly authorized representative does not exceed five percent (5%) of the original contract cost:

instruction: What is the procedure for a Quality-Cost Based Evaluation for consulting services?

The methodology to be used in the evaluation of the financial proposal shall be described in the Instructions to Bidders. The BAC shall rank the consultants in descending order based on the combined numerical ratings of their technical and financial proposals and identify the Highest Rated Bid
output: The total weight of the technical and financial criteria must sum to 100%. The BAC ranks consultants based on the combined ratings of their technical and financial proposals to identify the Highest Rated Bid, and the evaluation methodology for the financial proposal is detailed in the Instructions to Bidders.
