instruction: What are the key differences between quality-based and quality-cost based evaluation procedures for consultants?
input: For the quality-based evaluation procedure, 3 two-stage procedure shall be adopted whereby each consultant shall be required to submit his technical and financial proposals simultaneously in separate sealed envelopes, and the evaluation of consultants shall be made based only on the technical proposals without consideration of the estimated cost or financial terms of the services. ... For this purpose, it is hereby clarified that, in case of a Quality-Cost Based Evaluation, as distinguished from a Quality-Based Evaluation, the financial proposals of the consultants who meet the minimum technical rating shall be opened on a separate date and time set by the BAC, and not during negotiations.
output: In a quality-based evaluation, only the technical proposals are evaluated. In a quality-cost based evaluation, the financial proposals of technically qualified consultants are opened and evaluated on a separate date and time, and the final ranking is based on a combined score.

instruction: What is the procedure for alternative methods of procurement for goods and infrastructure projects?

input: As an exception to the rule the Regional Director/Head concerned may authorize the immediate start of work under any amendment to order in the event of emergencies to avoid detriment to public service, or damage to life and/or property or when time is of the essence:

instruction: What are the key points to discuss during a pre-procurement conference?
input: During this conference, the participants, led by the BAC, shall: ... 5. Review and agree on the number of eligible bidders to be included in the shortlist, from three to seven eligible bidders, and the minimum score required, as provided for in Section 24.15.2; 6. Review and agree on whether the quality-based or quality-cost based evaluation procedure shall be adopted in the selection of consultant, as provided for in Section 33.3.1; if the quality-cost based evaluation procedure, review and agree on the weights to be allocated to the technical and financial criteria and recommend to the head of the procuring entity for approval, as provided for in section 33.5; 7. Clarify that the specifications and other terms in the bidding documents are minimum requirements and that the bidder may submit an offer which provides for superior specifications and/or better terms and conditions to the Government at no extra cost, without any bonus, credit or premium in the bid evaluation; and 8. Reiterate and emphasize the importance of confidentiality during the bid evaluation process, and the applicable sanctions and penalties, as well as agree on measures to ensure compliance with the foregoing.
output: The key points to discuss are the number of bidders to be shortlisted, the evaluation procedure for consultants, the minimum requirements of bidding documents, and the confidentiality of the bid evaluation process.

instruction: What is the legal basis for the amendments to the IRR-A of RA 9184?
input: NOW THEREFORE, I GLORIA MACAPAGAL-ARROYO, President of the Republic of the Philippines, by virtue of the powers vested in me by law, hereby approve the amendments of the Implementing Rules and Regulation – Part A (IRR-A) of Republic Act (RA) 9184 as follows:
output: The amendments were approved by the President of the Philippines, Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, by virtue of the powers vested in her by law.

instruction: How do alternative methods of procurement for goods and infrastructure projects differ from standard public bidding?
input: The procedures for the conduct of public bidding shall be observed, and the lowest calculated and responsive bid shall be considered for award. However, the minimum period for each bidding procedure may be reduced.
output: While the same public bidding procedures are followed and the lowest responsive bid is considered for award, the key difference is that the minimum period for each bidding procedure can be reduced.

instruction: What are the requirements for a bidder's sworn statement and affidavit in the first envelope for infrastructure projects?
input: A sworn statement attesting compliance to the responsibilities of a Prospective or Eligible Bidder as provided in section 17.7 of the IRR-A; A sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act in ration to other provisions of R.A. 3019;
output: The first envelope must contain a sworn statement confirming compliance with the responsibilities in Section 17.7 of the IRR-A and a sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act.

instruction: What happens after the financial proposals of technically qualified consultants are opened?
input: The BAC shall rank the consultants in descending order based on the combined numerical ratings of their technical and financial proposals and identify the Highest Rated Bid: Provided, however, That subsequent negotiations in accordance with Section 33.4.3 of this IRR-A shall still be undertaken with the first in rank consultant, except for item (e) thereof.
output: After the financial proposals are opened, the BAC ranks the consultants based on the combined technical and financial ratings to identify the Highest Rated Bid, and then negotiations are undertaken with the first-in-rank consultant.

instruction: What are the rules for an amendment to order for goods, supplies, and materials?
input: An amendment to order may be issued only in emergency cases or during fortuitous events requiring necessary adjustments within the general scope of the contract in any one or more of the following is required in order to fully meet the requirements of the project: drawings, design or specifications, if the goods to be furnished are to be specifically manufactured for the Government in accordance therewith; method of shipment or packing; or place of delivery
output: An amendment to order can only be issued in emergencies or due to fortuitous events to make necessary adjustments to a contract's scope, specifically for drawings, design, specifications, shipment method, packing, or place of delivery.

instruction: What is the penalty for a procuring entity that fails to enter into a contract with the winning bidder within the specified timeframe?
input: The Procuring Entity shall enter into contract with the winning bidder within the same ten (10) day period provided that all the documentary requirements are complied with.
output: The document states a requirement for the procuring entity to enter into a contract within 10 days, but it does not specify any penalties for non-compliance.

instruction: As a bidder, what is my responsibility regarding the submission of bids?
input: Eligibility requirements and bids submitted after the deadline shall not be accepted by the BAC.
output: As a bidder, your responsibility is to ensure that your eligibility requirements and bids are submitted to the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) before the specified deadline.

instruction: How is the warranty for goods returned to the supplier?
input: The warranty shall be stated in Philippine Pesos, shall remain effective during the applicable warranty period stated in Section 62.2 of the IRR-A and shall be returned only after the lapse of the said warranty period.
output: The warranty is returned to the supplier only after the entire applicable warranty period, as stated in Section 62.2 of the IRR-A, has lapsed.

instruction: What is the minimum number of eligible bidders to be included in a shortlist for consulting services?
input: Review and agree on the number of eligible bidders to be included in the shortlist, from three to seven eligible bidders, and the minimum score required, as provided for in Section 24.15.2;
output: The minimum number of eligible bidders for a shortlist is three.

instruction: What is the purpose of the sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision for consulting services?
input: A sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act in relation to other provisions of RA 3019;
output: The purpose is for a bidder for consulting services to formally attest that they are in compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act and related provisions of RA 3019.

instruction: What is the legal effect of the Memorandum Order on other provisions of the IRR-A of RA 9184?
input: All other provisions of the IRR-A of RA 9184 shall remain unchanged.
output: All other provisions of the IRR-A of RA 9184 that were not specifically amended by the memorandum order remain unchanged and in effect.

instruction: Can a supplier start work on an amendment to order for goods without official approval?
input: Under no circumstances shall a supplier proceed to commence work under any amendment to order unless the same has been approved by the head of the procuring entity concerned or his duly authorized representative.
output: No, a supplier can under no circumstances start work on an amendment to order without prior approval from the head of the procuring entity or their authorized representative.

instruction: What happens if a bidder's offer for an infrastructure project includes superior terms?
input: Clarify that the specifications and other terms in the bidding documents are minimum requirements and that the bidder may submit an offer which provides for superior specifications and/or better terms and conditions to the Government at no extra cost, without any bonus, credit or premium in the bid evaluation;
output: If a bidder offers superior terms at no extra cost, they will not receive any bonus, credit, or premium during the bid evaluation, as the bidding documents only set minimum requirements.

instruction: What is the first step for a winning bidder after receiving a Notice of Award?
input: The winning bidder or its duly authorized representative shall comply with all the remaining documentary requirements, if any, prior to formally entering into contract with the procuring entity concerned within ten (10) calendar days from receipt by the winning bidder of the Notice of Award.
output: The first step is for the winning bidder or their representative to comply with any remaining documentary requirements within ten calendar days of receiving the Notice of Award.

instruction: What are the specific conditions under which an amendment to order can be issued?
input: An amendment to order may be issued only in emergency cases or during fortuitous events requiring necessary adjustments within the general scope of the contract in any one or more of the following is required in order to fully meet the requirements of the project: a) drawings, design or specifications... b) method of shipment or packing; or c) place of delivery
output: An amendment to order can be issued only in emergency cases or fortuitous events that require adjustments to drawings, design, specifications, shipment or packing method, or place of delivery.

instruction: What is the purpose of the additional performance security for infrastructure projects?
input: the winning bidder shall post an additional performance security following the schedule above to cover any cumulative increase of more than ten percent (10%) over the original value of the contract: as a result of amendments to order or change orders, extra work orders and supplemental agreements, as the case may be.
output: The purpose is to provide security coverage for any cumulative increase of more than ten percent over the original contract value resulting from amendments, change orders, or other agreements.

instruction: How does the Supreme Court decision on the Congressional Oversight Committee affect the IRR-A?
input: WHEREAS, the joint participation of the Congressional Oversight Committee in the formulation of implementing rules and regulations has recently been declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in Macalintal vs. Comelec, G.R. No. 157013, July 2003;
output: The Supreme Court's declaration that the joint participation of the Congressional Oversight Committee was unconstitutional is one of the reasons the amendments to the IRR-A of RA 9184 were approved.

instruction: When should the financial proposals of consultants be opened in a Quality-Cost Based Evaluation?
input: the financial proposals of the consultants who meet the minimum technical rating shall be opened on a separate date and time set by the BAC, and not during negotiations.
output: The financial proposals should be opened on a separate date and time determined by the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC), only for consultants who have met the minimum technical rating, and this should not happen during negotiations.

instruction: What is the role of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) in the pre-procurement conference for consultant selection?
input: if the quality-cost based evaluation procedure, review and agree on the weights to be allocated to the technical and financial criteria and recommend to the head of the procuring entity for approval, as provided for in section 33.5;
output: The BAC's role is to lead the review and agreement on the weights for the technical and financial criteria, and then recommend these weights to the head of the procuring entity for approval.

instruction: How are consultants ranked in a quality-based evaluation procedure?
input: The BAC shall rank the consultants in descending order based on the numerical ratings of their technical proposals subject to Section 33.3 of this IRR-A and identify the Highest Rated Bid: Provided, however, that the Highest Rated Bid shall pass the minimum score required.
output: The BAC ranks consultants in descending order based on the numerical ratings of their technical proposals, provided that the proposals meet the minimum score required.

instruction: What is the final step in the amendment to order process for an emergency?
input: That the corresponding amendment to order shall immediately be prepared and submitted for approval to the head of the procuring entity concerned or his duly authorized representative.
output: The final step is the immediate preparation and submission of the amendment to order for formal approval by the head of the procuring entity or their authorized representative.

instruction: What are the specific requirements for the first envelope in the procurement of goods?

A sworn statement attesting compliance to the responsibilities of a Prospective or Eligible Bidder as provided in Section 17.7 of the IRR-A; A sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act in relation to other provisions of R.A. 3019; and Other documents/materials as stated in the Instructions to Bidders.

instruction: When can a procuring entity reduce the minimum bidding period for alternative methods?

instruction: What is the rule for a winning bidder regarding contract signing and documentary requirements?

instruction: What are the rules regarding a supplier commencing work under an amendment to order that is not fully approved?
input: Provided, however, That the same is valid only on items up to the point where the cumulative increase in the contract cost which has not yet been duly fully approved by the head of the procuring entity concerned or his duly authorized representative does not exceed five percent (5%) of the original contract cost
output: A supplier can only commence work on items where the cumulative increase in contract cost has not yet been fully approved, provided that this cumulative increase does not exceed five percent of the original contract cost.

input: The BAC shall rank the consultants in descending order based on the numerical ratings of their technical proposals subject to Section 33.3 of this IRR-A and identify the Highest Rated Bid: Provided, however, that the Highest Rated Bid shall pass the minimum score required.

instruction: What is the rule for contract signing between a winning bidder and the procuring entity?

instruction: What is the process for a procuring entity when using alternative methods of procurement for goods?
input: For items (a) and (b) of Section 53, in the case of goods and infrastructure projects, the procuring entity shall draw up a list of at least three (3) suppliers or contractors which will be invited to submit bids. The procedures for the conduct of public bidding shall be observed, and the lowest calculated and responsive bid shall be considered for award.

instruction: What is the role of the Head of the Procuring Entity for contracts of at least ₱500 million that use alternative procurement methods?
input: Where the Head of the Procuring Entity has made a determination that a Government contract, including Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, involving an amount of at least Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500,000,000.00) falls under any of the exceptions from public bidding described in Section 3 hereof, the Head of the Procuring Entity shall, before proceeding with the alternative methods of procurement provided by law and applicable rules and regulations, obtain the approval of the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) that said Government proposed procurement undertaking falls within the exceptions from public bidding and that the proposed specific alternative mode of procurement is appropriate.
output: The Head of the Procuring Entity must first determine that the contract falls under a public bidding exception and then obtain approval from the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) for the alternative procurement method.

instruction: Who has the final approval authority for government contracts of at least ₱500 million entered into through alternative methods, except those requiring Presidential approval?

output: The Heads of the Procuring Entities have full authority for final approval, provided they have met the initial requirements.

input: WHEREAS, Section 4 of Executive Order 423 dated 18 September 2003 prescribes that in cases where government contracts amounting to at least P500 Million, the Head of the Procuring Entity is required to obtain an opinion and approval from the Government Procurement Policy Board and the Director-General of the National Economic and Development Authority before resorting to any of the alternative methods of procurement;...Where the Head of the Procuring Entity...obtain the approval of the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB)...
output: The process is simplified. Previously, two approvals were needed (GPPB and NEDA Director-General), but now only the GPPB's approval is required before the Head of the Procuring Entity can proceed.

instruction: What is the full name of the law being referenced in the document?
input: REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT REFORM ACT”
output: Republic Act No. 9184, which is also known as the Government Procurement Reform Act.

instruction: What is the implication of E.O. 645 for a policymaker?
input: WHEREAS, it has become necessary to amend Section 4 of Executive Order No. 423 dated 18 September 2003 to streamline and expedite procurement procedures for a more effective procurement system;
output: It implies that even existing procurement regulations may be amended to make the system more efficient and effective, especially when they conflict with a primary law like the Government Procurement Reform Act.

instruction: Who has the authority to make the final approval for contracts that do not require Presidential approval?
input: Except for Government contracts required by law to be acted upon and/or approved by the President, the Heads of the Procuring Entities, after obtaining the foregoing requirements, shall have full authority to give final approval and/or to enter into said Government contracts of their respective agencies, entered into through alternative methods of procurement allowed by law.
output: The Heads of the Procuring Entities have the full authority to give final approval.

instruction: What is the significance of the phrase 'in the year of Our Lord' in the document's conclusion?
input: Done in the City of Manila this 31st day of July in the year of Our Lord, Two Thousand and Seven.
output: It is a traditional and formal legal phrase used to denote the Christian calendar year of the document's signing.

instruction: What were the original approval requirements for government contracts worth at least ₱500 million under E.O. 423?
input: WHEREAS, Section 4 of Executive Order 423 dated 18 September 2003 prescribes that in cases where government contracts amounting to at least P500 Million, the Head of the Procuring Entity is required to obtain an opinion and approval from the Government Procurement Policy Board and the Director-General of the National Economic and Development Authority before resorting to any of the alternative methods of procurement;
output: The Head of the Procuring Entity was required to get an opinion and approval from both the GPPB and the Director-General of the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA).

instruction: Why was E.O. 645 issued?
input: WHEREAS, it has become necessary to amend Section 4 of Executive Order No. 423 dated 18 September 2003 to streamline and expedite procurement procedures for a more effective procurement system; WHEREAS, the Government Procurement Policy Board, in its Resolution No. 06-2006 dated 20 January 2006, recommends the issuance of this Executive Order;
output: It was issued to streamline and expedite procurement procedures for a more effective system, based on a recommendation from the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB).

instruction: How does E.O. 645 simplify the approval process for alternative procurement methods?
input: WHEREAS, Section 4 of Executive Order 423 dated 18 September 2003 prescribes that in cases where government contracts amounting to at least P500 Million, the Head of the Procuring Entity is required to obtain an opinion and approval from the Government Procurement Policy Board and the Director-General of the National Economic and Development Authority before resorting to any of the alternative methods of procurement;...Where the Head of the Procuring Entity...obtain the approval of the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB)...
output: It simplifies the process by eliminating the need for an opinion and approval from the Director-General of the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA), which was previously required under E.O. 423.

instruction: What is the primary purpose of Executive Order No. 662?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184 (R.A. 9184) or the Government Procurement Reform Act and its Implementing Rules and Regulations Pact A (IRR-A) recognize and adopt transparency as a governing principle in public procurement;...WHEREAS, there is a need for a body to monitor compliance to anti-graft mechanism, to deter anomalies in the awarding of public sector contracts and to prevent losses due to procurement irregularities;...ENHANCING TRANSPARENCY MEASURES UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184 AND CREATING THE PROCUREMENT TRANSPARENCY BOARD
output: The Executive Order enhances transparency measures under Republic Act No. 9184 and creates the Procurement Transparency Board to monitor compliance, deter anomalies, and prevent losses from procurement irregularities.

instruction: What government agencies are required to post procurement reports under Section 1?
input: All National Government Agencies (NGAs), Government Owned and/or Controlled Corporations (GOCCs), Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), and Local Government Units (LGUs), through their bids and awards committees are directed to post in the appropriate government website the following procurement reports as required under R.A. 9184 and its IRR-A
output: All National Government Agencies (NGAs), Government Owned and/or Controlled Corporations (GOCCs), Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), and Local Government Units (LGUs).

instruction: What specific procurement reports must be posted by government agencies on the appropriate website?
output: Agencies must post the Annual Procurement Plan, the Procurement Monitoring Report, the list of invited NGO/CSO observers, and blacklisting orders against suppliers, constructors, and consultants.

instruction: What is the threshold for public sector contracts that must be included in the GPPB database?
input: The GPPB shall cause to be maintained in the appropriate government website a database of proposed and concluded public sector contracts involving an amount of P100,000,000.00 and above.
output: The database must include proposed and concluded public sector contracts valued at P100,000,000.00 and above.

instruction: According to the Executive Order, what specific procurement information must be posted on the PhilGEPS bulletin board?
input: All NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs, Sucs, and LGUs, through its BACs, are likewise directed to post all their procurement opportunities, results thereof, and other related information in the PhilGEPS bulletin board, as required under Section 8.2.1 of the IRR-A of R.R. 9184.
output: All procurement opportunities, results, and other related information must be posted on the PhilGEPS bulletin board.

instruction: What are the potential consequences for officials who fail to comply with the posting obligations under this Order?
input: Non-compliance with the foregoing posting obligations shall render the accountable officials liable for dereliction of duty and conduct grossly prejudicial to the best interest of the service, without prejudice to other charges, whether administrative, civil or criminal, that may be filed under appropriate laws and regulations.
output: Accountable officials may be held liable for dereliction of duty and conduct grossly prejudicial to the best interest of the service, in addition to other possible administrative, civil, or criminal charges.

instruction: What is the name of the group created to enhance procurement transparency?
input: There is hereby created a PROCUREMENT TRANSPARENCY GROUP, headed by the GPPB and with the following government agencies and non-government organizations (NGOs) as members:
output: The group is named the Procurement Transparency Group.

instruction: Who heads the Procurement Transparency Group?
input: There is hereby created a PROCUREMENT TRANSPARENCY GROUP, headed by the GPPB and with the following government agencies and non-government organizations (NGOs) as members:
output: The Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) heads the group.

instruction: List the government agencies that are members of the Procurement Transparency Group.
output: The government agency members are the Presidential Anti-Graft Commission (PAGC), National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA), Department of Justice (DOJ), Department of Budget and Management (DBM), and the Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG).

instruction: Who are the non-government organization members of the Procurement Transparency Group?
output: The NGO members are the Bishops-Businessmen’s Conference for Human Development, Transparency and Accountability Network, Volunteers Against Crime and Corruption, and two other NGOs involved in training procurement observers or procurement reforms.

instruction: What is the specific function of the Procurement Transparency Group regarding government contracts?
input: The Group shall evaluate, comment on, record and monitor contracts entered into by NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs and SUCs involving an amount of One Hundred Million Pesos (100,000,000.00) and above.
output: The Group's function is to evaluate, comment on, record, and monitor contracts of NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs, and SUCs valued at P100,000,000.00 or more.

instruction: How is the participation of a non-government organization observer in the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) specified for large contracts?
input: For this purpose, pursuant to Procurement Law which requires at least one (1) NGO Observer in the BAC, there shall be one (1) NGO-member of the Group as specified above sitting as NGO Observer in the Bids and Awards Committee of NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs and SUCs for contracts involving an amount of P100,000,000.00 and above.
output: One NGO member of the Procurement Transparency Group shall serve as an NGO Observer in the Bids and Awards Committee for contracts of NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs, and SUCs that are P100,000,000.00 or more.

instruction: What is the responsibility of the NGO Observer in a Bids and Awards Committee?
input: The NGO Observer shall call the attention of agency heads on potential non-compliance with R.A. 9184 and its IRR-A.
output: The NGO Observer is responsible for calling the attention of agency heads to any potential non-compliance with R.A. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations-A (IRR-A).

instruction: Based on the findings of the NGO Observer, what actions can the Procurement Transparency Group take?
input: Based on the findings of the NGO Observer, the group shall make timely recommendations of remedial actions, improvements in procurement, contract implementation and monitoring processes to ensure compliance with contractual terms and to safeguard government and public interest.
output: The group can make timely recommendations for remedial actions and improvements in procurement, contract implementation, and monitoring processes.

instruction: What happens if a government agency refuses to provide documents and information on a contract to the Procurement Transparency Group?
input: All relevant documents and information on contracts requested by the Group shall be provided by the concerned NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs, SUCs and LGUs without causing any delay in the bidding process.
output: The document does not specify a direct consequence for refusal, but it states that all relevant documents must be provided to the Group without causing delay.

instruction: If the Procurement Transparency Group finds non-compliance, what actions can it recommend to the PAGC?
input: Upon findings of non-compliance with the foregoing directives, the Group shall recommend to PAGC the imposition of sanctions, implementation of remedial measures and the filing of criminal, civil and/or administrative charges, and provide information for actions that may be taken on its recommendations.
output: The Group can recommend that the Presidential Anti-Graft Commission (PAGC) impose sanctions, implement remedial measures, and file criminal, civil, and/or administrative charges.

instruction: How does this Executive Order affect the existing functions of government agencies related to procurement?
input: This Order shall not affect not modify existing functions of NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs, SUCs and LGUs relative to the processing, awarding, approval and review of procurement contracts except as herein specifically provided.
output: The Order does not affect or modify existing functions of government agencies regarding procurement processing, awarding, approval, and review, except for the specific provisions outlined in the Order.

instruction: What is the power of the Procurement Transparency Group regarding guidelines and deputization?
input: The Group shall issue guidelines for compliance and monitoring activities and utilize the personnel and facilities or its member agencies or organizations, and may, upon request, deputize and/or, on its own initiative, contract experts, local communities and government unit and non-government entities to assist in information gathering and evaluation, and in contract compliance monitoring.
output: The Group can issue guidelines, use personnel and facilities from member agencies, and deputize or contract experts, local communities, and non-government entities to assist with information gathering and monitoring.

instruction: What is the purpose of the 'Separability' section in the Executive Order?
input: Any portion of this Executive Order that may be declared unconstitutional shall not have the effect of nullifying its other portions or provisions, as long as such remaining portions can still be given effect.
output: The section ensures that if any part of the Executive Order is found to be unconstitutional, the remaining parts will still be valid and can be implemented.

instruction: On what date was Executive Order No. 662 signed?
input: DONE in the City of Manila, this 20th day of September in the year of Our Lord, Two Thousand and Seven.
output: The Executive Order was signed on September 20, 2007.

instruction: Who signed Executive Order No. 662?
input:
(Sgd.) GLORIA M. ARROYO
President of the Philippines
output: The order was signed by President Gloria M. Arroyo.

input:

output: The official title is 'ENHANCING TRANSPARENCY MEASURES UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184 AND CREATING THE PROCUREMENT TRANSPARENCY BOARD'.

instruction: Why was the Procurement Transparency Board created?
input: WHEREAS, there is a need for a body to monitor compliance to anti-graft mechanism, to deter anomalies in the awarding of public sector contracts and to prevent losses due to procurement irregularities;
output: It was created to monitor compliance with anti-graft mechanisms, deter anomalies in public sector contracts, and prevent losses from procurement irregularities.

output: R.A. 9184 establishes transparency as a governing principle in public procurement, which this Executive Order seeks to enhance.

instruction: Who is responsible for maintaining the database of large public sector contracts?
input: The GPPB shall cause to be maintained in the appropriate government website a database of proposed and concluded public sector contracts involving an amount of P100,000,000.00 and above.

output: The Bids and Awards Committees (BACs) are directed to post the required procurement reports and information on the appropriate government websites and PhilGEPS.

The NGO Observer shall discuss and addressed issued and concerns gathered from his/her procurement monitoring activities.

instruction: Who is responsible for designating the permanent representatives from government agencies to the Procurement Transparency Group?

instruction: What is the process for non-government organizations to authorize representatives to the Procurement Transparency Group?

input: WHEREAS, there is a need for a body to monitor compliance to anti-graft mechanism, to deter anomalies in the awarding of public sector contracts and to prevent losses due to procurement irregularities;

instruction: What is the purpose of the Procurement Transparency Group's recommendation to the PAGC?

output: The purpose is to provide a basis for the PAGC to impose sanctions, implement remedial measures, and file appropriate charges against non-compliant officials.

instruction: How can the Procurement Transparency Group expand its information gathering and evaluation capabilities?
input: It may, upon request, deputize and/or, on its own initiative, contract experts, local communities and government unit and non-government entities to assist in information gathering and evaluation, and in contract compliance monitoring.
output: The group can deputize or contract experts, local communities, and government and non-government entities to assist in these activities.

instruction: What are the key reports that all government agencies must post online?
output: The key reports are the Annual Procurement Plan, the Procurement Monitoring Report, the list of invited observers, and blacklisting orders.

instruction: What is the role of the GPPB's Technical Support Office in relation to procuring entities?

output: The GPPB-TSO is authorized to monitor and assist government entities in improving their compliance with R.A. 9184.

instruction: What is the significance of the P100,000,000.00 amount in Executive Order 662?
input: The GPPB shall cause to be maintained in the appropriate government website a database of proposed and concluded public sector contracts involving an amount of P100,000,000.00 and above. ... The Group shall evaluate, comment on, record and monitor contracts entered into by NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs and SUCs involving an amount of One Hundred Million Pesos (100,000,000.00) and above.
output: The amount of P100,000,000.00 is the threshold for contracts that must be included in the GPPB database and are subject to monitoring by the Procurement Transparency Group.

instruction: How are government agencies and non-government organizations represented in the Procurement Transparency Group?
input: The heads of the government agencies shall, by special written authority, designate their duly authorized permanent representatives to the Group. The non-government organizations are invited to authorize, by special written authority, permanent representatives to the Group.
output: Government agencies and NGOs designate their permanent representatives to the group via a special written authority.

instruction: What is the role of the PhilGEPS bulletin board under this Order?
input: All NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs, Sucs, and LGUs, through its BACs, are likewise directed to post all their procurement opportunities, results thereof, and other related information in the PhilGEPS bulletin board, as required under Section 8.2.1 of the IRR-A of R.R. 9184.
output: The PhilGEPS bulletin board serves as the mandatory public platform for posting procurement opportunities, results, and related information.

instruction: What does the Executive Order say about the role of the President of the Philippines in public procurement?
input: I, GLORIA M. ARROYO, President of the Republic of the Philippines, by virtue of the powers vested in me by law, do hereby order: ENHANCING TRANSPARENCY
output: The President, by virtue of powers vested in her by law, has ordered the enhancement of transparency measures in public procurement.

instruction: What does the Executive Order specify regarding the source of funding for deputized entities?
input: It may, subject to availability of funds, provide financial assistance to such deputized agencies or entities.
output: The Order states that financial assistance to deputized entities is possible, but it is subject to the availability of funds.

instruction: How does the Executive Order ensure that the Procurement Transparency Group's work is not a secret process?
input: The heads of agencies concerned, the Office of the Executive Secretary and such other agencies or offices as the Group may determine, shall be furnished copies of its comments and recommendations.
output: The Group is required to furnish copies of its comments and recommendations to heads of concerned agencies and other key offices, ensuring transparency in its operations.

instruction: What is the objective of close coordination between the GPPB and the Procurement Transparency Group?
input: WHEREAS, the efficiency and effectivity of the GPPB in the performance of its monitoring function would be further enhanced through close coordination with a procurement transparency body;
output: Close coordination with a procurement transparency body enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of the GPPB's monitoring function.

instruction: What is the ultimate purpose of the Procurement Transparency Group's functions?
input: The Group shall evaluate, comment on, record and monitor contracts entered into by NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs and SUCs involving an amount of One Hundred Million Pesos (100,000,000.00) and above...to ensure compliance with contractual terms and to safeguard government and public interest.
output: The ultimate purpose is to ensure compliance with contractual terms and safeguard government and public interest by monitoring large contracts.

instruction: What is the role of the Department of Budget and Management in the Procurement Transparency Group?
input: There is hereby created a PROCUREMENT TRANSPARENCY GROUP, headed by the GPPB and with the following government agencies and non-government organizations (NGOs) as members: ... d.)Department of Budget and Management;
output: The Department of Budget and Management is a member of the Procurement Transparency Group.

instruction: How are non-compliance issues reported and addressed according to the Executive Order?
input: The NGO Observer shall call the attention of agency heads on potential non-compliance with R.A. 9184 and its IRR-A. ... The group shall make timely recommendations of remedial actions, improvements in procurement, contract implementation and monitoring processes...Upon findings of non-compliance with the foregoing directives, the Group shall recommend to PAGC the imposition of sanctions, implementation of remedial measures and the filing of criminal, civil and/or administrative charges...
output: Non-compliance is first raised by the NGO Observer to agency heads. The group then makes recommendations for remedial actions and can recommend sanctions or charges to the PAGC.

instruction: What is the role of the Department of Justice in the Procurement Transparency Group?
input: There is hereby created a PROCUREMENT TRANSPARENCY GROUP, headed by the GPPB and with the following government agencies and non-government organizations (NGOs) as members: ... c.)Department of Justice;
output: The Department of Justice is a member of the Procurement Transparency Group.

instruction: What is the role of the Presidential Anti-Graft Commission (PAGC) in the Executive Order?
input: Upon findings of non-compliance with the foregoing directives, the Group shall recommend to PAGC the imposition of sanctions, implementation of remedial measures and the filing of criminal, civil and/or administrative charges, and provide information for actions that may be taken on its recommendations.
output: The PAGC is the body to which the Procurement Transparency Group recommends sanctions, remedial measures, and the filing of charges for non-compliance.

instruction: What are the two types of government entities whose contracts the Procurement Transparency Group evaluates?
input: The Group shall evaluate, comment on, record and monitor contracts entered into by NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs and SUCs involving an amount of One Hundred Million Pesos (100,000,000.00) and above.
output: The group evaluates contracts from National Government Agencies (NGAs), Government Owned and/or Controlled Corporations (GOCCs), Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), and State Universities and Colleges (SUCs).

instruction: How does the Executive Order empower the GPPB?
input: R.A. 9184 and its IRR-A empower the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) to protect national interest in all matters affecting public procurement and authorizes its Technical Support Office (GPPB-TSO) to monitor and assist procuring entities improve their compliance with R.A. 9481;
output: The GPPB is empowered by R.A. 9184 to protect national interest in all matters of public procurement.

instruction: What is the general purpose of the 'WHEREAS' clauses in the Executive Order?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184 (R.A. 9184) or the Government Procurement Reform Act and its Implementing Rules and Regulations Pact A (IRR-A) recognize and adopt transparency as a governing principle in public procurement;...WHEREAS, the projected increase in public sector capital spending under the Medium Term Philippine Development Plan requires transparency and compliance to the rule of law: ...
output: The 'WHEREAS' clauses provide the rationale and context for the Executive Order, explaining the need for its provisions based on existing laws and national development plans.

instruction: What is the responsibility of the heads of government agencies regarding their representatives to the Procurement Transparency Group?
input: The heads of the government agencies shall, by special written authority, designate their duly authorized permanent representatives to the Group.
output: They must designate their duly authorized permanent representatives to the group through a special written authority.

instruction: What is the specific role of non-government organizations that are members of the Procurement Transparency Group?
input: For this purpose, pursuant to Procurement Law which requires at least one (1) NGO Observer in the BAC, there shall be one (1) NGO-member of the Group as specified above sitting as NGO Observer in the Bids and Awards Committee of NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs and SUCs for contracts involving an amount of P100,000,000.00 and above.
output: One NGO member from the group serves as an NGO Observer on the Bids and Awards Committees for large contracts.

instruction: How is the Procurement Transparency Group's monitoring of contracts different from that of regular procurement monitoring?
input: The Group shall evaluate, comment on, record and monitor contracts entered into by NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs and SUCs involving an amount of One Hundred Million Pesos (100,000,000.00) and above... Based on the findings of the NGO Observer, the group shall make timely recommendations of remedial actions, improvements in procurement, contract implementation and monitoring processes...
output: The group's monitoring is specifically for large contracts (P100M+) and is tied to making recommendations and potentially recommending sanctions based on the findings of a dedicated NGO Observer.

instruction: If a policymaker wanted to understand the government's stance on procurement transparency, what part of the Executive Order would be most relevant?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act No. 9184 (R.A. 9184) or the Government Procurement Reform Act and its Implementing Rules and Regulations Pact A (IRR-A) recognize and adopt transparency as a governing principle in public procurement;
output: The 'WHEREAS' clauses that explicitly state transparency is a governing principle in public procurement under R.A. 9184 would be most relevant.

instruction: What specific action is required of bidders' associations regarding blacklisting orders under this Executive Order?
input: Blacklisting orders against suppliers, constructors, and consultants.
output: The document requires that blacklisting orders be posted, which would be relevant to bidders and their associations, but it does not specify any actions required of the associations themselves.

instruction: What is the relationship between the Procurement Transparency Group's findings and the recommendations it makes?
input: Based on the findings of the NGO Observer, the group shall make timely recommendations of remedial actions, improvements in procurement, contract implementation and monitoring processes to ensure compliance with contractual terms and to safeguard government and public interest.
output: The group's recommendations are directly based on the findings gathered by the NGO Observer, aiming to address identified issues and ensure compliance.

instruction: What is the main role of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) in this Executive Order?

output: The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) is a member of the Procurement Transparency Group.

input: All NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs, Sucs, and LGUs, through its BACs, are likewise directed to post all their procurement opportunities, results thereof, and other related information in the PhilGEPS bulletin board, as required under Section 8.2.1 of the IRR-A of R.R. 9184.

instruction: What is the role of the National Economic and Development Authority in the Procurement Transparency Group?

output: The group's primary function is to evaluate, comment on, record, and monitor all contracts of P100,000,000.00 and above.

instruction: What is the role of the Bids and Awards Committees (BACs) in implementing the transparency measures under this order?
input: All National Government Agencies (NGAs), Government Owned and/or Controlled Corporations (GOCCs), Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), and Local Government Units (LGUs), through their bids and awards committees are directed to post in the appropriate government website the following procurement reports...

instruction: What specific documents and information must government agencies provide to the Procurement Transparency Group upon request?
input: All relevant documents and information on contracts requested by the Group shall be provided by the concerned NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs, SUCs and LGUs without causing any delay in the bidding process.

instruction: What is the primary purpose of Executive Order No. 662-A?
input: EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 662-A AMENDING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 662, SERIES OF 2007 ENTITLED “ENHANCING TRANSPARENCY MEASURES UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184 AND CREATING THE PROCUREMENT TRANSPARENCY GROUP”

instruction: What is the key change made by E.O. 662-A to the membership of the Procurement Transparency Group?

instruction: What is the stated goal of E.O. 662-A regarding public perception of procurement activities?

instruction: What is the function of the Procurement Transparency Group?

instruction: Which government agencies are members of the Procurement Transparency Group?

Upon submission of an irrevocable letter of credit or bank guarantee issued by a Universal or Commercial Bank, advance payment not to exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the contract amount shall be allowed and paid within sixty (60) calendar days from signing of the contract. The irrevocable letter of credit or bank guarantee must be for an equivalent amount, shall remain valid until the goods are delivered, and accompanied by a claim for advance payment.”
output: It contains the actual, verbatim text of the amended provision, replacing the old rule with the new one.

instruction: How does the memorandum ensure the government is protected financially when an advance payment is made?
input: The irrevocable letter of credit or bank guarantee must be for an equivalent amount, shall remain valid until the goods are delivered, and accompanied by a claim for advance payment.
output: It requires the submission of an irrevocable letter of credit or bank guarantee that is for an equivalent amount to the advance payment and remains valid until the goods are delivered.

instruction: What is the main difference between an irrevocable letter of credit and a bank guarantee in this context?
input: WHEREAS, in order to provide sufficient safeguards for the Government, the GPPB recognizes the need to provide for the inclusion of a provision authorizing advance payment upon submission of an irrevocable letter of credit as an alternative to a bank guarantee;
output: The document treats them as equivalent alternatives for providing a safeguard to the government for the advance payment.

instruction: What is the significance of the phrase “to give equal opportunities to local suppliers”?
input: WHEREAS, the GPPB and the National Economic Development Authority (NEDA), through GPPB Resolution No. 04-2010 (s. 2010), recognize the need to amend No. 4.5 of Annex “D” by increasing the allowable amount of advance payment to fifteen percent (15%) of the contract amount and expanding the rule to include procurement of goods, regardless of their source, consistent with the policy of giving equal opportunities to local suppliers;
output: It states a key policy goal of the amendment, which is to remove a disadvantage faced by local suppliers under the previous rule.

instruction: What is the legal basis for the GPPB's authority to amend the IRR of RA 9184?
input: WHEREAS, Section 63 of RA No. 9184 authorizes the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) to formulate and amend, whenever necessary, the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA No. 9184;
output: It is Section 63 of RA No. 9184.

instruction: What is the primary purpose of Administrative Order No. 17?
input: WHEREAS, the national government has undertaken comprehensive reforms to modernize and standardize government procurement systems to ensure transparency and accountability in government transactions, and enhance efficiency and effectiveness in the procurement of goods, services and civil works;
output: To modernize and standardize government procurement systems to ensure transparency, accountability, efficiency, and effectiveness.

instruction: Who signed Administrative Order No. 17 and when was it signed?
input:
Signed on July 28, 2011

(Sgd.) BENIGNO S. AQUINO III
President of the Philippines
output: It was signed by President Benigno S. Aquino III on July 28, 2011.

instruction: What is the overarching policy reiterated by Administrative Order No. 17 regarding government procurement?
input: The national government hereby reiterates the policy that procurement of government supplies, materials, and equipment shall be done in the most transparent and competitive manner by purchasing from legally, technically, and financially capable sources in economic lot sizes, by observing cost-efficient specifications, and by making prompt payment.
output: Government procurement must be transparent and competitive, sourcing from legally, technically, and financially capable entities, with cost-efficient specifications and prompt payment.

instruction: What are the two main systems government agencies must use for procurement according to Section 1?
input: In line with this, all government agencies shall procure their common-use supplies from the PS and use the PhilGEPS in all their procurement activities, including publishing all their bid opportunities and posting all their awards and contracts in it, in accordance with R.A. No. 9184.
output: The Procurement Service (PS) for common-use supplies and the Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) for all procurement activities.

instruction: Which government entities are covered by Administrative Order No. 17?
input: This Administrative Order shall apply to all National Government Agencies, including Military and Police Units; Government-Owned and/or -Controlled Corporations (GOCCs); Government Financial Institutions (GFIs); State Universities and Colleges (SUCs); and Local Government Units (LGUs).
output: National Government Agencies, Military and Police Units, GOCCs, GFIs, SUCs, and LGUs.

instruction: Define 'Common-Use Supplies' as per the document.
input: Common-Use Supplies refers to those supplies, materials, and equipment included in the price list of the PS which are necessary in the transaction of the official business of the procuring entity and consumed in its day-to-day operations.
output: Supplies, materials, and equipment on the PS price list that are necessary for the day-to-day operations of a procuring entity.

instruction: What is the 'Electronic Bulletin Board' in PhilGEPS?
input: Electronic Bulletin Board refers to the central repository of government procurement opportunities, notices, and bid results including awards, bidding documents, supplemental bid bulletins, and other related documents in the PhilGEPS.
output: A central repository within PhilGEPS for government procurement opportunities, notices, bid results, and related documents.

instruction: What is the purpose of the 'Suppliers' Registry'?
input: Suppliers’ Registry refers to the centralized electronic database of all manufacturers, suppliers, distributors, contractors, and consultants registered under the PhilGEPS.
output: It is a centralized electronic database of all manufacturers, suppliers, distributors, contractors, and consultants registered in PhilGEPS.

instruction: What is the difference between an 'Electronic Catalogue' and a 'Virtual Store'?
input:
Electronic Catalogue  refers to the list of common-use supplies that are available from the PS and its depots as appearing in the PhilGEPS.
Virtual Store – refers to an enhanced electronic catalogue of the PhilGEPS that allows procuring entities to purchase common-use supplies online that are available from the PS and its depots.
output: The Electronic Catalogue is a list of common-use supplies, while the Virtual Store is an enhanced catalogue that allows procuring entities to purchase these supplies online.

instruction: Explain what 'Electronic Payment' entails.
input: Electronic Payment (E-payment)  refers to any digital financial transaction such as the transfer of funds from procuring entities to and from PhilGEPS and from procuring entities to suppliers.
output: It refers to digital financial transactions, including the transfer of funds between procuring entities, PhilGEPS, and suppliers.

instruction: What is 'Electronic Bid Submission'?
input: Electronic Bid Submission (E-bid Submission) refers to a facility in PhilGEPS that allows bidders through the Internet to download bidding documents and submit bid proposals or tenders online.
output: A PhilGEPS facility that allows bidders to download documents and submit their bid proposals online.

instruction: How should government entities procure common-use supplies?
input: Common-use supplies shall be procured directly from the PS or its depots without need of public bidding as provided in Section 53.5 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRRs) of R.A. 9184.
output: They must be procured directly from the Procurement Service (PS) or its depots without the need for public bidding.

instruction: What are the specific actions mandated for all government procuring entities regarding PhilGEPS?
input: All government procuring entities are mandated to use the PhilGEPS in its procurement activities, and shall post all opportunities, notices, awards, and contracts in it as the central portal of government procurement transactions in accordance with R.A. 9184 and its IRRs.
output: They must use PhilGEPS for all procurement activities and post all opportunities, notices, awards, and contracts on the system.

instruction: What will the DBM consider when evaluating agencies' proposed budgets?
input: The DBM may consider data available in the PhilGEPS, such as opportunities, notices, and awards posted, in its evaluation and review of the proposed budgets of the agencies.
output: The DBM may consider PhilGEPS data such as posted opportunities, notices, and awards.

instruction: What should a procuring entity do if it does not have Internet access to use PhilGEPS?
input: Procuring entities without Internet access may use the Public Access Terminals located in the nearest PS Depots or other public Internet facilities. For this purpose, they may also seek the assistance of the PhilGEPS Help Desk.
output: They can use Public Access Terminals at PS Depots, other public Internet facilities, or seek assistance from the PhilGEPS Help Desk.

instruction: Can the Procurement Service charge fees for the use of PhilGEPS?
input: The PS may charge fees for the use of PhilGEPS in order to sustain its operation, subject to existing rules and regulations.
output: Yes, the PS may charge fees to sustain its operation, subject to existing rules and regulations.

instruction: What is the DBM's responsibility concerning PhilGEPS funding?
input: In line with this, the DBM shall provide funding from its appropriations for the continuous enhancement and operation of the PhilGEPS until such time that it achieves financial sustainability as determined by the Government Procurement and Policy Board (GPPB).
output: The DBM must provide funding for the continuous enhancement and operation of PhilGEPS until it becomes financially sustainable, as determined by the GPPB.

instruction: How will the Procurement Service improve product quality for common-use supplies?
input: Review of Product Standards and Specifications. Periodically review product standards and specifications for common-use supplies in coordination with the Bureau of Product Standards of the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) for the purpose of improving product quality.
output: By periodically reviewing product standards and specifications in coordination with the Bureau of Product Standards of the DTI.

instruction: How will the PS expand the list of common-use supplies?
input: Expansion of Product List. Regularly conduct a survey to determine other products commonly purchased by procuring entities for addition to the list of common-use supplies.
output: By regularly conducting a survey to identify other commonly purchased products by procuring entities.

instruction: What activity will the PS undertake to benchmark prices of common-use supplies?
input: Price Monitoring. Regularly conduct price monitoring of common-use supplies for the purpose of benchmarking prices against the market.
output: It will regularly conduct price monitoring of common-use supplies to benchmark them against market prices.

instruction: How can the PS expand its distribution system?
input: Expansion of Distribution System. Encourage LGUs to establish depots in their locality, as part of their economic enterprise activity.
output: By encouraging Local Government Units (LGUs) to establish depots in their localities.

instruction: What is the main objective of the new computerized system for inventory management?
input: Develop a computerized system to manage inventories, with the primary objective of determining and controlling stock levels within the physical distribution function to balance the need for product availability against the need for minimizing stock holding and handling costs.
output: To determine and control stock levels to balance product availability with minimizing stock holding and handling costs.

instruction: What new features will the PS pursue for PhilGEPS to enhance transparency?
input: Additional PhilGEPS Features. Pursue the development of additional PhilGEPS features and enhancements to enhance transparency and competition such as the Expanded Suppliers’ Registry, integration of Annual Procurement Plans into the system, module for contract implementation, and monitoring tools for Civil Society Organizations and Commission on Audit (COA) Auditors.
output: Expanded Suppliers' Registry, integration of Annual Procurement Plans, a contract implementation module, and monitoring tools for CSOs and COA Auditors.

instruction: Who is responsible for periodically evaluating the performance of the centralized procurement system?
input: The GPPB shall conduct periodic evaluation of the performance of the centralized procurement system in terms of economy and efficiency pursuant to Section 2 of EO No. 359.
output: The Government Procurement and Policy Board (GPPB) is responsible for this evaluation.

instruction: What must Procuring Entities do regarding procurement training and manuals according to RA 9187?
input: In addition, the GPPB shall also conduct periodic evaluation of all Procuring Entities in terms of their compliance with Section 63, Art. XX of RA 9187, which requires them to conduct Procurement Training Programs and produce Procurement Operations Manuals for all offices and agencies of the government.
output: They are required to conduct Procurement Training Programs and produce Procurement Operations Manuals for all their offices and agencies.

instruction: What happens if a government agency does not comply with this Administrative Order?
input: Non-compliance with the provisions of this AO shall be dealt with in accordance with applicable laws, rules and regulations.
output: Non-compliance will be dealt with in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations.

instruction: If a procurement officer needs to purchase new common-use supplies, what is the required procurement method?
input: Common-use supplies shall be procured directly from the PS or its depots without need of public bidding as provided in Section 53.5 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRRs) of R.A. 9184.
output: The officer must procure them directly from the PS or its depots without public bidding.

instruction: How should a bidder find a procurement opportunity from a government agency?

output: The bidder should check the PhilGEPS Electronic Bulletin Board, as all government entities must post opportunities there.

instruction: How can a COA Auditor use PhilGEPS to monitor a government agency's procurement?
input: Pursue the development of additional PhilGEPS features and enhancements to enhance transparency and competition such as the... monitoring tools for Civil Society Organizations and Commission on Audit (COA) Auditors.
output: The PS is pursuing the development of specific monitoring tools within PhilGEPS for COA Auditors to use.

instruction: What is the purpose of the policy innovations mentioned in the document's preamble?
input: WHEREAS, innovations in procurement have been successfully implemented by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) through the Procurement Service (PS) and its Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) which currently features an Electronic Bulletin Board, a Suppliers’ Registry, and an Electronic Catalogue;

instruction: Which government office provides funding for the continuous operation of PhilGEPS?
input: In line with this, the DBM shall provide funding from its appropriations for the continuous enhancement and operation of the PhilGEPS until such time that it achieves financial sustainability as determined by the Government Procurement and Policy Board (GPPB).

instruction: What specific action will the PS take to make its new inventory system more useful for client agencies?
input: This system shall be connected to the Virtual Store for common-use goods to enable client agencies to know the stock availability of items that they are ordering.
output: The computerized inventory system will be connected to the Virtual Store to allow client agencies to check the stock availability of items they wish to order.

instruction: What is the role of the Government Procurement and Policy Board (GPPB) in relation to the Procurement Service?
input: The GPPB shall conduct periodic evaluation of the performance of the centralized procurement system in terms of economy and efficiency pursuant to Section 2 of EO No. 359.
output: The GPPB is responsible for periodically evaluating the centralized procurement system's performance for economy and efficiency.

instruction: What is the legal basis for the mandatory compliance of all government agencies with the policies mentioned in the Administrative Order?
input: WHEREAS, R. A. No. 9184 incorporates said policies and innovations and. reiterates the mandatory compliance therewith by all government agencies in support of transparency, competitiveness, streamlined procurement process, system of accountability, and public monitoring.

instruction: If a bidder wants to submit a proposal online, which PhilGEPS feature should they use?

output: They should use the Electronic Bid Submission (E-bid Submission) facility.

instruction: What is one key function of the Procurement Service's strengthened operations?
input: In line with the directives of this Administrative Order, the PS shall strengthen its operations and shall undertake the following activities on a regular basis: ... Price Monitoring. Regularly conduct price monitoring of common-use supplies for the purpose of benchmarking prices against the market.
output: To regularly conduct price monitoring of common-use supplies to benchmark them against market prices.

instruction: What is the primary role of the PS according to Letter of Instruction No. 755 and EO No. 359?
input: WHEREAS, the PS, by virtue of Letter of Instruction No. 755 (s. 1978) and Executive Order (EO) No. 359 (s. 1989), is tasked with the implementation of a government-wide procurement system for common-use office supplies, materials, and equipment on behalf of all government agencies;
output: To implement a government-wide procurement system for common-use supplies on behalf of all government agencies.

instruction: What is the purpose of a computerized inventory management system for the PS?
input: Improvement of Inventory Management. Develop a computerized system to manage inventories, with the primary objective of determining and controlling stock levels within the physical distribution function to balance the need for product availability against the need for minimizing stock holding and handling costs.
output: To manage inventories by determining and controlling stock levels to balance product availability with cost minimization.

instruction: What is the goal of the PhilGEPS enhancements being pursued by the PS?
input: Pursue the development of additional PhilGEPS features and enhancements to enhance transparency and competition such as the Expanded Suppliers’ Registry, integration of Annual Procurement Plans into the system, module for contract implementation, and monitoring tools for Civil Society Organizations and Commission on Audit (COA) Auditors.
output: To enhance transparency and competition in the procurement process.

instruction: What is the role of the DTI's Bureau of Product Standards in relation to the PS?
input: Review of Product Standards and Specifications. Periodically review product standards and specifications for common-use supplies in coordination with the Bureau of Product Standards of the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) for the purpose of improving product quality.
output: The PS must coordinate with the Bureau of Product Standards to periodically review product standards and specifications for common-use supplies.

instruction: What is the goal of the expansion of the PS's distribution system?
input: Expansion of Distribution System. Encourage LGUs to establish depots in their locality, as part of their economic enterprise activity.
output: The goal is to expand the distribution system by encouraging LGUs to establish depots in their locality as an economic enterprise.

instruction: What is a 'Suppliers' Registry'?
input: Suppliers’ Registry refers to the centralized electronic database of all manufacturers, suppliers, distributors, contractors, and consultants registered under the PhilGEPS.
output: A centralized electronic database of all manufacturers, suppliers, distributors, contractors, and consultants who are registered with the PhilGEPS.

instruction: What is the purpose of the policy that procurement should be done from 'legally, technically, and financially capable sources'?
input: The national government hereby reiterates the policy that procurement of government supplies, materials, and equipment shall be done in the most transparent and competitive manner by purchasing from legally, technically, and financially capable sources in economic lot sizes, by observing cost-efficient specifications, and by making prompt payment.
output: This policy ensures that government procurement is competitive, transparent, and results in effective transactions by working with qualified parties.

instruction: Why does the Administrative Order reiterate policies on procurement?
input: R. A. No. 9184 incorporates said policies and innovations and. reiterates the mandatory compliance therewith by all government agencies in support of transparency, competitiveness, streamlined procurement process, system of accountability, and public monitoring.
output: To ensure mandatory compliance by all government agencies and to support transparency, competitiveness, a streamlined process, accountability, and public monitoring.

instruction: How will the PS enable client agencies to check stock availability?
input: This system shall be connected to the Virtual Store for common-use goods to enable client agencies to know the stock availability of items that they are ordering.
output: By connecting its new computerized inventory system to the PhilGEPS Virtual Store.

instruction: Who determines when PhilGEPS achieves financial sustainability?
input: the DBM shall provide funding from its appropriations for the continuous enhancement and operation of the PhilGEPS until such time that it achieves financial sustainability as determined by the Government Procurement and Policy Board (GPPB).
output: The Government Procurement and Policy Board (GPPB).

instruction: What must all government agencies do with their bid awards and contracts?
input: All government agencies shall procure their common-use supplies from the PS and use the PhilGEPS in all their procurement activities, including publishing all their bid opportunities and posting all their awards and contracts in it, in accordance with R.A. No. 9184.
output: They must post all their awards and contracts on PhilGEPS.

instruction: What is the primary function of the PhilGEPS Help Desk?
input: For this purpose, they may also seek the assistance of the PhilGEPS Help Desk.
output: To assist procuring entities that lack Internet access or need help using PhilGEPS.

instruction: What is the purpose of including an 'Expanded Suppliers' Registry' as a new PhilGEPS feature?
input: Pursue the development of additional PhilGEPS features and enhancements to enhance transparency and competition such as the Expanded Suppliers’ Registry...
output: The purpose is to enhance transparency and competition in the procurement process.

instruction: When should government agencies subscribe to the new features of PhilGEPS like the Virtual Store?
input: All shall subscribe to the additional features of the PhilGEPS such as the Virtual Store, E-payment and E-bid submission as they become available and are implemented.
output: They must subscribe to these features as they become available and are implemented.

instruction: What specific action is the PS tasked to do to expand its product list?
input: Regularly conduct a survey to determine other products commonly purchased by procuring entities for addition to the list of common-use supplies.
output: The PS is tasked to regularly survey procuring entities to determine other products to add to the common-use supplies list.

instruction: What will happen to existing inconsistent rules and regulations after the Administrative Order's effectivity?
input: All issuances, orders, rules, and regulations or parts thereof which are inconsistent with the provisions of this Administrative Order are hereby revoked and/or modified accordingly.
output: They are revoked or modified to be consistent with the provisions of the Administrative Order.

instruction: What is the main objective of the national government's procurement reforms?
input: WHEREAS, the national government has undertaken comprehensive reforms to modernize and standardize government procurement systems to ensure transparency and accountability in government transactions, and enhance efficiency and effectiveness in the procurement of goods, services and civil works;
output: To modernize and standardize procurement systems to ensure transparency, accountability, efficiency, and effectiveness.

instruction: What is the purpose of PhilGEPS's features like the Electronic Bulletin Board, Suppliers' Registry, and Electronic Catalogue?
input: WHEREAS, innovations in procurement have been successfully implemented by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) through the Procurement Service (PS) and its Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) which currently features an Electronic Bulletin Board, a Suppliers’ Registry, and an Electronic Catalogue;
output: These features were implemented to modernize and standardize government procurement systems.

instruction: When did Administrative Order No. 17 take effect?
input: This Administrative Order shall take effect immediately upon publication in a newspaper of general circulation.
output: It took effect immediately upon its publication in a newspaper of general circulation.

instruction: What is the PhilGEPS Electronic Bulletin Board?

instruction: What is the role of the DBM in the operation of PhilGEPS?

output: To manage inventories by balancing the need for product availability with the need to minimize costs associated with stock holding and handling.

instruction: What kind of data from PhilGEPS can the DBM use for budget evaluation?
input: The DBM may consider data available in the PhilGEPS, such as opportunities, notices, and awards posted, in its evaluation and review of the proposed budgets of the agencies.

instruction: What does a 'Virtual Store' in PhilGEPS allow procuring entities to do?
input: Virtual Store refers to an enhanced electronic catalogue of the PhilGEPS that allows procuring entities to purchase common-use supplies online that are available from the PS and its depots.
output: It allows them to purchase common-use supplies online from the PS and its depots.

instruction: What is the purpose of Administrative Order No. 34?
input:
ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO. 34
DIRECTING STRICT COMPLIANCE BY ALL AGENCIES AND INSTRUMENTALITIES OF THE EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT WITH TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY AND GOOD GOVERNANCE POLICIES AND MEASURES IN THE PROCUREMENT PROCESS
output: It directs all agencies and instrumentalities of the Executive Department to strictly comply with transparency, accountability, and good governance policies in the procurement process.

instruction: What constitutional policies are cited as a basis for this Administrative Order?
input: WHEREAS, Article II, Sections 27 and 28 of the Constitution declare it a policy of the State to maintain honesty and integrity in the public service, take positive and effective measures against graft and corruption, and implement a policy of full public disclosure of transactions involving public interest;
output: Article II, Sections 27 and 28, which declare a state policy to maintain honesty and integrity, take measures against graft and corruption, and implement full public disclosure of transactions involving public interest.

instruction: What is the role of Republic Act No. 9184 in relation to this Administrative Order?
input: WHEREAS, Republic Act (RA) No. 9184 or the 'Government Procurement Reform Act,' has instituted measures to ensure transparency in the procurement process and in the implementation of procurement contracts, as well as accountability of public officials directly or indirectly involved in the same, and, under warranted circumstances, private parties that deal with the government;
output: RA No. 9184, the 'Government Procurement Reform Act,' institutes measures for transparency and accountability in the procurement process.

instruction: How does the General Appropriations Act (GAA) for FY 2020 relate to the directive?
input: WHEREAS, Sections 18, 93 and 94 of the General Provisions of RA No. 11465 or the 'General Appropriations Act (GAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2020,' require transparency in the disbursement of public funds through posting of financial and physical reports of government programs, and reporting on the status of infrastructure projects;

instruction: Who issued Administrative Order No. 34 and on what date?
