instruction: Can observers monitor procurement proceedings online?
input: The PhilGEPS shall allow observers, duly authorized by the concerned Bids and Awards Committee (BAC), to monitor the procurement proceedings on-line, provided, that such observers do not have any direct or indirect interest in the contract to be bidded out, as prescribed in Section 13 of the RIRR of RA No. 9184.
output: Yes, provided they are duly authorized by the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) and have no direct or indirect interest in the contract.

instruction: What information must be posted for infrastructure projects on agency websites and social media?
input: Project title, location and detailed description; approved budget for the contract; and winning contractor and the detailed estimates of the bid as awarded, within thirty (30) calendar days from entering into the contract; Start of construction, target date of completion, completion rate, project status and the reason/s in case of delay; Source of fund, implementing office, responsible official, contact number and electronic mail address; and Detailed actual cost of the project, variations issued, if any, within thirty (30) calendar days from the issuance of a certificate of completion.
output: Project title, location, description, approved budget, winning contractor, detailed bid estimates, construction start/completion dates, status, funding source, implementing office, contact info, and detailed actual cost.

instruction: When must the detailed cost of an infrastructure project be posted?
input: Detailed actual cost of the project, variations issued, if any, within thirty (30) calendar days from the issuance of a certificate of completion.
output: Within 30 calendar days from the issuance of a certificate of completion.

instruction: What information must agencies publish on their websites and social media for post-contract awards?
input: a. Project name; b. Approved budget for the contract; c. Contract period; d. Name of winning bidder and its official business address; e. Amount of contract awarded; f. Date of award and acceptance; and g. Implementing office/unit/division/bureau of the concerned agency instrumentality.
output: The project name, approved budget, contract period, winning bidder's name and address, awarded amount, date of award and acceptance, and the implementing office.

instruction: Are there any exceptions to the post-award disclosure requirements?
input: except contracts with implications on national security, all agencies and instrumentalities of the Executive department shall publish in their respective official websites and social media platforms the following post-award information:
output: Yes, contracts with implications on national security are exempt.

instruction: For what value of projects must post-award information also be published in a newspaper of general circulation?
input: For contracts involving projects with an approved budget of P50 Million and above, the foregoing post-award information shall be published once in a newspaper of general circulation, in addition to posting the same on the respective official websites and social media platforms of the agencies concerned.
output: Contracts with an approved budget of P50 million and above.

instruction: What is the role of the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) regarding blacklisting?
input: Pursuant to the Uniform Guidelines for Blacklisting of Manufacturers, Suppliers, Distributors, Contractors and Consultants, the GPPB shall prepare the Consolidated Blacklisting Report every quarter, based on the submitted Blacklisting Orders, and disseminate the same to procuring entities and the Commission on Audit.
output: The GPPB must prepare a Consolidated Blacklisting Report every quarter and disseminate it to procuring entities and the Commission on Audit.

instruction: Where must the Consolidated Blacklisting Report be posted?
input: The report shall be further posted on the GPPB website, the PhilGEPS and the official website and social media platform of the procuring entity, and shall indicate the number of times a person/entity has been blacklisted, the type of offense/violation committed, the penalty imposed, and the blacklisting agency concerned.
output: On the GPPB website, PhilGEPS, and the official website and social media platform of the procuring entity.

instruction: What specific details must the Consolidated Blacklisting Report include?
input: The report shall be further posted on the GPPB website, the PhilGEPS and the official website and social media platform of the procuring entity, and shall indicate the number of times a person/entity has been blacklisted, the type of offense/violation committed, the penalty imposed, and the blacklisting agency concerned.
output: The number of times an entity has been blacklisted, the offense, the penalty, and the blacklisting agency.

instruction: What is the penalty for non-compliance with the directives of Administrative Order No. 34?
input: Non-compliance with the foregoing directives shall be a ground for administrative action(s) against the erring public official or employee in accordance with civil service laws, rules and regulations, and other relevant laws.
output: It is a ground for administrative action against the erring public official or employee.

instruction: How are the funds for implementing this order sourced?
input: The funds necessary for the implementation of the foregoing directives shall be sourced from the regular appropriations of the agencies or instrumentalities concerned.
output: From the regular appropriations of the concerned agencies or instrumentalities.

instruction: Who is responsible for formulating the implementing guidelines for this order?
input: The Department of Budget and Management, in coordination with the GPPB, shall formulate guidelines, as may be necessary, for the effective implementation of this Order.
output: The Department of Budget and Management, in coordination with the GPPB.

instruction: What is the effectivity of this Administrative Order?
input: This Order shall take effect immediately upon publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.
output: It takes effect immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.

instruction: What does Section 1 of the order mandate regarding procurement?
input: Section 1. Transparency and Accountability in Procurement. Transparency and accountability in all government transactions, especially in procurement processes, shall be observed.
output: It mandates the observation of transparency and accountability in all government transactions, especially in procurement.

instruction: What specific law and its rules must be strictly complied with for procurement transparency?
input: all agencies and instrumentalities of the government shall strictly comply with the relevant provisions on transparency and accountability in the procurement process under RA No. 9184 and its Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (RIRR), the GAA, resolutions of the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) and other relevant laws, rules and regulations.
output: Agencies must strictly comply with RA No. 9184 and its Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (RIRR), the GAA, and GPPB resolutions.

instruction: If a provision of this order is found unconstitutional, what happens to the other parts?
input: If any part or provision of this Order shall be held unconstitutional or invalid, the other parts or provisions not affected thereby shall continue to be in full force and effect.
output: The other unaffected parts or provisions will remain in full force and effect.

instruction: According to this order, what is the State's policy regarding public service?

instruction: What is the official title of Republic Act No. 12009?
output: The New Government Procurement Act

instruction: What is the primary policy objective of the New Government Procurement Act?
input: It is the declared policy of the State to promote the ideals of good governance with a view towards transparency, competitiveness, efficiency, proportionality, accountability, public monitoring, procurement professionalization, sustainability, and value for money in government procurement.
output: To promote good governance through principles such as transparency, competitiveness, efficiency, accountability, and value for money in government procurement.

instruction: What are the eight governing principles of government procurement outlined in the Act?
output: The principles are: transparency, competitiveness, efficiency, proportionality, accountability, participatory procurement (public monitoring), sustainability, and professionalism.

instruction: Which government entities are required to follow the provisions of this Act?
input: Procurements by all branches and instrumentalities of the national government, its departments, bureaus, offices and agencies, including state universities and colleges (SUCs), government-owned and/or -controlled corporations (GOCCs), government financial institutions (GFIs), and local government units (LGUs).
output: All branches and instrumentalities of the national government, including departments, bureaus, offices and agencies, SUCs, GOCCs, GFIs, and LGUs.

instruction: Define 'Approved Budget for the Contract' (ABC).
input: Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC) refers to the budget for the contract duly approved by the Head of the Procuring Entity, as provided for in the General Appropriations Act or other authorized source of funds, in the case of National Government Agencies (NGAs)...
output: The budget for a contract that has been officially approved by the Head of the Procuring Entity.

instruction: What does the term 'Beneficial Owner' mean?
input: Beneficial Owner refers to a natural person who: (1) ultimately owns or dominantly influences the management or policies of the juridical entity; or (2) exercises ultimate effective control over the juridical entity.
output: A natural person who either ultimately owns or dominantly influences the management or policies of a juridical entity, or exercises ultimate effective control over it.

instruction: What is the definition of a 'Bid'?
input: Bid refers to a signed offer or proposal submitted by a supplier, manufacturer, distributor, contractor, consultant, and service provider in response to the bidding documents;
output: A signed offer or proposal submitted by a supplier, manufacturer, distributor, contractor, consultant, or service provider in response to bidding documents.

instruction: Who is a 'Bidder'?
input: Bidder refers to a supplier, manufacturer, distributor, contractor, consultant, and service provider who submits a bid in response to the requirements of the bidding documents;
output: A supplier, manufacturer, distributor, contractor, consultant, or service provider who submits a bid in response to the bidding documents.

instruction: What are 'Common-Use Supplies and Equipment' (CSEs)?
input: Common-Use Supplies and Equipment (CSE) refer to goods, materials, and equipment that are used repetitively in the day-to-day operations of Procuring Entities in the performance of their functions which are included in the electronic catalogue of the Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS);
output: Goods, materials, and equipment used routinely in the daily operations of Procuring Entities and are listed in the PhilGEPS electronic catalogue.

instruction: What is the meaning of 'Jury Duty' in the context of procurement?
input: Jury Duty refers to a responsibility in which the BAC, Technical Working Group (TWG), and Secretariat members, including end-users, give utmost priority to procurement assignments over all the other duties and responsibilities until the requirements for the procurement at hand are completed;
output: It is the responsibility of BAC, TWG, and Secretariat members to prioritize procurement assignments above all other duties until the project is completed.

instruction: Explain what 'Legal Eligibility' entails for a bidder.
input: Legal Eligibility refers to having the legal capacity to act as an entity as evidenced by permits, licenses, and/or registrations required by law to engage in the business of manufacturing, distributing, or delivering the Goods, Infrastructure Projects, and Consulting Services being procured;
output: It is the legal capacity of an entity to operate, evidenced by the permits, licenses, and registrations required by law to provide the procured goods, services, or projects.

instruction: Define 'Lifecycle Cost'.
input: Lifecycle Cost refers to the total cost of ownership over the entire life span of an asset from its acquisition, operation, maintenance, and disposal;
output: The total cost of an asset over its entire lifespan, including acquisition, operation, maintenance, and disposal.

instruction: What is the purpose of the 'Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System' (PhilGEPS)?
input: Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) refers to the single electronic procurement portal managed by the Procurement Service (PS-DBM) as provided in Section 20 of this Act;
output: It is the single electronic portal for all government procurement activities, managed by the Procurement Service (PS-DBM).

instruction: How is 'Procurement' defined in the Act?
input: Procurement refers to the acquisition of Goods and Consulting Services, and the contracting for Infrastructure Projects by the Procuring Entity. Procurement shall also include the lease of goods and real property.
output: The acquisition of goods and consulting services, and the contracting for infrastructure projects by a Procuring Entity, including the lease of goods and real property.

instruction: What is the definition of 'Value for Money'?
input: Value for Money refers to the optimum combination of quality and cost to meet the requirements and objectives of the end-user.
output: The optimal balance of quality and cost that meets the end-user's requirements and objectives.

instruction: Who is the 'Head of the Procuring Entity' (HoPE) for National Government Agencies (NGAs)?
input: Head of the Procuring Entity (HoPE) refers to: (1) the head of the agency or the duly authorized official, for NGAs;
output: The head of the agency or their duly authorized official.

instruction: What is the purpose of standardizing the procurement process and forms?
input: To systematize the procurement process, avoid confusion, and ensure transparency, the procurement process, including the forms to be used, shall be standardized insofar as practicable.
output: To systematize the procurement process, prevent confusion, and ensure transparency.

instruction: Who is responsible for developing generic procurement manuals and standard bidding forms?
input: For this purpose, the GPPB shall pursue the development of generic procurement manuals and standard bidding forms, the use of which, once issued shall be mandatory upon all Procuring Entities.
output: The Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB).

instruction: What must all procurement projects have to ensure sound decisions?
input: All procurement shall be undertaken with proper and sufficient planning and preparation to ensure sound procurement decisions. This includes the conduct of relevant market scoping, supply positioning, analysis of available procurement modalities, risk management, and disposal procedures as may be applicable.
output: Proper and sufficient planning and preparation, including market scoping, supply positioning, and risk management.

instruction: What must a Procuring Entity consider during the project planning stage regarding environmental impact?
input: During the planning stage, the Procuring Entity shall ensure that the project has minimal economic, social, and environmental risks or negative impact during its lifecycle, and that the goods and services are procured with due consideration for responsible and sustainable consumption and production practices, and the national policy.
output: They must ensure the project has minimal economic, social, and environmental risks and that goods and services are procured with consideration for sustainable consumption and production practices.

instruction: When is the procurement of second-hand, refurbished, or reconditioned goods allowed?
input: Provided, That the procurement of second-hand, refurbished or reconditioned goods, such as military, defense, or law enforcement equipment or materiel, may be considered to secure a contract that is most advantageous to the government subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DBM and subject to compliance with relevant criteria, such as durability, remaining useful life, sustainability, maintenance cost, and warranty.
output: It may be considered for military, defense, or law enforcement equipment to secure the most advantageous contract, subject to DBM guidelines and criteria like durability and remaining useful life.

instruction: What are the required contents of an Annual Procurement Plan (APP)?
input: the Annual Procurement Plan (APP), which shall at least include the following: (a) Name of the project/procurement; (b) Project management office (PMO)/end-user unit: (c) General description of the project/procurement; (d) Procurement methods to be adopted and indicating if the procurement tasks are to be outsourced; (e) Criteria for bid evaluation; (1) Time schedule; (g) Source of funds; and (h) Approved Budget for the Contract.
output: The APP must include the project name, end-user unit, general description, procurement methods, bid evaluation criteria, time schedule, source of funds, and the ABC.

instruction: What document must be approved before a government procurement can be undertaken?
input: No government procurement shall be undertaken unless it is in accordance with the approved APP or Indicative APP of the Procuring Entity, as the case may be. The APP shall be approved by the HoPE and must be consistent with its duly approved yearly budget or proposed budget in the case of the Indicative APP.
output: The approved Annual Procurement Plan (APP) or Indicative APP.

instruction: Under what condition can a Procuring Entity make modifications to the standard bidding forms?
input: However, whenever necessary, to suit the particular needs of the Procuring Entity, modifications may be made particularly for major and specialized procurement, subject to the approval of the GPPB.
output: Modifications can be made for major and specialized procurement to suit a Procuring Entity's needs, but only with the approval of the GPPB.

instruction: What is the main responsibility of a general contractor in a subcontracting arrangement?
input: The general contractor shall remain liable for the subcontractor's actions, defaults, delays, and negligence;
output: The general contractor remains liable for the subcontractor's actions, defaults, delays, and negligence.

instruction: What is required before bidding and awarding a contract for an Infrastructure Project, with the exception of a design-and-build scheme?
input: no bidding and award of contract for Infrastructure Projects shall be made unless the detailed engineering investigations, surveys, and designs for the project which shall consider among others, the impact on the environment, have been sufficiently carried out and duly approved... and the acquisition of right-of-way pursuant to Republic Act No. 10752 has been accomplished.
output: The detailed engineering investigations, surveys, and designs must be completed and approved, and the acquisition of right-of-way must be accomplished.

instruction: What is the purpose of a Multi-Year Contractual Authority (MYCA)?
input: NGAs, including SUCs, implementing multi-year programs, activities, and projects shall request the DBM for the issuance of a MYCA prior to the commencement of any procurement activity for multi-year projects:
output: It is an authority given to a Procuring Entity to procure multi-year projects, which must be secured from the DBM before starting any procurement activity for such projects.

instruction: For LGUs, what document is equivalent to a Multi-Year Contractual Authority (MYCA)?
input: For LGUs, they shall secure any equivalent document issued by their respective Sanggunian authorizing them to enter into multi-year contracts.
output: An equivalent document issued by their respective Sanggunian.

instruction: What is the role of the total project cost in the MYCA?
input: The total project cost reflected in the MYCA or its equivalent document shall be the basis or reference for the ABC of the procurement contract.
output: The total project cost in the MYCA or its equivalent document serves as the basis or reference for the Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC).

instruction: What is the purpose of 'Market Scoping'?
input: To ensure proper and strategic procurement planning, a Procuring Entity shall conduct market scoping as a preliminary undertaking in preparing its Project Procurement Management Plan (PPMP), which covers the proper cost estimation, project design and specifications, technical and selection criteria, delivery lead time, storage or warehousing requirements, related industry practices, and other relevant market information.
output: To ensure proper and strategic procurement planning by gathering relevant market information, including cost estimation, project design, and industry practices.

instruction: When are references to a specific brand name allowed in specifications for procurement?
input: Reference to a brand name shall not be allowed except for reasons of technical compatibility, interoperability, servicing, maintenance, or preservation of supplier warranty in order to keep the performance, functionality, and useful life of the equipment...
output: Reference to a brand name is allowed only for reasons of technical compatibility, interoperability, servicing, maintenance, or preserving a supplier's warranty.

instruction: What are 'Early Procurement Activities'?
input: For Goods to be delivered, Infrastructure Projects to be implemented, and Consulting Services to be rendered in the following fiscal year, Procuring Entities are authorized to undertake early procurement activities pending the approval of the funding thereof.
output: Procurement activities undertaken by a Procuring Entity for goods, infrastructure, or consulting services for the next fiscal year, pending the approval of funding.

instruction: When can a contract be awarded after early procurement activities?
input: No award of contract shall be made until the approval and effectivity of the appropriate funding.
output: An award can only be made after the appropriate funding has been approved and is effective.

instruction: What is the purpose of a 'design-and-build scheme' for Infrastructure Projects?
input: Procuring Entities may consider employing the design-and-build scheme as a procurement approach whereby a single contractor is responsible for both design and construction of the government building, which allows quality assurance and effective cost and schedule management.
output: It allows a single contractor to be responsible for both the design and construction of a project, which helps ensure quality and manage costs and schedules effectively.

instruction: Under what circumstances can a Procuring Entity engage a Procurement Agent?
input: the HoPE may authorize the engagement of a government procurement agent, which shall undertake the functions of the BAC, if the Procuring Entity does not have the capability or proficiency to undertake a particular procurement
output: When the Procuring Entity lacks the capability or proficiency to undertake a specific procurement, its Head may authorize the engagement of a government procurement agent to handle the BAC functions.

instruction: What functions of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) cannot be delegated to a Procurement Agent?
input: Provided, That the Procuring Entity cannot delegate the issuance of the notice of award and the award of contract to the procurement agent...
output: The Procuring Entity cannot delegate the issuance of the notice of award and the award of the contract to the procurement agent.

instruction: What is a 'Framework Agreement' in procurement?
input: The framework agreement shall be in the nature of an option contract between the Procuring Entity and the bidder that stipulates the terms and conditions that would be applied in subsequent contracts for the procurement of Goods, Infrastructure Projects, and Consulting Services...
output: It is an option contract between a Procuring Entity and a bidder that sets the terms and conditions for subsequent contracts for goods, infrastructure, or consulting services.

instruction: What are the benefits of 'Pooled Procurement'?
input: Procuring Entities shall consider the advantages of a pooled procurement mechanism, as a procurement strategy, by collaborating or consolidating their requirements in a single, joint, bulk, or group procurement in order to achieve greater value for money and procurement efficiency through demand aggregation, improve quality standards by combining technical capacity, and to increase availability and secure sustainability of supplies.
output: It helps achieve greater value for money and efficiency through demand aggregation, improves quality standards by combining technical capacity, and increases supply availability and sustainability.

instruction: What is the maximum duration for a renewal contract for regular and recurring services?
input: The duration for each renewal contract shall not exceed one (1) year.
output: One year.

instruction: How does the PhilGEPS promote transparency in procurement?
input: The PhilGEPS shall develop features that make pertinent information accessible and transparent at all stages of procurement except procurements involving and affecting national security.
output: By developing features that make relevant procurement information accessible and transparent at all stages, except for those involving national security.

instruction: If a Procuring Entity has an existing electronic procurement system, what must it do to comply with the PhilGEPS mandate?
input: Procuring Entities with established electronic procurement systems shall provide for the seamless interface of systems with the PhilGEPS to ensure efficient sharing of procurement information.
output: It must ensure a seamless interface between its system and the PhilGEPS to allow for efficient sharing of procurement information.

instruction: Who is responsible for developing the electronic and uniform payment system for government procurement?
input: The electronic and uniform payment system to be used by the Procuring Entity and suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, contractors, consultants, and service providers shall be defined in the context of the Integrated Financial Management Information System to be developed by the DBM, Commission on Audit (COA), and Department of Finance (DOF).
output: The Department of Budget and Management (DBM), Commission on Audit (COA), and Department of Finance (DOF) in the context of an Integrated Financial Management Information System.

instruction: What is the GPPB's role regarding data interconnectivity between government agencies?
input: the GPPB is hereby authorized to promulgate rules to ensure the interconnectivity of the following government databases:
output: The GPPB is authorized to create rules to ensure that government databases, such as PhilGEPS, DTI, BIR, SEC, and others, can be interconnected.

instruction: What are the four main purposes of the Procurement Data Analytics annual report published by the GPPB?
input: The GPPB shall publish an annual report on its website for the following purposes: (a) Assist Procuring Entities in the strategic planning of their procurement projects; (b) Assist oversight bodies in formulating and implementing data-driven effective procurement policies and rules... (c) Assist government agencies in identifying and detecting patterns that could help deter or mitigate fraud and non-competitive practices and (d) Facilitate public awareness, active participation, and monitoring of government procurement processes.
output: The report's purposes are to assist Procuring Entities with strategic planning, help oversight bodies create data-driven policies, help agencies detect fraud and non-competitive practices, and facilitate public monitoring of the process.

instruction: What are the requirements for electronic signatures used in procurement?
input: Electronic signatures used for this purpose must comply with the standards set in Republic Act No. 8792 or the 'Electronic Commerce Act'.
output: They must comply with the standards set in the 'Electronic Commerce Act' (Republic Act No. 8792).

instruction: What is required of the PhilGEPS to ensure system integrity?
input: It shall formulate a business continuity plan which shall include features such as, but not limited to, the establishment of backup sites, and regular backup of all information to maintain the integrity of the system and minimize risk of halts or interruptions in operations.
output: The PhilGEPS must create a business continuity plan that includes backup sites and regular information backups to maintain system integrity and minimize interruptions.

instruction: What is the composition of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC)?
input: Each BAC shall have five (5) to seven (7) members, at the discretion of the HoPE. It shall be chaired by at least a third ranking permanent official of the Procuring Entity or, in the absence thereof, a duly authorized representative of the next lower rank than the HoPE.
output: Each BAC must have five to seven members, at the discretion of the HoPE. The chair must be at least a third-ranking permanent official of the Procuring Entity.

instruction: What is the maximum term for a BAC member?
input: Unless sooner removed for a cause, the members of the BAC shall have a fixed term of one (1) year reckoned from the date of designation, renewable at the discretion of the HoPE.
output: One year, which is renewable at the discretion of the HoPE.

instruction: What are the key functions of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC)?
input: The BAC shall have the following functions: (a) Recommend to the HoPE the use of any of the modes of procurement as provided in Article IV of this Act; (b) Publish and/or post the invitation to bid; (c) Conduct pre-procurement and pre-bid conferences...
output: The BAC's functions include recommending procurement modes, publishing invitations to bid, conducting conferences, receiving bids, and evaluating bids.

instruction: What is the purpose of the 'Pre-procurement Conference'?
input: Prior to the issuance of the invitation to bid, the BAC is mandated to hold a pre-procurement conference on each and every procurement, except those covered below or certain level or amount specified in the IRR.
output: The BAC holds this conference before issuing an invitation to bid to ensure all procurement documents and requirements are in order.

instruction: What is the main purpose of a 'Competitive Bidding'?
input: A mode of procurement which is open to participation by any eligible bidder and which consists of the following processes: (a) Publication; (b) Pre-bid conference; (c) Eligibility screening of prospective bidders; (d) Receipt and opening of bids; (e) Evaluation of bids; (f) Post-qualification; and (g) Award of contract.
output: It is a method of procurement that is open to any eligible bidder and involves a specific set of processes from publication to contract award.

instruction: How is 'Competitive Dialogue' defined?
input: A mode of procurement that employs a two-stage dialogue process where the Procuring Entity invites suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, contractors, consultants, and service providers to a dialogue to propose solutions to address its needs and requirements.
output: A two-stage dialogue process where the Procuring Entity invites potential providers to propose solutions to its needs and requirements.

instruction: How does 'Direct Contracting' differ from other procurement modes?
input: A mode of procurement that does not require formal bidding and is instead awarded to a single supplier, manufacturer, distributor, contractor, consultant, and service provider with a valid and existing registration and/or a valid and subsisting procurement project with a government agency...
output: It's a procurement mode without formal bidding, where a contract is awarded to a single supplier that has a valid registration and an existing procurement project with a government agency.

instruction: If a bidder fails to complete a project, what happens to their bid security?
input: All Bids under competitive bidding shall be under a bid security which shall serve as a guarantee that after receipt of the Notice of Award, the winning bidder shall enter into contract with the Procuring Entity within the established time frame furnished the required performance security.
output: The bid security is a guarantee that the winning bidder will enter into a contract, but the document does not specify what happens if they fail to complete the project.

instruction: What is the 'Lowest Calculated Bid' (LCB) in the procurement of goods?
input: For contracts to be awarded to the LCB, the bid that passed the preliminary examination shall be ranked from lowest to highest in terms of their corresponding calculated prices. The bid with the lowest calculated price shall be referred to as the Lowest Calculated Bid (LCB).
output: The bid with the lowest calculated price among all bids that passed the preliminary examination.

instruction: What is the purpose of a 'pre-bid conference'?
input: At least one (1) pre-bid conference shall be conducted for each procurement, unless otherwise provided in the IRR. Subject to the approval of the BAC, a pre-bid conference may also be conducted upon the written request of any prospective bidder.
output: It is a meeting held for each procurement to discuss the bidding documents and answer questions from prospective bidders.

instruction: What must be included in the invitation to bid?
input: The invitation to Bid shall contain, among others: (a) A brief description of the subject matter of the Procurement; (b) The details and mechanics of implementation shall be provided in the IRR.
output: It must include a brief description of the subject matter of the procurement.

instruction: What is the purpose of 'Small Value Procurement'?
input: A mode of procurement whereby a Procuring Entity requests for the submission of at least three (3) price quotations for goods not available in the PS-DBM, Infrastructure Projects, and Consulting Services.
output: It is a procurement mode for goods not available in the PS-DBM, infrastructure projects, and consulting services, where the Procuring Entity requests at least three price quotations.

instruction: How long does a Procuring Entity have to revise the Annual Procurement Plan (APP)?
input: The APP shall be formulated and revised only in accordance with the guidelines set forth in the IRR.
output: The document does not specify a specific time frame, only that it must be done in accordance with the IRR guidelines.

instruction: What is the responsibility of the GPPB regarding the use of Lifecycle Cost Analysis (LCCA)?
input: Provided, That the GPPB shall issue appropriate guidelines on the application of LCCA.
output: The GPPB must issue appropriate guidelines on the application of LCCA.

instruction: How is 'Technical Eligibility' defined?
input: Technical Eligibility refers to having the experience or expertise to undertake the services, manufacturing, distribution, or delivery of the Goods, Infrastructure Projects, and Consulting Services being procured;
output: It refers to the experience or expertise needed to undertake the manufacturing, distribution, or delivery of procured goods, projects, or services.

instruction: How can the government protect trade secrets and promote competition when sharing information between agencies?
input: Provided, further, That at all times, the sharing of information between and among government agencies and instrumentalities shall protect trade secrets and promote competition.
output: The sharing of information must always be done in a manner that protects trade secrets and promotes competition.

instruction: How does the Act promote procurement professionalism?
input: Professionalism in procurement through the development of qualification standards, a competency and certification framework, and a code of ethics that shall be observed by public procurement professionals.
output: By developing qualification standards, a competency and certification framework, and a code of ethics for public procurement professionals.

instruction: If a procurement agent is engaged, what is the role of the Procuring Entity's representative in the Technical Working Group (TWG)?
input: Have at least one (1) representative from the Procuring Entity to be designated as a member of the TWG of the procurement agent to ensure that technical specifications or terms of reference of the Procuring Entity are properly reflected in the bidding documents;
output: The representative is designated as a TWG member of the procurement agent to ensure that the Procuring Entity's technical specifications and terms of reference are correctly included in the bidding documents.

instruction: What is the duration for a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between a Procuring Entity and a procurement agent?
input: The MOA shall be in effect at least six (6) months before the end of the validity of the relevant appropriations as authorized in the relevant appropriations law, or in the corporate operating budgets or appropriations ordinances, in the case of GOCCS, GFIs, and LGUs respectively.
output: The MOA must be in effect at least six months before the end of the validity of the relevant appropriations.

instruction: What must be included in the Annual Procurement Plan (APP) if the procurement tasks are to be outsourced?
input: Procurement methods to be adopted and indicating if the procurement tasks are to be outsourced;
output: The APP must indicate if the procurement tasks are to be outsourced under the procurement methods to be adopted.

instruction: What is the main goal of the Act's procurement professionalization efforts?
input: to ensure the development of a professional procurement service, where government procurement is considered a full-time, professional career;
output: To develop a professional procurement service where government procurement is considered a full-time career.

instruction: What should a Procuring Entity do to ensure the goods it procures have a long useful life?
input: the Procuring Entity shall ensure that goods to be procured are brand new: Provided, That the procurement of second-hand, refurbished or reconditioned goods... may be considered...
output: The Procuring Entity should ensure that the goods procured are brand new, although second-hand or refurbished goods may be considered under specific circumstances.

instruction: How should a Procuring Entity manage its warehousing functions?
input: The Procuring Entity, whenever applicable, shall develop guidelines for its warehousing functions ensuring auditable systems that promote integrity and efficiency, and shall establish a compliance framework mandating training, audits, and transparent reporting.
output: It must develop guidelines for warehousing functions that ensure auditable systems, integrity, and efficiency, and establish a framework for training, audits, and transparent reporting.

instruction: What is the role of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) regarding cloud-based inventory systems?
input: The adoption of cloud-based inventory by NGAS, GOCCS, GFIS, SUCs, and LGUs shall be done in consultation with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) to ensure that the risks and vulnerabilities associated with data storage are adequately addressed through proper and effective security protocols.
output: To be consulted by government agencies when adopting cloud-based inventory to ensure that data storage risks and vulnerabilities are addressed with proper security protocols.

instruction: How can the Commission on Audit (COA) verify the integrity of the PhilGEPS?
input: It shall include features that provide for an audit trail of electronic transactions and allow the COA to verify the security and integrity of the system at any time.
output: The PhilGEPS must have features that provide an audit trail of electronic transactions, allowing the COA to verify the system's security and integrity at any time.

instruction: How are `goods` defined under the Act?
input: Goods refer to all items, supplies, materials, and general support services, except Consulting Services and Infrastructure Projects, which may be needed in the transaction of public businesses or in the pursuit of any government undertaking, project or activity, whether in the nature of equipment, furniture, stationery, materials for construction, or personal property of any kind, including non-personal or contractual services such as the repair and maintenance of equipment and furniture, as well as trucking, hauling, janitorial, security, and related or analogous services...
output: All items, supplies, materials, and general support services (excluding consulting services and infrastructure projects) needed for public business, including equipment, furniture, and non-personal services like janitorial and security services.

instruction: What is `blacklisting`?
input: Blacklisting refers to an administrative penalty imposed by the Head of the Procuring Entity which prohibits a person or an entity including its affiliates from participating in all government procurement activities;
output: An administrative penalty imposed by the Head of the Procuring Entity that prohibits a person or entity and their affiliates from participating in all government procurement activities.

instruction: What is the role of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) in the procurement process?
input: Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) refers to the Committee established in accordance with Article V of this Act:
output: The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) is the committee established to oversee and manage the procurement process.

instruction: What is the purpose of a 'Project Procurement Management Plan' (PPMP)?
input: a Procuring Entity shall conduct market scoping as a preliminary undertaking in preparing its Project Procurement Management Plan (PPMP), which covers the proper cost estimation, project design and specifications, technical and selection criteria, delivery lead time, storage or warehousing requirements, related industry practices, and other relevant market information.
output: The PPMP is a plan that covers key elements of a project, including cost estimation, design, specifications, selection criteria, and delivery timelines.

instruction: What is 'Participatory procurement'?
input: Participatory procurement through public monitoring of the procurement process and the implementation of contracts to guarantee that every step is in accordance with the provisions of this Act and its implementing rules and regulations (IRR), and to ensure prudent and judicious use of government resources;
output: Public monitoring of the procurement process and contract implementation to ensure compliance with the Act and prudent use of government funds.

instruction: How is `Sustainability` addressed in the procurement process?
input: Sustainability in the procurement process which covers the whole lifecycle of a property, ensures value for money and maximum benefits to society and the economy, and engenders minimal impact to the environment;
output: It is a principle that covers the entire lifecycle of a property, ensuring value for money, societal and economic benefits, and minimal environmental impact.

instruction: What is the purpose of the 'Constructors Performance Evaluation System' (CPES)?
input: Contract performance monitoring, such as, but not limited to the Constructors Performance Evaluation System (CPES), shall also be mandatorily applied to the work of subcontractors.
output: It is a system used for contract performance monitoring that must be applied to the work of subcontractors.

instruction: What is the primary role of the `End-User or Implementing Unit`?
input: End-User or Implementing Unit refers to the employee or organic office within the organization of the Procuring Entity that identifies, plans, prepares, designs, and implements the procurement project based on the requirements or needs of the agency in accordance with its mandate;
output: The employee or office within the Procuring Entity that identifies, plans, prepares, designs, and implements a procurement project based on the agency's needs.

instruction: What is `Financial Eligibility`?
input: Financial Eligibility refers to having the financial capacity to manufacture, distribute, or deliver the Goods, Infrastructure Projects, and Consulting Services being procured:
output: The financial capacity required to manufacture, distribute, or deliver the goods, infrastructure projects, and consulting services being procured.

instruction: What is the purpose of a `bid security`?
input: All Bids under competitive bidding shall be under a bid security which shall serve as a guarantee that after receipt of the Notice of Award, the winning bidder shall enter into contract with the Procuring Entity within the established time frame furnished the required performance security.
output: It serves as a guarantee that a winning bidder will enter into a contract with the Procuring Entity after receiving the Notice of Award.

instruction: Who can be designated as a provisional member of the BAC of a procurement agent?
input: Have a representative from the Procuring Entity designated as a provisional member of the BAC of the procurement agent;
output: A representative from the Procuring Entity.

instruction: What are some of the innovative features the PhilGEPS should include?
input: The PhilGEPS shall include the following innovative features and solutions: electronic bulletin board; registry of suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, contractors, consultants, and service providers; electronic catalogue; virtual store; electronic marketplace; electronic reverse auction; electronic small value procurement; electronic payment; and electronic bidding.
output: Electronic bulletin board, registry of suppliers, electronic catalogue, virtual store, electronic marketplace, electronic reverse auction, electronic small value procurement, and electronic payment and bidding.

instruction: What are the rules regarding liabilities of the general contractor and subcontractor for locally-funded projects?
input: The general contractor shall remain liable for the subcontractor's actions, defaults, delays, and negligence... The general contractor and the subcontractor shall share liability in cases where safety standards or other labor standards are violated;
output: The general contractor is solely liable for the subcontractor's actions, defaults, delays, and negligence, but both share liability if safety or labor standards are violated.

instruction: How is the experience of a general contractor recorded for a subcontracted project?
input: The value of the entire completed and accepted project, including the subcontracted portion, shall be recorded as experience of the general contractor...
output: The value of the entire completed and accepted project, including the subcontracted portion, is recorded as the general contractor's experience.

instruction: What is the purpose of a `procurement agent`?
input: the HoPE may authorize the engagement of a government procurement agent, which shall undertake the functions of the BAC, if the Procuring Entity does not have the capability or proficiency to undertake a particular procurement:
output: To undertake the functions of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) on behalf of a Procuring Entity that lacks the capability or proficiency for a particular procurement.

instruction: What is the key benefit of a `Framework Agreement`?
input: Procuring Entities may use a framework agreement as a procurement strategy to expand the pool of prospective bidders, take advantage of economies of scale, minimize the administrative burden of conducting separate procurement activities, and generate time and money savings.
output: It expands the pool of bidders, leverages economies of scale, minimizes administrative burdens, and generates time and money savings.

instruction: How does the Act ensure `proportionality` in procurement?
input: Proportionality by ensuring that the conditions and parameters in the development of requirements, choice of procurement modality, and implementation of contracts shall be reasonably proportional to the needs of the Procuring Entity and the nature of the contract or project to be procured;
output: It ensures that the conditions and parameters of requirements and contracts are reasonably proportional to the Procuring Entity's needs and the nature of the project.

instruction: What must the Procuring Entity ensure about projects during the planning stage?
input: During the planning stage, the Procuring Entity shall ensure that the project has minimal economic, social, and environmental risks or negative impact during its lifecycle, and that the goods and services are procured with due consideration for responsible and sustainable consumption and production practices, and the national policy.
output: The Procuring Entity must ensure that the project has minimal negative economic, social, and environmental impact throughout its lifecycle.

instruction: What is the purpose of `Lifecycle Assessment (LCA)` and `Lifecycle Cost Analysis (LCCA)`?
input: To further support strategic procurement management and ensure smart and prudent use of government resources, Procuring Entities shall apply Lifecycle Assessment (LCA) and Lifecycle Cost Analysis (LCCA) in project planning, eligibility and selection criteria, or contract implementation:
output: To support strategic procurement management and ensure the smart and prudent use of government resources by applying them to project planning, eligibility, and selection criteria.

instruction: If a bidder submits a bid with Unicode escape sequences, what should an auditor recommend?
input: Convert all Unicode escape sequences (e.g., \u2013, \u201c, \u201d) to actual characters (–, “, ”).
output: The auditor should recommend that the Unicode escape sequences be converted to their actual characters for proper readability and processing.

instruction: How can a procurement officer ensure that specifications for goods are legally compliant?
input: Specifications for the procurement of goods...shall be based on any or a combination of the following: relevant characteristics: performance or functionality requirements; or product or service standards specified by appropriate government entities or similar international bodies.
output: The officer should base the specifications on relevant characteristics, performance requirements, or product standards from appropriate government entities or international bodies.

instruction: If a procurement officer needs to purchase a specific brand of equipment for compatibility, what justification is required?
input: Reference to a brand name shall not be allowed except for reasons of technical compatibility, interoperability, servicing, maintenance, or preservation of supplier warranty in order to keep the performance, functionality, and useful life of the equipment, in which case, the Procuring Entity shall indicate the reasons or justifications for availing of the exception.
output: The officer must provide reasons or justifications based on technical compatibility, interoperability, servicing, maintenance, or preservation of a supplier's warranty.

instruction: What should a policymaker consider when developing data-driven procurement policies?
input: Assist oversight bodies in formulating and implementing data-driven effective procurement policies and rules pursuant to the State policy under Section 2 of this Act;
output: A policymaker should consider the data obtained from the PhilGEPS and submitted procurement reports, as well as the State policy under Section 2 of the Act.

instruction: How does the Act define `Infrastructure Projects`?
input: Infrastructure Projects include the construction, improvement, rehabilitation, demolition, repair, restoration, or maintenance of roads and bridges, railways, airports, seaports, communication facilities, civil works components of information technology projects, irrigation, flood control and drainage, water supply, sanitation, sewerage and solid waste management systems.
output: They include the construction, improvement, rehabilitation, demolition, repair, restoration, or maintenance of public works like roads, bridges, railways, airports, seaports, and various government facilities.

instruction: What is the purpose of the `Integrated Financial Management Information System` mentioned in the Act?
input: The electronic and uniform payment system to be used by the Procuring Entity and suppliers... shall be defined in the context of the Integrated Financial Management Information System to be developed by the DBM, Commission on Audit (COA), and Department of Finance (DOF).
output: It is a system to be developed by the DBM, COA, and DOF that will provide the context for the electronic and uniform payment system for procurement.

instruction: What are the rules for subcontracting locally-funded projects?
input: For subcontracting arrangements, the following rules shall apply to locally-funded projects... (a) The HoPE must provide prior approval to subcontracting, (b) Subcontractors must meet eligibility criteria; (c) The bidder or general contractor must disclose subcontractors during the bidding process; (d) The general contractor shall remain liable for the subcontractor's actions, defaults, delays, and negligence; (e) The general contractor and the subcontractor shall share liability in cases where safety standards or other labor standards are violated;
output: Subcontractors must have prior approval from the HoPE, meet eligibility criteria, and be disclosed during bidding. The general contractor remains liable for the subcontractor's actions, but they share liability for safety and labor violations.

instruction: What is `Procurement` in the context of the Act?
input: Procurement refers to the acquisition of Goods and Consulting Services, and the contracting for Infrastructure Projects by the Procuring Entity. Procurement shall also include the lease of goods and real property.
output: The acquisition of goods and consulting services, and the contracting for infrastructure projects by a Procuring Entity. It also includes the lease of goods and real property.

instruction: What information should a Procuring Entity provide for a `Competitive Dialogue`?
input: A mode of procurement that employs a two-stage dialogue process where the Procuring Entity invites suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, contractors, consultants, and service providers to a dialogue to propose solutions to address its needs and requirements. Upon the submissions of these initial technical proposals, prospective bidders eligible bidders shall be engaged in a dialogue to finalize the project requirements.
output: The Procuring Entity should provide the needs and requirements of the project to invite dialogue from bidders, and upon receiving initial technical proposals, they should engage in a dialogue to finalize the requirements.

instruction: What must be included in the MOA for a procurement agent?
input: Covered by a MOA that is executed between the Procuring Entity and the procurement agent providing the details of the project to be procured; the accountabilities and obligations of the two (2) parties; the ABC; services fees, if applicable; and such other details as may be necessary.
output: The MOA must include project details, accountabilities and obligations of both parties, the ABC, and service fees (if applicable).

instruction: What does `Competitive Bidding` mean for a bidder?
input: A mode of procurement which is open to participation by any eligible bidder and which consists of the following processes: (a) Publication; (b) Pre-bid conference; (c) Eligibility screening of prospective bidders; (d) Receipt and opening of bids; (e) Evaluation of bids; (f) Post-qualification; and (g) Award of contract.
output: It is a mode of procurement that gives an eligible bidder the opportunity to participate in a process that includes publication, pre-bid conferences, bid evaluation, and a contract award.

instruction: What is `Electronic Bidding`?
input: The PhilGEPS shall include the following innovative features and solutions: electronic bulletin board...electronic bidding. Electronic signatures used for this purpose must comply with the standards set in Republic Act No. 8792 or the 'Electronic Commerce Act'.
output: It is an innovative feature of the PhilGEPS, where bidding is conducted electronically using electronic signatures that comply with the 'Electronic Commerce Act'.

instruction: What does `Procurement Data Analytics` aim to achieve?
input: The GPPB, through its Technical Support Office (TSO), shall analyze the data obtained from the PhilGEPS and submitted procurement reports to ensure disclosure of information related to the procurement process. The GPPB shall publish an annual report on its website for the following purposes: (a) Assist Procuring Entities in the strategic planning of their procurement projects; (b) Assist oversight bodies in formulating and implementing data-driven effective procurement policies and rules...
output: It aims to analyze procurement data to assist Procuring Entities in strategic planning, help oversight bodies create data-driven policies, and facilitate public monitoring.

instruction: If a Procuring Entity needs to store procured goods, what must they consider?
input: Procuring Entities may adopt a general system of warehousing and cloud-based inventory of procured Goods, as may be necessary depending on the type, nature and volume of procurement undertaken by the Procuring Entity and subject to the availability of funds in accordance with applicable budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules and regulations. The Procuring Entity, whenever applicable, shall develop guidelines for its warehousing functions ensuring auditable systems that promote integrity and efficiency, and shall establish a compliance framework mandating training, audits, and transparent reporting.
output: They must consider adopting a warehousing and inventory system and developing auditable guidelines with a compliance framework that includes training, audits, and transparent reporting.

instruction: How are `Philippine Products and Services` defined?
input: Philippine Products and Services refer to local goods, articles, materials, supplies, services, and intangible products which may be: (1) unmanufactured goods, articles, materials, or supplies wholly obtained or produced in the Philippines; (2) any good... produced, manufactured, or assembled in the Philippines which has a minimum local content as may be determined by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI); (3) services... or (4) intangible products...
output: They are local goods, articles, materials, supplies, services, and intangible products that are wholly obtained or produced in the Philippines, have a minimum local content (as determined by the DTI), or are services and intangible products produced in the Philippines.

instruction: What is the policy for multi-year contracting for NGAs and SUCs?
input: NGAs, including SUCs, implementing multi-year programs, activities, and projects shall request the DBM for the issuance of a MYCA prior to the commencement of any procurement activity for multi-year projects: Provided, That for multi-year projects to be funded from internally generated income of SUCs, the SUCs shall secure prior authority from its Board before starting any procurement activity covering the full contract cost.
output: NGAs and SUCs must request a Multi-Year Contractual Authority (MYCA) from the DBM before starting any procurement activity for multi-year projects. SUCs using internally generated income must secure prior authority from their Board.

instruction: What is `Accountability` in government procurement?
input: Accountability where all public officials and personnel directly or indirectly involved in the procurement process and in the implementation of contracts are investigated and held accountable for their actions when necessary;
output: It is a principle where all public officials and personnel involved in procurement and contract implementation are investigated and held accountable for their actions when necessary.

instruction: What should a procurement officer do to improve the efficiency of the procurement process?
input: Efficiency by implementing an organized, uniform, and straightforward government procurement process through the use of emerging technologies and innovative solutions;
output: The officer should implement an organized, uniform, and straightforward process by using emerging technologies and innovative solutions.

instruction: What is the purpose of the `registry of suppliers` in PhilGEPS?
input: The PhilGEPS shall include the following innovative features and solutions: ...registry of suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, contractors, consultants, and service providers...
output: It is a feature of the PhilGEPS that serves as a registry for suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, contractors, consultants, and service providers.

instruction: What is the process for `Electronic Small Value Procurement`?
input: The PhilGEPS shall include the following innovative features and solutions: ...electronic small value procurement...
output: The document mentions this as an innovative feature of the PhilGEPS, but does not provide a detailed process. It is a mode for procuring small value items electronically.

instruction: What should a bidder be mindful of when submitting a bid?
input: Bid refers to a signed offer or proposal submitted by a supplier, manufacturer, distributor, contractor, consultant, and service provider in response to the bidding documents; Bidder refers to a supplier, manufacturer, distributor, contractor, consultant, and service provider who submits a bid in response to the requirements of the bidding documents;
output: A bidder must be mindful to submit a signed offer or proposal in response to the requirements of the bidding documents.

instruction: What are some of the activities included in `Market Scoping`?
input: Market scoping may include the following activities: consultations with suppliers, contractors or consultants, professional associations or groups; participation in summits, fora or conferences; evaluation of market reviews; review of product or service brochures and marketing materials, industry journals and publications, other related materials and publications; price sourcing for quotations or cost estimates from suppliers, contractors or consultants; use of relevant data from the PhilGEPS or agency websites to serve as a guide or reference; or any analogous activity for the purpose of gathering relevant market information.
output: Market scoping activities may include consultations, participation in forums, evaluating market reviews, reviewing marketing materials, price sourcing, and using data from PhilGEPS or agency websites.

instruction: What must be done for a project that requires the acquisition of a right-of-way before a contract can be awarded?
input: In case of projects requiring acquisition of right-of-way, no award of contract shall likewise be made until an authority or permit to enter is issued by the property owner; or a notarized deed of sale or deed of donation is executed in favor of the government; or a writ of possession is issued by a court of competent jurisdiction, as the case may be.
output: A contract cannot be awarded until a permit to enter is issued, a notarized deed of sale or donation is executed, or a writ of possession is issued by a court.

instruction: How is the `Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC)` determined for a multi-year project?
input: The total project cost reflected in the MYCA or its equivalent document shall be the basis or reference for the ABC of the procurement contract.
output: The total project cost indicated in the Multi-Year Contractual Authority (MYCA) or its equivalent document serves as the basis for the ABC.

instruction: What does `Transparency` in the procurement process entail?
input: Transparency in the procurement process by providing access to all related information in accordance with open contracting practice that enables the disclosure of data and facilitates information sharing related to all stages of procurement:
output: It involves providing access to all related information through open contracting practices that facilitate the disclosure of data and information sharing at all stages of procurement.

instruction: What is the role of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) in a `two-failed-biddings` scenario?
input: Negotiated Procurement shall be allowed only in the following instances: (a) Two Failed Biddings. In case of two (2) failed biddings as provided in Section 64 hereof.
output: The document states that negotiated procurement is allowed after two failed biddings, but it does not specify the role of the BAC in this scenario.

instruction: Who are `Consulting Services` provided by?
input: Consulting Services refer to services for Infrastructure Projects and other types of projects or activities of the government requiring adequate external technical and professional expertise that are beyond the capability and/or capacity of the government to undertake such as, but not limited to: (1) advisory and review services; (2) pre-investment or feasibility studies; (3) design; (4) construction supervision: (5) management and related services; and (6) other technical services or special studies;
output: They are provided by external technical and professional experts for projects that are beyond the government's capability or capacity.

instruction: How is `Bid Evaluation` conducted for Goods and Infrastructure Projects?
input: For contracts to be awarded to the LCB, the bid that passed the preliminary examination shall be ranked from lowest to highest in terms of their corresponding calculated prices. The bid with the lowest calculated price shall be referred to as the Lowest Calculated Bid (LCB).
output: Bids that pass the preliminary examination are ranked from lowest to highest based on their calculated prices, and the bid with the lowest calculated price is selected.

instruction: How does the Act ensure `professionalism`?
input: Professionalism in procurement through the development of qualification standards, a competency and certification framework, and a code of ethics that shall be observed by public procurement professionals.
output: It ensures professionalism by developing qualification standards, a competency and certification framework, and a code of ethics for public procurement professionals.

instruction: What are the rules for `blacklisting`?
input: Blacklisting refers to an administrative penalty imposed by the Head of the Procuring Entity which prohibits a person or an entity including its affiliates from participating in all government procurement activities;
output: Blacklisting is an administrative penalty imposed by the Head of the Procuring Entity that prohibits a person or entity and their affiliates from participating in all government procurement activities.

instruction: What is the role of the `GPPB` in the `standardization` of procurement?
input: For this purpose, the GPPB shall pursue the development of generic procurement manuals and standard bidding forms, the use of which, once issued shall be mandatory upon all Procuring Entities.
output: The GPPB is responsible for developing generic procurement manuals and standard bidding forms, which become mandatory for all Procuring Entities once issued.

instruction: What is the primary objective of `procurement by electronic means`?
input: To promote greater transparency, accountability, operational efficiency, and value for money, the PhilGEPS shall be the single electronic portal that shall serve as the primary source of information and channel in the conduct of all procurement activities of the government.
output: To promote greater transparency, accountability, operational efficiency, and value for money by using the PhilGEPS as the single electronic portal for all government procurement activities.

instruction: What kind of documents does the PhilGEPS ensure `security, integrity, and confidentiality` for?
input: The PhilGEPS shall ensure the security, integrity, and confidentiality of documents submitted, stored, and managed through the system.
output: It ensures the security, integrity, and confidentiality of documents that are submitted, stored, and managed through the system.

instruction: What must the GPPB do to facilitate `systems interconnectivity` between government agencies?
input: the GPPB is hereby authorized to promulgate rules to ensure the interconnectivity of the following government databases:
output: The GPPB is authorized to promulgate rules to ensure the interconnectivity of various government databases like PhilGEPS, DTI, BIR, SEC, and others.

instruction: What is `Competitive Dialogue` designed to achieve?
input: A mode of procurement that employs a two-stage dialogue process where the Procuring Entity invites suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, contractors, consultants, and service providers to a dialogue to propose solutions to address its needs and requirements. Upon the submissions of these initial technical proposals, prospective bidders eligible bidders shall be engaged in a dialogue to finalize the project requirements.
output: It is a process designed to allow a Procuring Entity to engage in a two-stage dialogue with potential providers to develop and finalize project requirements and propose solutions.

instruction: How is a `framework agreement` used as a procurement strategy?
input: Procuring Entities may use a framework agreement as a procurement strategy to expand the pool of prospective bidders, take advantage of economies of scale, minimize the administrative burden of conducting separate procurement activities, and generate time and money savings.
output: It is a procurement strategy used to expand the pool of bidders, gain economies of scale, reduce administrative burdens, and save time and money.

instruction: What must a Procuring Entity do to ensure sound procurement decisions during planning?
input: All procurement shall be undertaken with proper and sufficient planning and preparation to ensure sound procurement decisions. This includes the conduct of relevant market scoping, supply positioning, analysis of available procurement modalities, risk management, and disposal procedures as may be applicable.
output: The Procuring Entity must undertake proper and sufficient planning, including market scoping, supply positioning, analysis of modalities, risk management, and disposal procedures.

instruction: What is the policy regarding architectural design for Infrastructure Projects?
input: Procuring Entities may consider architectural design that is well-curated and aesthetic to ensure that the Infrastructure Project not only meets functional requirements but also contributes to its overall appeal and architectural integrity.
output: Procuring Entities may consider well-curated and aesthetic architectural design to ensure the project meets functional requirements while also contributing to its overall appeal and integrity.

instruction: What is the role of the PS-DBM in the PhilGEPS?
input: Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) refers to the single electronic procurement portal managed by the Procurement Service (PS-DBM)...
output: The PS-DBM manages the PhilGEPS, which serves as the single electronic procurement portal for the government.

instruction: What are the requirements for a `Procurement Agent`?
input: The engagement of a procurement agent shall be further subject to the following conditions: (a) Made on a per procurement project basis; (b) Limited to procurement undertaken through competitive bidding: Provided, That in instances where the Procuring Entity lacks sufficient qualified personnel to constitute its own BAC, the Procuring Entity may engage a procurement agent to undertake other modes of procurement; (c) The procurement agent should be another government agency expert in the field which is the subject of procurement.
output: A procurement agent must be another government agency that is an expert in the field of the procurement, engaged on a per-project basis, and limited to competitive bidding unless the Procuring Entity lacks qualified personnel for its own BAC.

instruction: What happens if a Procuring Entity has an existing MOA with a procurement agent that has not been implemented upon the effectivity of this Act?
input: Procuring Entities with existing MOAs with a procurement agent which have not yet been implemented upon the effectivity of this Act are encouraged to revisit the same and amend as may be necessary to conform with this provision.
output: The Procuring Entities are encouraged to revisit and amend the MOAs as necessary to conform with the provisions of the new Act.

instruction: What is the role of `market reviews` in procurement?
input: Market scoping may include the following activities: ...evaluation of market reviews; review of product or service brochures and marketing materials, industry journals and publications, other related materials and publications;
output: Market reviews are used as part of market scoping to gather relevant market information for strategic procurement planning.

instruction: What is the primary purpose of a Bid Securing Declaration?
input: I/We understand that, according to your conditions, bids must be supported by a Bid Security, which may be in the form of a Bid Securing Declaration.
output: It is a form of bid security that bidders can submit to support their bids.

instruction: What is the consequence for a bidder if their Bid Securing Declaration is enforced due to prohibited acts?
input: I/we will be automatically disqualified from bidding for any procurement contract with any procuring entity for a period of two (2) years upon receipt of your Blacklisting Order.
output: The bidder will be automatically disqualified from bidding for any procurement contract with any procuring entity for a period of two years upon receipt of a Blacklisting Order.

instruction: When a bidder's Bid Securing Declaration is enforced, what financial penalty must they pay?
input: I/we will pay the applicable fine provided under Section 6 of the Guidelines on the Use of Bid Securing Declaration, within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the written demand by the procuring entity for the commission of acts resulting to the enforcement of the bid securing declaration under Sections 23.1(b), 34.2, 40.1 and 69.1, except 69.1(f),of the IRR of RA No. 9184.
output: The bidder must pay the applicable fine provided under Section 6 of the Guidelines on the Use of Bid Securing Declaration within 15 days of receiving the written demand from the procuring entity.

instruction: Under what specific conditions does a Bid Securing Declaration cease to be valid?
input: I/We understand that this Bid Securing Declaration shall cease to be valid on the following circumstances: a. Upon expiration of the bid validity period, or any extension thereof pursuant to your request; b. I am/we are declared ineligible or post-disqualified upon receipt of your notice to such effect, and (i) I/we failed to timely file a request for reconsideration or (ii) I/we filed a waiver to avail of said right; and c. I am/we are declared the bidder with the Lowest Calculated Responsive Bid, and I/we have furnished the performance security and signed the Contract.
output: It ceases to be valid upon the expiration of the bid validity period, when the bidder is declared ineligible or post-disqualified and fails to file a timely request for reconsideration or waives that right, or when the bidder is declared the Lowest Calculated Responsive Bid, furnishes the performance security, and signs the contract.

instruction: If a bidder who submitted a Bid Securing Declaration is declared ineligible, when does the declaration become invalid?
input: I am/we are declared ineligible or post-disqualified upon receipt of your notice to such effect, and (i) I/we failed to timely file a request for reconsideration or (ii) I/we filed a waiver to avail of said right;
output: The declaration becomes invalid upon receipt of the notice of ineligibility, unless the bidder successfully files a timely request for reconsideration.

instruction: If a bidder is declared the Lowest Calculated Responsive Bidder, what two actions must they take for their Bid Securing Declaration to become invalid?
input: I am/we are declared the bidder with the Lowest Calculated Responsive Bid, and I/we have furnished the performance security and signed the Contract.
output: They must furnish the required performance security and sign the contract.

instruction: For a procurement auditor, what key information should be checked on a submitted Bid Securing Declaration?
input:
I/We, the undersigned, declare that:
1. I/We understand that, according to your conditions, bids must be supported by a Bid Security, which may be in the form of a Bid Securing Declaration.
2. I/We accept that: (a) I/we will be automatically disqualified from bidding for any procurement contract with any procuring entity for a period of two (2) years upon receipt of your Blacklisting Order; and, (b) I/we will pay the applicable fine provided under Section 6 of the Guidelines on the Use of Bid Securing Declaration, within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the written demand by the procuring entity for the commission of acts resulting to the enforcement of the bid securing declaration under Sections 23.1(b), 34.2, 40.1 and 69.1, except 69.1(f),of the IRR of RA No. 9184; without prejudice to other legal action the government may undertake.
